title: He Goes With You
verse: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
meaning: Moses said this to Israel just before he died and they crossed into a hard new land. The courage he asked for was not swagger. It rested on one fact: the LORD himself would go with them. Moses would not cross with them. Joshua would lead. But the One who mattered most would never leave them.
heart: You may be facing a new school, a new job, or a fear you never say out loud. Strength starts with who walks beside you, not with how tough you look. Fear can be real and still not be the boss. You can feel it and keep walking. Take one step today, knowing you are not alone.
holdOn: I am not alone in this. God goes with me.
prayer: Lord, you went with Israel into a hard land. Go with me into today. When I feel small or scared, remind me that you will not fail me or leave me. Give me courage that comes from you. When I want to hide or quit, keep me steady, and let the people around me see your strength in me. Amen.
teaser: Courage is not a feeling you wait for. It starts with who walks next to you.

title: A Clean Road
verse: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
meaning: This psalm asks a question every young man faces. How do you stay clean when the world pulls hard the other way? The answer is not willpower alone. It is living by God's word, one choice at a time. The psalm writer loved God's word because it kept him close to God. Purity grows from that closeness, not from fear.
heart: Your phone, your friends and your own thoughts all pull at you. You will not win by trying harder at midnight. Win in the morning. The battle is easier when you plan before the moment comes. Decide while your head is clear. Read today's word, and decide now what you will not look at tonight.
holdOn: I keep my way clean by living by God's word, one choice at a time.
prayer: God, I want a clean heart and a clear head. You know what pulls at me when no one is watching. Fill my mind with your word before the day fills it with other things. Guard my eyes tonight. When I fall, do not let me hide from you. Wash me clean and help me get back up. Amen.
teaser: How does a young man stay clean? The psalm gives a surprisingly simple answer.

title: There Is a Way Out
verse: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
meaning: Paul wrote this to young believers in Corinth, a city full of temptation. He told them their struggle was common, not strange. And he made a promise: God is faithful and will always provide a way out. Corinth was known for loose living. Paul did not say temptation would stop. He said God would stay faithful in it.
heart: Temptation lies to you. It says you are the only one and that you have no choice. Both are false. The way out is usually small and fast. It shows up early, before the moment gets strong. Next time it hits, look for the exit God promised: leave the room, call a friend, or put the phone down.
holdOn: I am not the only one, and there is always a way out.
prayer: Faithful God, you know every temptation I face. Thank you that I am not alone in it. When it comes today, open my eyes to the way out, and give me the strength to take it fast. Keep me honest with my friends, so I do not fight this alone. Amen.
teaser: Temptation tells you two lies. Here is the truth that beats both of them.

title: God Looks Deeper
verse: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
meaning: Samuel came to anoint Israel's next king. He was sure the tall, strong brother was the one. God said no. People judge by height and looks, but God looks at the heart. God chose David, the youngest, out in the fields. Even Samuel, a prophet, judged by looks at first. God had to correct him. What God sees is the truer picture.
heart: Muscles, money, likes and looks are what people notice. God sees what is underneath, and he is not put off by it. You can stop performing for people who only see the outside. God already knows the real you. Today, spend less time on how you look and more on what kind of man you are becoming.
holdOn: God sees my heart, and that is what matters most.
prayer: Lord, you see past my face and into my heart. Thank you that your love does not depend on how I look or what I own. Shape my heart into one that is good, brave and true. When I compare myself to other guys, turn my eyes back to what matters to you. Amen.
teaser: God passed over the tallest brother. Here is what he was looking for instead.

title: Iron on Iron
verse: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
meaning: Iron blades get sharp by striking other iron. The proverb says friends work the same way. A good friend does not just agree with you. He pushes you, tells you the truth, and makes you better. Sharpening throws sparks and takes some friction. A real friend will sometimes say what you do not want to hear.
heart: Who sharpens you? Some friends only make you dull. Think of one man who makes you better, and reach out to him today. Do not wait for him to call first. Send the text, set up the game, or grab food. Ask him how he is really doing, and be honest when he asks you back.
holdOn: I need friends who sharpen me, and I can sharpen them.
prayer: God, thank you for the friends who make me better. Show me who to draw closer to and who to step back from. Make me a friend who speaks the truth and keeps showing up. Give me the humility to listen when a brother corrects me, and the courage to do the same. Amen.
teaser: Some friends make you dull. Some make you sharp. Here is how to tell.

title: Young Is Not Too Young
verse: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
meaning: Paul wrote to Timothy, a young leader that older people doubted. Paul did not tell him to wait until he was older. He told him to show his worth by how he lived: his words, love, faith and purity. Paul knew some would dismiss Timothy. He did not argue about age. He pointed to the life that would speak for itself.
heart: You do not need a title to lead. People notice how you talk, how you treat others and what you do when it is hard. Younger guys watch you too, even if you never notice. Your choices teach them what faith looks like. Pick one of Paul's five today, maybe your words, and set the example there.
holdOn: I do not have to wait to be an example. I can start today.
prayer: Lord, I am young, but you can still use me. Guard my words today. Help me love people well, trust you more and keep my life clean. Let others see you in how I live. When someone looks down on me, keep me humble and steady. Let my life answer them better than my words. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave a young man five places to lead before anyone gave him a title.

title: Strength That Lasts
verse: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
meaning: Isaiah wrote to tired people far from home who felt God had forgotten them. He reminded them that even the young grow tired. But those who wait on the LORD get new strength, strength that does not run out. Eagles do not flap hard the whole way up. They ride the wind and rise. It is a picture of trusting God's strength.
heart: Some days you are running on empty, and coffee or pride will not fix it. Waiting on God is not sitting around. It is leaning on him first. Sleep, food and a real break matter too. God made your body, and he cares how you treat it. Before you push through today, stop and ask him for strength.
holdOn: When I am tired, God gives new strength to those who wait on him.
prayer: God, I am more tired than I let people see. I cannot run on my own strength forever. Renew me today. Help me wait on you, lean on you and keep going with strength from you. When I feel like giving up, lift me like the eagle on the wind. Teach me to rest in you. Amen.
teaser: Even strong young men grow tired. Isaiah points to strength that does not run out.

title: Made With Care
verse: For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother’s womb. I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
meaning: David wrote this song in awe. Before he was born, God was already forming him with care. David does not boast in himself. He praises God, who made him on purpose and knows him completely. The word knit pictures careful, patient work. Nothing about you was rushed or random to God.
heart: Some days you do not like what you see in the mirror. God does not make mistakes, and he did not make one when he made you. Your worth was set before you lifted a weight or earned a dollar. You do not have to prove it. Today, thank him for one thing about how you are made.
holdOn: God made me on purpose, and he knows me completely.
prayer: Creator God, you made me with care before I took a breath. Forgive me for the times I hate how I am made. Teach me to see myself the way you see me. When I feel like I am not enough, remind me that your works are wonderful, and I am one of them. Amen.
teaser: Before your first breath, someone was already working on you with care.

title: Light for the Next Step
verse: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
meaning: In David's time, a lamp at night lit only a few steps ahead. The psalm says God's word works like that. It may not show your whole future, but it shows you the next right step. People walked dark roads with small clay lamps. They kept walking because the light moved with them.
heart: You may want to see your whole life mapped out: the job, the city, the money. God often gives just enough light for today. Waiting for the whole plan can freeze you in place. Faithful steps today lead to tomorrow's light. Read his word and ask him one question: what is the next right step?
holdOn: I do not need the whole map. I need the next step.
prayer: Lord, I want to see everything, but you give light one step at a time. Help me trust you with the parts I cannot see. Show me the next right step, and give me the guts to take it. Give me a love for your word, so I come back to it every morning. Amen.
teaser: God rarely shows the whole map. He does give you light for the next step.

title: Come Tired
verse: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
meaning: Jesus spoke to people worn out by hard work and by strict religious rules that kept piling up. He did not hand them another list. He invited them to come to him, just as they were, and find rest. Rest from Jesus is more than a nap. It is peace with God, and a lighter way to live.
heart: Men are told to carry it all and never say they are tired. Jesus says something different: come to me. You do not need to clean up first. Pride says push through alone. Faith says bring the weight to someone strong enough to carry it. Tell him today, in plain words, what is weighing you down.
holdOn: I can come to Jesus tired and find real rest.
prayer: Jesus, I am carrying more than I admit. Thank you for asking me to come as I am. Take the weight I cannot carry. Give me rest in my mind and in my body. Quiet the noise in my head tonight, and help me trust you with what I cannot fix. Amen.
teaser: Jesus did not hand tired people another list. He gave them an invitation.

title: Made in His Image
verse: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
meaning: At the start of the Bible, God makes people in his own image, male and female. This was a huge claim. Kings said they alone carried a god's image. Genesis says every person does. So no one is worth less because of money, race or strength. Every person reflects something of God.
heart: That truth changes how you treat yourself and everyone else, even people you do not like. It also means you cannot write yourself off. You carry that image too, on your worst day. Today, notice someone others ignore. Treat that person as someone made in God's image, because that is what they are.
holdOn: I carry God's image, and so does every person I meet.
prayer: God, thank you for making me in your image. Help me see that image in every person today, even the ones who annoy me. Teach me to treat people with the honor you gave them. Forgive me for the times I mocked or ignored someone. Make me quick to respect people. Amen.
teaser: Ancient kings claimed a god's image for themselves alone. Genesis disagreed.

title: Even God Rested
verse: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
meaning: After six days of making the world, God rested on the seventh day. He was not tired. He set a pattern: work is good, and so is stopping. Rest is part of how God made life to work. Later God gave his people a weekly day of rest. It reminded them they were free, not slaves.
heart: There is always one more game, one more task, one more scroll. Rest can feel lazy or weak. It is not. Your worth is not measured by how busy you are. Stopping is a way of trusting God. Plan a real break this week, with your phone off, and let it be a gift from God.
holdOn: Rest is not weakness. God built it into how life works.
prayer: Lord, I find it hard to stop. Teach me to stop without feeling guilty. Help me trust that the world keeps turning when I put things down. Give me real rest this week. Slow me down, and let me enjoy the good things and good people you have given me. Amen.
teaser: God did not rest because he was tired. So why did he stop?

title: Sin at the Door
verse: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”
meaning: Cain was angry that God accepted his brother's offering and not his. God warned him: sin was crouching at the door like an animal ready to pounce. Cain could still choose. He could rule over it. Sadly, Cain ignored the warning and killed his brother. God had given him a chance to turn back first.
heart: Anger and jealousy rarely knock politely. They crouch and wait. When you feel that heat rising today, stop before you act. Anger is not always wrong. What you do with it decides whether it rules you. Name what you feel, step away, and pray before you speak or type a word.
holdOn: Sin crouches at the door, but I can choose not to open it.
prayer: God, you see the anger and jealousy in me. Warn me when sin is crouching close. Give me the strength to rule over it and not let it rule me. When my temper flares, cool me down before I act. Help me be glad for others when they win. Amen.
teaser: God warned an angry young man about something crouching at his door.

title: Leave and Go
verse: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
meaning: God called Abram to leave his country, his people and his father's house. He was not told where he was going. Abram trusted God enough to start walking. His story of faith begins with a step. Abram was seventy-five years old. He left a settled life on the strength of God's promise alone.
heart: Some steps of faith are scary because you cannot see the end. Leaving a bad crowd, a habit or a comfort zone takes trust. You will not get every answer first. Abram only knew who was leading him. Is there one thing God is asking you to leave behind? Start walking away from it.
holdOn: Faith often starts with leaving before I can see where I am going.
prayer: Lord, you called Abram into the unknown, and he went. Show me what I need to leave behind. Give me faith to walk with you even when I cannot see the road ahead. Help me trust your promises more than my comfort, and keep me close to you on every step. Amen.
teaser: God told Abram to go, but not where. He went anyway.

title: God Was Here All Along
verse: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
meaning: Jacob was running from his brother after cheating him. He slept on a rock in the open, alone. That night God met him in a dream. Jacob woke up stunned: God had been in that place, and he had not known. God also promised to bring Jacob home again. A liar on the run was still not out of reach.
heart: You may feel far from God because of what you did or where you are. God is not limited to church buildings. He meets people on the run. A dorm room, a car or a hard bed can become a holy place when God shows up. Wherever you are today, say it out loud: God is here.
holdOn: Even when I am running, God is already here.
prayer: God, you met Jacob when he was running and alone. Meet me where I am today, even if I made the mess. Open my eyes to see that you are here. Turn my running into returning. Let me find you in places I never expected, and remember that you keep your promises. Amen.
teaser: A young man on the run slept on a rock and woke up shocked.

title: Wrestle and Hold On
verse: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob said, “I won’t let you go unless you bless me.”
meaning: The night before facing his angry brother, Jacob wrestled with a mysterious man until dawn. Jacob was hurt, but he refused to let go without a blessing. He walked away limping, with a new name. God named him Israel, meaning he struggles with God. The limp reminded Jacob that God had met him there.
heart: Faith is not always calm. Sometimes it looks like wrestling with God through the night. You can bring God your fears and questions and refuse to let go. Honest prayer is better than polite silence. God can handle your anger, your doubt and your tears. Hold on to him today, even if you walk away limping.
holdOn: I can wrestle with God and still refuse to let go of him.
prayer: God, I have fears and questions I do not say out loud. Thank you that I can bring them all to you. I will not let go of you. Bless me, and change me. When I am worn out from the fight, hold on to me too. Give me a new start like you gave Jacob. Amen.
teaser: Jacob fought all night and walked away limping. He also walked away blessed.

title: When No One Is Watching
verse: No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”
meaning: Joseph was a young slave in Egypt, trusted by his master. His master's wife kept pushing him toward sex. Joseph refused. He saw it as a sin against God and a betrayal of the man who trusted him. She kept asking day after day. One day Joseph ran, leaving his coat in her hand. He chose honor over comfort.
heart: Temptation often comes when no one would find out. Joseph's answer was simple: how could I do this against God? Decide your lines before the moment comes. Running is not weakness. Sometimes leaving fast is the bravest thing a man can do. Today, choose one place where you will say no in advance.
holdOn: My choices in private matter to God and to the people who trust me.
prayer: God, give me the courage Joseph had. When temptation comes in secret, remind me that you see and that people trust me. Help me say no early and walk away fast. Keep my heart loyal to you first. Make me a man people can trust, whether or not anyone is watching. Amen.
teaser: Joseph was alone, tempted and sure no one would find out. Here is what he said.

title: Meant for Good
verse: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive, as is happening today.
meaning: Joseph's brothers sold him into slavery. Years later, he was a leader in Egypt and saved them from famine. When they feared his revenge, Joseph said they meant it for evil, but God meant it for good. Joseph had every reason for revenge, and the power to take it. He chose mercy, because he trusted God's bigger plan.
heart: This does not mean the hurt done to you was good. It was evil, and it is fine to say so. But God can still bring good out of it. Healing can take time. You can be honest about the pain and still hope. Bring him one old wound today and ask him to work in it.
holdOn: What others meant for harm, God can still use for good.
prayer: God, you know the wounds other people gave me. I will not pretend they did not hurt. But I trust you to bring good from them. Heal me, and keep me from becoming bitter. Help me forgive the way Joseph did, and show me where you are already working. Amen.
teaser: Joseph's brothers sold him. Years later, he told them something they never expected.

title: God Sees the Pain
verse: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.
meaning: Israel had been slaves in Egypt for many years, crying out under cruel masters. God spoke to Moses from a burning bush. He said he had seen their misery, heard their cry and knew their pain. Then God said he had come down to rescue them. Seeing their pain led him to act.
heart: Some of your pain no one else sees. God does. He is not distant or bored by your struggle. He knows it in detail. You do not have to act fine. Hiding pain does not make it smaller. It only makes you carry it alone. Tell him today about the thing you hide from everyone else.
holdOn: God sees my pain, hears my cry and knows what I carry.
prayer: God who saw Israel in Egypt, you see me too. Thank you that my pain is not hidden from you. Hear my cry today, and give me hope that you are already moving. Send me people who will listen, and help me tell the truth about how I am doing. Amen.
teaser: A whole nation was crying out in slavery. God answered from a burning bush.

title: Help With Your Words
verse: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”
meaning: God sent Moses to free Israel, but Moses kept making excuses. He said he was a poor speaker. God did not deny it. He promised to be with Moses' mouth and teach him what to say. Even when Moses begged him to send someone else, God did not drop him. He sent Aaron to help instead.
heart: Maybe you avoid speaking up because you think you are bad with words. God does not wait for perfect speakers. He works through shaky voices and plain words. What matters is that you say what is true. If there is a hard talk you keep avoiding, ask God for the words and have it this week.
holdOn: God does not need me to be perfect. He promises to help me speak.
prayer: Lord, I make excuses like Moses did. You know where I feel weak. Be with my mouth today. Give me the right words and the courage to say them. Help me speak with kindness and truth, and not hide behind silence when someone needs to hear from me. Amen.
teaser: Moses gave God every excuse in the book. God's reply was short.

title: Cloud by Day, Fire by Night
verse: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:
meaning: After Israel left Egypt, God led them through the desert. By day he went ahead in a pillar of cloud. By night he gave light in a pillar of fire. They never had to find the way alone. For forty years, the cloud and fire never left them. Israel's guide was always in sight.
heart: You are not expected to have life figured out. God leads one day at a time, in the light and in the dark. In your hardest night this week, remember he goes ahead of you. He also guards your back, like the cloud that stood between Israel and Pharaoh's army. Ask him to lead.
holdOn: God goes ahead of me in the day and in the night.
prayer: God who led Israel through the desert, lead me today. When I do not know the way, go ahead of me. When my night is dark, be my light. Help me follow when you move, and wait when you stay. Keep my eyes on you, not on my fears. Amen.
teaser: Israel crossed a desert with no map. They had something better.

title: The LORD Will Fight for You
verse: The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
meaning: Israel was trapped between the sea and Pharaoh's army. The people panicked. Moses told them to stand firm and be still. The battle in front of them was too big for them. The LORD would fight for them. God opened a path through the sea, and Israel walked across on dry ground. The army that chased them never caught them.
heart: Some fights are too big for you: a family mess, debt, a diagnosis, a fear. You do not have to fake strength. Do what is yours to do, then be still. Being still is not giving up. It is trusting that God is still working when you cannot see it. Let God fight the part you cannot.
holdOn: Some battles are too big for me. God fights for me.
prayer: Lord, I am facing something too big for me. I am tired of fighting it alone. Fight for me. Teach me to be still and trust you while you work. Calm my panic, and help me do the next thing in front of me while I wait for you. Amen.
teaser: Trapped between an army and the sea, Israel got a strange command: be still.

title: Bread for Today
verse: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not.
meaning: In the desert, God sent bread from heaven called manna. There was enough for each day, but it could not be stored. God was teaching Israel to trust him daily, not to hoard for tomorrow. On the sixth day God gave a double portion, so they could rest on the seventh.
heart: Worry tries to solve next month today. God gives strength and provision for today. Pray for today's needs, do today's work, and leave tomorrow with God. Planning ahead is wise. Worry is different. It borrows trouble God has not asked you to carry yet. Notice one way he provided for you today.
holdOn: God gives me what I need for today. Tomorrow is his too.
prayer: God, you fed your people every morning in the desert. Teach me to trust you one day at a time. Give me what I need today, and help me let go of tomorrow's worry. When money is tight or the future feels unsure, remind me that you know what I need. Amen.
teaser: God fed a nation in the desert with bread that went bad overnight. Why?

title: You Cannot Carry It Alone
verse: You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.
meaning: Moses tried to judge every problem for the whole nation by himself, from morning to night. His father-in-law Jethro saw it and warned him. The load was too heavy. Moses would wear out unless he shared it. Jethro told him to choose honest, capable men to share the work. Moses listened, and the people were served better.
heart: Many men think asking for help is weak. Moses was a great leader, and he still needed help. Where are you carrying too much alone? Help can be a friend, a mentor, a pastor or a counselor. Letting people in is part of being strong. Ask one person for help this week, and mean it.
holdOn: Asking for help is not weakness. I was not made to carry it alone.
prayer: God, I try to carry too much on my own. Give me the humility to ask for help. Send good people around me, and help me let them in. Show me who to trust. Teach me to share the load, and to not feel ashamed when I need others. Amen.
teaser: Moses was wearing himself out. The fix came from his father-in-law.

title: Honor Your Parents
verse: “Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
meaning: This command is part of the Ten Commandments. In Israel, honoring parents meant respect and care, even when they grew old. It did not mean pretending they were perfect. It meant treating them with weight and dignity. Paul later called it the first command with a promise. He also told fathers not to provoke their children.
heart: Family can be complicated. Some fathers are absent, some are harsh, some are great. Honor does not mean you accept abuse. It can mean a respectful word or a call. If your father hurt you, God does not ask you to forget it. He can be the Father you needed. If it is safe, reach out to a parent this week.
holdOn: I can honor my parents without pretending everything is perfect.
prayer: Lord, you know my family, the good and the hard. Help me honor my parents in a way that pleases you. Heal what is broken, and give me wisdom where it is not safe. Thank you for every good thing my family gave me. Make me a man who brings peace home. Amen.
teaser: Honoring your parents does not mean pretending they are perfect. So what does it mean?

title: Help Your Enemy
verse: If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.
meaning: God's law said that if your enemy's donkey fell under its load, you must help lift it. Hating the man did not cancel your duty. Doing good to an enemy was part of living as God's people. Jesus took this further. He told his followers to love their enemies and pray for those who hurt them.
heart: It is easy to be decent to people who like you. Real strength shows up when you help someone you do not get along with. Kindness does not mean you agree with them. It means you refuse to let hate decide how you act. Do one useful thing for someone who has wronged you this week.
holdOn: Doing good to someone who wronged me is real strength.
prayer: God, you were kind to me when I was against you. Help me do good to people who are against me. Soften my heart, and show me one way to help today. When I want to see them fail, change what I want. Let your kindness show in how I treat them. Amen.
teaser: God's law gave a strange order about your enemy's donkey.

title: His Presence Goes With You
verse: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
meaning: After Israel worshiped a golden calf, Moses begged God not to leave them. God answered with a promise: his presence would go with them, and he would give them rest. Moses would not lead alone. Moses even said that if God would not go with them, he did not want to leave at all.
heart: Success without God's presence is empty, and Moses knew it. Grades, money and wins can be good gifts. They make poor gods, and they cannot go with you everywhere. Before you chase your next goal, ask God to go with you. Start this day by inviting him into your plans, your work and your rest.
holdOn: I would rather have God with me than any success without him.
prayer: Lord, I do not want to go anywhere without you. Go with me today into my work, my friendships and my plans. Give me rest in knowing you are near. When I feel lonely or lost, remind me that you are with me. That is enough for me today. Amen.
teaser: Moses refused to move forward unless one thing came with him.

title: No Revenge, No Grudge
verse: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
meaning: God's law told Israel not to take revenge or hold a grudge against their own people. Instead they were to love their neighbor as themselves. Jesus later called this one of the greatest commands. Leviticus links love to God's own name: I am the LORD. Loving your neighbor is part of belonging to him.
heart: Revenge feels strong, and grudges feel safe. Both slowly eat you alive. Is there someone you keep replaying in your head? Letting go is not saying it did not matter. It is handing the case to God, the fair judge. You do not have to trust them again, but you can choose to let go of payback today.
holdOn: I can let go of revenge without pretending the hurt was nothing.
prayer: God, you know who hurt me and how much. I give you my desire to get even. Help me love my neighbor, even the one who wronged me. Free me from this grudge. When the old anger comes back, help me release it again, as many times as it takes. Amen.
teaser: Revenge feels strong. This old command says it is the weaker choice.

title: The Blessing Over You
verse: ‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
meaning: God gave this blessing to Israel's priests to speak over the people. It is full of God's face turned toward them: kindness, grace and peace. God wanted his people to know he looked at them with favor. Aaron and his sons spoke it over Israel. God said that in this way, they would put his name on his people.
heart: Many men grow up without hearing anyone bless them out loud. Read these words slowly as God's heart toward you. You do not have to earn God's kindness first. His face is already turned toward you with peace. Then speak a kind word of blessing over someone else today.
holdOn: God's face is turned toward me with grace and peace.
prayer: LORD, bless me and keep me. Let your face shine on me today. Be gracious to me where I have failed, and give me your peace where I am restless. Make me a blessing to others. Teach me to speak words that lift people up, the way your blessing lifts me. Amen.
teaser: Many men have never heard someone bless them out loud. Here are the words.

title: Shared Burden
verse: I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you don’t bear it yourself alone.
meaning: Moses was crushed by the complaints of the whole nation. He told God the load was too heavy. God answered by putting his Spirit on seventy elders, so they could carry the burden with him. The same Spirit that rested on Moses rested on them. Moses was not meant to lead alone, and neither are you.
heart: God's answer to Moses' burnout was people. Leaders who try to do everything alone eventually break. Who shares your load? Burnout often starts with one thought: I will just do it myself. Shared weight is lighter weight. If no one does, take one step this week to let someone in.
holdOn: God often answers my heavy load by sending people to share it.
prayer: God, you heard Moses when he said he could not go on. Hear me too. Send people to share my load, and help me stop pretending I can do it all alone. Give me the courage to tell someone the truth about how tired I really am. Amen.
teaser: Moses told God he could not go on. God's answer came with seventy names.

title: God Does Not Lie
verse: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and he won’t do it? Or has he spoken, and he won’t make it good?
meaning: A foreign king hired a prophet named Balaam to curse Israel. Instead God made him bless them. Balaam said God is not like people who lie or change their minds. What God promises, he does. The king tried three times to get a curse from Balaam. Each time, God turned it into a blessing.
heart: People break promises, even people you trust. That can make it hard to trust anyone, including God. But God is not like the men who let you down. His promises are not moods. What he said yesterday is still true this morning. Pick one promise from God and hold on to it today.
holdOn: God is not a man who lies. What he says, he will do.
prayer: Faithful God, people have broken their word to me, and I have broken mine. You never have. Help me trust your promises today, and make me a man who keeps his word too. When my feelings tell me you have forgotten me, let your word speak louder. Amen.
teaser: A prophet was paid to curse Israel. What came out of his mouth surprised everyone.

title: On Your Heart
verse: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
meaning: Moses told Israel that God's words were not just for the temple or a scroll. They were meant to live on their hearts, shaping what they loved and how they lived every day. This comes right after the great command to love God with all your heart. Love grows where his words are kept close.
heart: What is written on your heart right now? Song lyrics, ads, other people's opinions? Pick one verse this week and learn it by heart. Write it on a card, set it as your lock screen, or say it on your drive. Say it when you wake up and before you sleep.
holdOn: I want God's words written on my heart, not just in a book.
prayer: Lord, write your words on my heart. Push out the lies I have learned. Help me remember your truth when I need it most, and let it shape how I live today. When temptation or fear comes, bring your word to my mind before anything else. Amen.
teaser: What is written on your heart? Moses had a plan for that.

title: Talk About It Everywhere
verse: and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
meaning: God told parents in Israel to teach his words to their children all day long. They talked at home, on the road, at bedtime and in the morning. Faith was meant to be part of normal life. Few people owned scrolls then. Faith passed from parents to children through talk at the table and on the road.
heart: Faith is not meant to stay inside a church building. You can talk about God in the car, at the gym or with a little brother. You do not need a sermon. Honest words about your own life often speak louder than arguments. Today, mention one thing God has done for you in a normal conversation.
holdOn: Faith belongs in ordinary conversations, not just on Sundays.
prayer: God, I do not want my faith to stay hidden. Give me natural ways to talk about you today. Help me live in a way that makes people curious about you. Make me ready to share my story without fear, and give me the right moments. Amen.
teaser: God told Israel to talk about him in four ordinary places. You visit them daily.

title: Remember the Road
verse: You shall remember all the way which the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.
meaning: After forty years in the desert, Moses told Israel to remember how God led them. The hard years were not wasted. God used them to humble them, test them and show what was in their hearts. He also fed them with manna, so they would learn that people live by every word from God's mouth.
heart: Hard seasons reveal what is in you. Look back at a tough year in your life. What did God show you about yourself, and how did he carry you? Pain is not proof that God left you. Often it is where he was doing deep work. Write it down and thank him.
holdOn: God used the hard road to show me what was in my heart.
prayer: Lord, help me remember how you led me through hard times. Show me what they revealed in my heart. Humble me where I am proud, and thank you for never letting go. Use the hard days I am in right now to make me humble and strong in you. Amen.
teaser: Israel wandered for forty years. Moses said those years taught them something.

title: God Defends the Weak
verse: He executes justice for the fatherless and widow and loves the foreigner in giving him food and clothing.
meaning: Moses said God brings justice for the fatherless and the widow. He loves the foreigner and gives him food and clothes. Israel's mighty God cared most for the people others ignored. Israel had been strangers in Egypt. God told them to remember that and love the stranger among them.
heart: Real strength protects people who cannot protect themselves. Who is easy to overlook around you: the new guy, the kid without a dad, the one who does not fit in? Standing with someone can be simple: a seat at lunch, a kind word, a refusal to laugh along. Do one thing to stand with him today.
holdOn: God's strength protects the weak, and mine should too.
prayer: God of justice, you defend the fatherless and the stranger. Make me like you. Open my eyes to people others ignore, and give me courage to stand with them. Forgive me for the times I went along with the crowd and left someone standing alone. Amen.
teaser: Israel's mighty God had a soft spot. It was for people others ignored.

title: Open Hands
verse: If a poor man, one of your brothers, is with you within any of your gates in your land which the LORD your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother;
meaning: God told Israel not to harden their hearts or shut their hands to a poor brother. Generosity was not optional kindness. It was part of being God's people in the land he gave them. Every seventh year, debts between Israelites were to be canceled. God did not want anyone trapped in poverty forever.
heart: A closed fist and a hard heart often go together. You may not have much money, but you have something to give: time, food, skills or a ride. Giving loosens money's grip on you. It also reminds you that God is your provider, not your paycheck. Open your hand to someone in need this week.
holdOn: A hard heart and a closed hand go together. I choose open hands.
prayer: Lord, everything I have came from you. Keep my heart soft and my hands open. Show me someone in need today, and help me give gladly, without showing off. When I am tempted to look away from someone in need, turn my eyes back and move my hands. Amen.
teaser: God connected two body parts in this command: your heart and your hand.

title: Follow What Is Right
verse: You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live and inherit the land which the LORD your God gives you.
meaning: Moses told Israel's judges to follow justice and only justice. No bribes, no favorites and no shortcuts were allowed. A fair nation would live and flourish in the land God gave them. Judges were not to take bribes, because a gift blinds the eyes of the wise. God cared about fair courts.
heart: Small shortcuts add up: a copied answer, a padded timesheet, a lie to look good. Choose what is right even when it costs you. Honesty in small things builds a man people can trust with big things. Today, pick one small area where you will be fully honest.
holdOn: I want to follow what is right, even when a shortcut is easier.
prayer: God, you are always fair. Make me a man who does what is right when it is easy and when it costs me. Forgive my shortcuts, and give me a clean conscience. Give me the backbone to speak up when I see something unfair happen. Amen.
teaser: Small shortcuts add up. Moses told Israel's judges to follow one thing only.

title: Choose Life
verse: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants,
meaning: At the end of his life, Moses put a clear choice before Israel: life or death, blessing or curse. He called heaven and earth as witnesses and begged them to choose life by loving God. Choosing life meant loving God, listening to him and holding on to him. He is their life, Moses said.
heart: Every day you choose what feeds your life and what slowly drains it. Some habits look fun but lead toward death. The small choices add up. Sleep, friends, screens and words slowly shape the man you become. Name one choice today that leads toward life, and make it before noon.
holdOn: Every day I get to choose life with God.
prayer: Lord, you set life in front of me. Help me choose it in my habits, my words and my friendships. When I am drawn toward what drains me, pull me back to you. Thank you that it is never too late to turn around and choose you. Amen.
teaser: Moses put two roads in front of a nation and begged them to pick one.

title: The Rock
verse: The Rock: his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness who does no wrong, just and right is he.
meaning: In his final song, Moses called God the Rock. His work is perfect and his ways are just. He is faithful and does no wrong. In a shaky world, God was the one thing that would not move. Rock was a strong word for desert people. It meant shelter, safety and a firm place to stand.
heart: You may stand on grades, a relationship, money or your reputation. All of them can shift. God does not. Even your own feelings change by the hour. God's goodness does not depend on how you feel. When life feels unstable this week, remind yourself who your Rock is.
holdOn: Everything else can shift. God is my Rock.
prayer: God, you are my Rock. Everything else I lean on can crack. Help me build my life on you. When I feel shaky, remind me that you are faithful and do no wrong. When everything around me shifts, keep my feet on solid ground in you. Amen.
teaser: Moses ended his life with a song about the one thing that does not move.

title: Arms Underneath
verse: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, ‘Destroy!’
meaning: Moses blessed Israel with a picture of God's care. God is their home, and underneath them are his everlasting arms. When they fall, they do not fall past his reach. These were among his last words to Israel. After a lifetime of leading them, Moses pointed them to the arms that would never tire.
heart: Some men act tough because they are afraid of falling. With God, falling does not mean the end. His arms are underneath you. That does not make you careless. It makes you brave enough to step out. Let that give you courage to try, fail and get back up.
holdOn: When I fall, I fall into everlasting arms.
prayer: Eternal God, be my home. When I fall, catch me. When I am afraid to try, remind me that your arms are underneath me. Give me courage to get back up. Hold me when I feel like I am slipping, and let me rest in your strength tonight. Amen.
teaser: Moses gave Israel a picture of what is underneath them when they fall.

title: Wherever You Go
verse: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
meaning: Moses was dead, and Joshua now had to lead Israel into a land full of enemies. God told him three times to be strong and brave. The reason was not Joshua's skill. God would be with him everywhere. God also told him to keep his law close and think on it day and night. Courage and obedience went together.
heart: God does not tell you to be brave because you are strong. He tells you because he is with you. Fear may still show up. Courage is doing the right thing while fear is still in the room. Wherever you go today, class, work, the gym or a hard talk, go with that promise.
holdOn: I can be strong and brave because God is with me wherever I go.
prayer: Lord, you told Joshua not to be afraid because you were with him. I am afraid of some things today. Be with me wherever I go, and give me courage that comes from you. Keep me close to your word, so I know which way to go. Amen.
teaser: God told Joshua to be brave three times. The reason was not what you think.

title: Stones to Remember
verse: that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’
meaning: After Israel crossed the Jordan River on dry ground, God told them to stack twelve stones. When their children asked what the stones meant, they would tell the story of what God had done. The stones came from the middle of the riverbed, where the priests had stood. They were proof that God had made a way.
heart: It is easy to forget what God has done for you. Make your own stones: a note on your phone, a journal, a photo. Your stories can also help someone younger trust God when his own river looks too wide. Write down one time God came through for you, so you remember it next time.
holdOn: I will mark what God has done so I do not forget it.
prayer: God, you have carried me more times than I remember. Help me mark what you have done. When I doubt you, bring those moments back to mind, and let me tell others. Give me a grateful heart that notices your help in small things, not only big ones. Amen.
teaser: Israel stacked twelve stones by a river. Kids were supposed to ask about them.

title: Choose Today
verse: If it seems evil to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”
meaning: Near the end of his life, Joshua gathered Israel and told them to choose whom they would serve. They could follow other gods if they wanted. But Joshua made his choice clear: he and his house would serve the LORD. The people answered that they too would serve the LORD. Joshua set up a large stone to witness their promise.
heart: Not choosing is still a choice. Joshua did not wait for the crowd. He decided first and said it out loud. Your choice now shapes the home you build later, and whoever looks up to you. What would it look like to say, today, that you will serve the LORD?
holdOn: As for me, I choose to serve the LORD.
prayer: Lord, I do not want to drift. Today I choose you. Help me follow through when the crowd goes another way. Make my home, now and in the future, a place that serves you. When following you costs me friends or fun, keep my choice firm. Amen.
teaser: Joshua gave a whole nation a choice. Then he went first.

title: The Least in the Family
verse: He said to him, “O Lord, how shall I save Israel? Behold, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”
meaning: God called Gideon to rescue Israel from raiders. Gideon was hiding at the time. He said his clan was the weakest and he was the least in his family. God did not argue. He promised to be with him. God's angel called him a mighty man of valor before Gideon had done a single brave thing.
heart: You may feel like the least likely guy to be used by God. That is exactly the kind of person God often calls. Stop listing your weaknesses today. God sees what you can become with him, not only what you are today. Ask God what he wants you to do, and trust him with it.
holdOn: God often calls the guy who feels the least ready.
prayer: God, I feel small and not ready. You called Gideon while he was hiding. Call me too. Help me trust your strength more than I fear my own weakness. Lead me. When I want to hide, give me the courage to step out and obey. Amen.
teaser: God called a man who was hiding. His reply was a list of reasons he was wrong.

title: The LORD Is Peace
verse: Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD, and called it “The LORD is Peace.” To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
meaning: After meeting God's angel, Gideon was terrified he would die. God told him not to be afraid. Gideon built an altar and named it The LORD Is Peace. His fear met God's calm. That same night, God sent Gideon to tear down his father's idol. Peace with God came first, then courage to act.
heart: Peace is not the absence of fear. It is God's presence in the middle of it. When your mind is racing today, stop for one minute. Anxiety is real, and sometimes it needs a doctor or a counselor too. God is not against help. Breathe slowly and pray: LORD, you are my peace.
holdOn: Peace is not the absence of fear. It is God with me in it.
prayer: LORD, you are peace. My mind races, and fear pushes in. Calm me the way you calmed Gideon. Be my peace today, in the noise and in the quiet. Thank you that I can come near you without fear, because you are kind to me. Amen.
teaser: Gideon thought he was about to die. Instead he built an altar with a strange name.

title: Closer Than a Brother
verse: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
meaning: This proverb warns that having lots of buddies can still leave you ruined. Many friends can be shallow. But there is a kind of friend who sticks closer than a brother, loyal when it costs him. In Israel, family was everything. Saying a friend can stick closer than that was a strong claim.
heart: A thousand followers cannot replace one real friend. Be that friend for someone. Loyalty is proven in the bad times, when you have nothing to gain from staying. This week, check in on a friend who is going through something, and keep showing up even when it is awkward.
holdOn: One loyal friend is worth more than many shallow ones.
prayer: God, thank you for the friends who stick with me. Make me a loyal friend, not a fair-weather one. Show me who needs me to show up this week. Thank you that Jesus is the friend who never leaves. Teach me to love my friends the way he loves me. Amen.
teaser: You can have many friends and still be alone. Proverbs explains why.

title: Three Strands
verse: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
meaning: The Teacher noticed that one man alone is easy to overpower. Two can defend each other. And a cord of three strands is hard to break. Life was never meant to be fought alone. He also said two are better than one, because when one falls, the other can lift him up.
heart: Lone wolves get picked off. Who has your back, and whose back do you have? Ask one or two friends to meet, pray or train together regularly. It does not need to be formal. A weekly breakfast or a group chat that prays can be enough. Put God in the middle, and you become a three-strand cord.
holdOn: I am stronger with brothers beside me and God in the middle.
prayer: God, I do not want to fight alone. Give me brothers who stand with me, and make me one who stands with them. Be the third strand that holds us together. When I start to pull away from people, draw me back into honest friendship. Amen.
teaser: One man alone is easy to beat. The Teacher had a better plan.

title: Wounds From a Friend
verse: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
meaning: A friend who tells you a hard truth may hurt you, but his wounds are faithful. An enemy may flatter you with many kisses. The proverb says to trust the honest friend over the smooth talker. Kisses here means the show of friendship. Judas would later betray Jesus with a kiss.
heart: It stings when a friend calls you out. Pride wants to win the argument. Wisdom wants to learn something, even from words that hurt. Before you get defensive, ask if he is right. And be that honest friend yourself, with kindness. Who needs a hard but loving word from you this week?
holdOn: Honest wounds from a friend are better than flattery from an enemy.
prayer: Lord, give me friends who tell me the truth, and the humility to hear it. Make me honest with others in a kind way. Guard me from people who only flatter me. When I need to say something hard, help me say it with love and good timing. Amen.
teaser: Some wounds are good for you. Some kisses are not. Proverbs explains.

title: A Covenant of Friends
verse: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
meaning: After David beat Goliath, Jonathan, the king's son, made a covenant with him. Jonathan loved David like himself. He later protected David from his own father, even though it cost him the throne. Jonathan even gave David his robe, his sword, his bow and his belt. It was a picture of giving up his place.
heart: Jonathan had every reason to be jealous of David, but he chose loyalty. Real friends cheer when you win, even when it costs them. Envy keeps score. Love is glad when a brother does well, even when he does better than you. Whose win can you celebrate today without envy?
holdOn: Real friendship chooses loyalty over jealousy, even when it costs.
prayer: God, thank you for loyal friends. Kill the jealousy in me. Help me celebrate other men's wins and stand by them when it costs me something. Make me a friend like Jonathan. Help me be glad for my friends' blessings, and content with the ones you gave me. Amen.
teaser: The king's son had every reason to hate David. He made a promise instead.

title: Greater Love
verse: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
meaning: Jesus said this the night before he died. The greatest love is laying down your life for your friends. The next day he did exactly that, dying on the cross for people who would run away. He also called his followers friends, not servants. He had shared with them everything he heard from the Father.
heart: You may never die for a friend, but you can lay down your time, pride and comfort for one. Love costs something. That might mean giving up your seat, your Saturday or the last word in an argument. Give something up for someone else today, quietly, the way Jesus did.
holdOn: The greatest love lays down its life. Jesus did that for me.
prayer: Jesus, you laid down your life for me, even when I was not loyal to you. Thank you. Teach me to give up my comfort for others, and to love like you love. When love costs me, remind me what loving me cost you on the cross. Amen.
teaser: Jesus described the greatest love. The next day, he showed it.

title: Growing Up Right
verse: The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with the LORD and also with men.
meaning: Samuel grew up in the temple while the priest's own sons were corrupt. Even in a bad environment, the boy kept growing in favor with God and with people. His character was being built quietly. Luke later used almost the same words for the boy Jesus, who grew in favor with God and people.
heart: You cannot always choose your surroundings, but you can choose who you become in them. Character grows slowly, through small daily choices. Bad examples around you do not have to become your excuse. Samuel grew anyway. Pick one habit today that helps you grow, and do it even if no one notices.
holdOn: I can grow in favor with God, even in a bad environment.
prayer: Lord, I want to grow into a man you are pleased with. Protect me from what corrupts. Build my character day by day, even when no one is watching. Give me people who build me up, and help me be a good influence on others. Amen.
teaser: Samuel grew up around corrupt leaders. He still turned out right. How?

title: Words That Hold
verse: Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
meaning: As Samuel grew, God was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground. What Samuel spoke from God came true, and people trusted him. His words carried weight. All Israel, from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, came to know he was a true prophet.
heart: Do your words carry weight? If you often exaggerate or break small promises, people stop listening. Say less, mean more. Trust takes years to build and seconds to lose. Being careful with small words protects it. Today, keep one small promise exactly as you said it.
holdOn: I want my words to carry weight because I keep them.
prayer: God, be with me like you were with Samuel. Help me speak truth and keep my word. Let my yes mean yes and my no mean no, every single time. Forgive me for the times I said things just to sound good. Make my words honest and few. Amen.
teaser: None of Samuel's words fell to the ground. What does that even mean?

title: Speak, I Am Listening
verse: The LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears.”
meaning: God called young Samuel in the night, but Samuel thought it was the old priest Eli. Eli told him how to answer. When God called again, Samuel said: Speak, your servant is listening. Back then the word of the LORD was rare. God chose to speak to a boy who was ready to listen.
heart: God still speaks, mostly through his word, but noise drowns him out. Find five quiet minutes today. Listening also means being willing to obey. Samuel's first message from God was a hard one to deliver. Put the phone in another room, read the verse again, and pray Samuel's prayer: speak, I am listening.
holdOn: I want to hear God more than I want to be heard.
prayer: Speak, Lord. I am listening. Turn down the noise in my head and around me. Help me hear you in your word, and give me the courage to do what you say. If you ask me to do something hard, help me trust you and say yes. Amen.
teaser: God called a boy in the night. It took him three tries to answer.

title: Thus Far He Helped
verse: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
meaning: After God gave Israel victory over the Philistines, Samuel set up a stone. He named it Ebenezer, which means stone of help, saying the LORD had helped them all the way up to that point. Years before, Israel had lost a battle at a place also called Ebenezer. Now the name stood for God's help.
heart: You do not know what is ahead, but you can look back and see how far God has brought you. Name three times God helped you. Gratitude is not pretending life is easy. It is noticing that God has not let go. Let that past help give you courage for what is next.
holdOn: Up to now, the LORD has helped me. He is not stopping.
prayer: LORD, you have helped me all the way here. Thank you for times I did not even notice. Help me trust you with what is ahead because of what you have already done. Let my life become a stone of help that points others to you. Amen.
teaser: Samuel set up a stone with a name that means more than you think.

title: I Will Keep Praying
verse: Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and the right way.
meaning: Israel had rejected God's way by demanding a king. Samuel could have walked away hurt. Instead he said it would be a sin to stop praying for them. He kept praying and kept teaching them the right way. Samuel also told them not to fear, because God would not abandon his people for his great name's sake.
heart: When people let you down, it is tempting to write them off. Samuel prayed instead. Think of someone who has disappointed you. Praying for someone keeps your heart from turning cold. It is hard to hate a man you pray for. Pray for that person by name today, and ask God for their good.
holdOn: I will not stop praying for people, even when they let me down.
prayer: God, there are people I have given up on. Forgive me. Help me keep praying for them like Samuel did. Do good in their lives, and soften my heart toward them. Keep me from bitterness, and help me keep showing them what is right with patience. Amen.
teaser: Israel rejected Samuel's leadership. He answered with a surprising promise.

title: The Battle Is the LORD's
verse: and that all this assembly may know that the LORD doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
meaning: Young David faced Goliath with a sling while the soldiers hid. He told the giant that God does not save by sword or spear. The battle belonged to the LORD, and everyone would see it. David had trusted God against a lion and a bear while guarding sheep. That trust had grown in hidden places.
heart: Your giants may be debt, addiction, anxiety or fear of failing. David did not pretend Goliath was small. He just knew God was bigger. Giving it to God does not mean doing nothing. David still ran toward the fight. Name your giant today, and give the battle to God first.
holdOn: My giant is real, but the battle belongs to the LORD.
prayer: LORD, I have a giant in front of me. I cannot beat it on my own. The battle is yours. Give me David's courage, and let people see your strength in my weakness. Help me take the next step, and get the help I need, while I trust you with the outcome. Amen.
teaser: Soldiers hid from Goliath. A teenager walked out with a sling and one sentence.

title: In the Name of the LORD
verse: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
meaning: Goliath came with a sword, a spear and a javelin. David came with a sling and a name. He told the giant he came in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God Goliath had mocked. Saul had dressed David in his own armor. David could not move in it, so he went out as he was.
heart: David's confidence was not in his own skill. It was in who he belonged to. When you face something big today, remember whose name you carry. You do not have to fight in someone else's armor. God can use what is already in your hand. Walk in as his, not as someone trying to prove himself.
holdOn: I do not face my giants alone. I go in God's name.
prayer: LORD of Armies, I come to today in your name. Take away my need to prove myself. Give me courage that rests on you, not on what I can do. When I feel small next to the giant today, remind me how big you are. Amen.
teaser: Goliath brought three weapons. David brought one name.

title: Go in Peace
verse: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, because we have both sworn in the LORD’s name, saying, ‘The LORD is between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, forever.’” He arose and departed; and Jonathan went into the city.
meaning: Jonathan learned his father Saul wanted David dead. He warned David and helped him escape. Before they parted, the two friends wept and reminded each other of their promise: the LORD stands between us forever. They had used arrows shot into a field as a secret signal. The message meant David had to run.
heart: Some goodbyes are hard, even between strong men. Jonathan and David did not hide their tears. Friendship that is built on God can survive distance. Distance tests a friendship. A short message can keep a bond alive across years and miles. Text or call a friend you have not seen in a while.
holdOn: A friendship built on God can survive distance and goodbyes.
prayer: God, thank you for friends who have stood by me. Be between me and them, even when life pulls us apart. Help me keep my promises and stay in touch. When saying goodbye hurts, comfort me with the truth that you go with each of us. Amen.
teaser: Two warriors said goodbye in a field. Neither of them hid his tears.

title: Not By My Hand
verse: He said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
meaning: King Saul hunted David to kill him. One day Saul walked into the very cave where David was hiding. David's men urged him to strike. David refused. He would not harm the king God had anointed. David only cut off a corner of Saul's robe. Even that bothered his conscience afterward.
heart: Revenge was easy and close, and David's men cheered him on. He still said no. Strength is knowing when not to strike. Holding back is not the same as doing nothing. David spoke to Saul honestly afterward, from a safe distance. When you could hit back this week, with words or fists, hold back and leave it to God.
holdOn: Real strength knows when not to strike back.
prayer: Lord, when I want to get even, hold my hand back. Give me David's self-control. Help me trust you with justice instead of taking it into my own hands today. Give me a sensitive conscience, so I notice even small wrongs before they grow in me. Amen.
teaser: David had his enemy alone in a cave. His men told him to strike.

title: Strength in God
verse: David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people were grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
meaning: Raiders burned David's town and took the families. His own men were so crushed that they talked of stoning him. David was alone and in deep distress. Then he found strength in the LORD his God. He asked God what to do, then went after the raiders. Every family and every child was brought back.
heart: There may come a day when even your friends turn on you. David did not wait for someone to cheer him up. He went to God. Strengthening yourself in God can look like prayer, a psalm read aloud, or remembering what he has done. On your low days, go to God first, before your phone or your friends.
holdOn: When no one else lifts me up, I can find strength in God.
prayer: LORD my God, there are days when I feel alone and blamed. Strengthen me in you. Lift my head when others push me down, and show me the next step. Then give me the courage to stand up, take that step and not look back. Amen.
teaser: David's own men wanted to stone him. Here is where he went for strength.

title: Who Am I?
verse: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD; and he said, “Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
meaning: God promised King David that his family line would last forever. David did not brag. He went in and sat before the LORD, amazed, and asked: who am I, that you have brought me this far? David had wanted to build a house for God. Instead, God promised to build David's house, a family line that would lead to Jesus.
heart: Success can make a man proud fast. David's response was wonder and thanks. Look at what you have today: health, friends, chances. Pride says I earned this. Gratitude says I was given this. Only one of them leaves room for God. Sit for a minute and say thank you, as if none of it was owed to you.
holdOn: Who am I, that God has brought me this far?
prayer: Lord GOD, who am I that you would care for me? Everything good I have is from you. Keep me humble when things go well, and grateful every day. When I start to think I made it on my own, bring me back to sit before you. Amen.
teaser: God made David a huge promise. David's reply was a question.

title: An Understanding Heart
verse: Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?”
meaning: When young Solomon became king, God offered him anything. Solomon did not ask for money or long life. He asked for an understanding heart to tell good from evil and to lead people well. God was pleased. God gave Solomon wisdom first, and also riches and honor he had not asked for.
heart: If God offered you anything, what would you ask for? Most of us would ask for comfort. Solomon asked for wisdom. Wisdom is not just knowing facts. It is seeing what is right and having the backbone to choose it. Ask God today for wisdom in one real decision you are facing.
holdOn: I want a wise heart more than an easy life.
prayer: God, give me an understanding heart. Help me tell good from evil when it is not obvious. Make me wise in my choices, my words and how I treat people. When I do not know what to do, let me ask you before I ask anyone else. Amen.
teaser: God offered a young king anything he wanted. He chose something boring and wise.

title: Bigger Than the Building
verse: But will God in very deed dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
meaning: Solomon built a magnificent temple for God. At its opening, he prayed with honesty: heaven itself cannot contain you, so how could this house? God was far bigger than anything Solomon could build. Yet God still chose to meet his people there. He is too big for a building, and still near enough to hear a prayer.
heart: We can shrink God down to fit our schedule, our church or our ideas. He does not fit. Spend a minute outside today looking at the sky. Stars, storms and mountains are small next to the one who made them. Let it remind you how big God really is.
holdOn: God is bigger than anything I could build or imagine.
prayer: God, heaven cannot hold you, and I keep trying to make you small. Forgive me. Open my eyes to how great you are, and let that make my worries smaller. Thank you that a God this great still bends down to listen when I pray. Amen.
teaser: Solomon built God the greatest building of his day. Then he said it was too small.

title: Show Yourself a Man
verse: “I am going the way of all the earth. You be strong therefore, and show yourself a man;
meaning: As King David was dying, he called his son Solomon. He told him to be strong and show himself a man. In the next verse David explains what that meant: walk in God's ways and keep his commands. Solomon was still young. David knew the throne would test him in ways no battle could.
heart: Some say being a man means being loud, rich or hard. David defined it as faithfulness to God. Strength that matters is quiet: keeping your word, protecting the weak and owning your mistakes. Today, show yourself a man by doing the right thing quietly when nobody is clapping.
holdOn: Being a man means being strong in faithfulness to God.
prayer: God, show me what real manhood looks like. Make me strong in the right things: honesty, faith, courage and love. Help me walk in your ways today, even when no one sees. Where I have tried to prove myself the wrong way, turn me back to your way. Amen.
teaser: A dying king told his son to show himself a man. Then he defined it.

title: Sleep and Eat
verse: He lay down and slept under a juniper tree; and behold, an angel touched him, and said to him, “Arise and eat!”
meaning: After a huge victory, the prophet Elijah ran for his life and collapsed in despair. He wanted to die. God did not lecture him. An angel let him sleep, then woke him up to eat. This happened twice. The angel said the trip ahead was too great for him, and Elijah went on in that strength.
heart: Sometimes your low mood is not only spiritual. You may need sleep, food and help. God cared for Elijah's body first. Hopeless thoughts can lie to you, even when they feel completely true. If you feel hopeless, rest, eat, and tell someone you trust. If it is serious, get help today.
holdOn: God cares for my body as well as my soul.
prayer: God, you cared for Elijah when he was worn out and hopeless. Care for me too. Help me rest, eat well and ask for help when I need it. Give me hope again. When I want to give up, send someone to sit with me, and remind me you are not done with me. Amen.
teaser: A great prophet wanted to die. God's first answer was a nap and a meal.

title: The Quiet Voice
verse: After the earthquake a fire passed; but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.
meaning: God told Elijah to stand on the mountain. A great wind came, then an earthquake, then fire, but God was not in them. Then came a still small voice. God spoke in the quiet. In that quiet, God gave Elijah new work to do and told him he was not alone. Seven thousand had stayed faithful.
heart: We often look for God in big moments. He often speaks quietly, and you will miss it if you never slow down. Sit in silence for three minutes today. No phone, no music. Quiet may feel strange at first. Your mind will wander, and that is normal. Just listen.
holdOn: God often speaks in a whisper, so I need to slow down.
prayer: Lord, my life is loud. Help me make room for quiet so I can hear you. Speak to me in the stillness today, and give me ears to listen. When I feel alone in my faith, remind me that you have others standing with me. Amen.
teaser: God was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire. He was somewhere quieter.

title: Just Wash
verse: His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”
meaning: Naaman was a powerful army commander with a skin disease. The prophet told him to wash in the Jordan seven times. Naaman was offended by the simple order. His servants talked him into obeying, and he was healed. His skin became like a young boy's. Naaman went back to thank the prophet and said Israel's God was the true God.
heart: Pride wants a big, impressive fix. God often asks for simple obedience. Is there a simple step you keep skipping because it feels beneath you, like an apology or asking for help? Small obedience often opens the door to big change. Naaman's healing started in muddy water. Do it today.
holdOn: Pride wants something impressive. God often asks for something simple.
prayer: God, I am proud like Naaman. Humble me. Help me obey you in small, simple ways, even when they feel beneath me. Heal what my pride has kept sick. Thank you for people who tell me the truth when my pride gets in the way, like Naaman's servants did. Amen.
teaser: A powerful general got an easy fix for his disease. He was furious.

title: More With Us
verse: He answered, “Don’t be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”
meaning: An enemy army surrounded the city to capture the prophet Elisha. His servant panicked. Elisha said there were more with them than against them. God opened the servant's eyes to see the hills full of fiery chariots. Then Elisha prayed, and God struck the soldiers with blindness. Elisha led them away and had them fed, not killed.
heart: Fear only counts what you can see. Faith remembers that God is unseen but real. You may not see chariots of fire. You can still trust that God is closer than the trouble. When you feel outnumbered this week, pray Elisha's prayer for yourself: Lord, open my eyes to see.
holdOn: Those who are with me are more than those against me.
prayer: Lord, open my eyes. When I feel surrounded and outnumbered, show me that you are near and stronger than what I see. Calm my panic, and give me courage. And when I have the upper hand over someone, teach me to show mercy like Elisha did. Amen.
teaser: A servant woke up to an army around the city. Then his eyes were opened.

title: A Tender Heart
verse: because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and have torn your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you,’ says the LORD.
meaning: Young King Josiah heard God's law read for the first time and realized how far his nation had wandered. He tore his clothes and wept. God said he heard him because his heart was tender and humble. Josiah then cleared idols out of the land and led the people back to keeping God's covenant.
heart: A hard heart shrugs at wrong. A tender heart feels it and turns. That is not weakness. It is what God listens to. If something you did is bothering you, do not bury it. Shame wants you to hide. God wants you to come home, and his mercy is ready. Bring it to God today.
holdOn: God listens to a heart that is tender and humble.
prayer: God, keep my heart from going hard. When I hear your word, let it reach me. Make me quick to feel my sin and quick to turn back to you. Thank you that a broken heart is not something you turn away. Lead me to change, not just feel bad. Amen.
teaser: A young king heard God's law and ripped his clothes. God noticed.
