title: Make It Known
verse: Oh give thanks to the LORD. Call on his name. Make what he has done known among the peoples.
meaning: When the ark came to Jerusalem, David wrote a song of thanks. He told the people to give thanks, call on God's name, and tell the nations what God had done. Thanks was meant to be shared. David also put singers in charge of giving thanks every day. Praise was not left to chance.
heart: Gratitude grows when you say it out loud. Share one thing God has done for you with a friend or online today. Your story of God's help might be exactly what a struggling friend needs to hear. It does not need to be preachy, just honest.
holdOn: Thanks grows when I say it out loud.
prayer: LORD, thank you for what you have done in my life. Give me the courage to tell others about it in honest, simple words. Let my thanks point people to you. Keep my thanks honest on hard days too, not only when life goes my way. Amen.
teaser: David's song of thanks came with an instruction: do not keep it to yourself.

title: Know the God of Your Father
verse: You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for the LORD searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
meaning: Before he died, David charged his son Solomon to know God personally and serve him with a whole heart and willing mind. God sees every thought. Those who seek him will find him. David also gave Solomon the plans for the temple, and told him not to be afraid of the work.
heart: You may have inherited faith from family, or no faith at all. Either way, it has to become your own. Seek God for yourself today. Borrowed faith may hold for a while. Faith you have tested yourself is ready when life gets hard. Read, pray and ask him to make himself real to you.
holdOn: Faith has to become my own. If I seek God, I will find him.
prayer: God, I want to know you for myself, not just through others. Make yourself real to me. Help me serve you with a whole heart and a willing mind. If my faith has been mostly borrowed, make it mine, and help me seek you every day. Amen.
teaser: David gave his son one charge before he died. It was not about the throne.

title: Giving Back What Is His
verse: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.
meaning: David and the people gave huge gifts to build the temple. Then David prayed, amazed: who are we to give like this? Everything comes from you, and we have only given you back your own. The people gave freely and with a whole heart, and they rejoiced in their giving.
heart: Your money, time and talent are on loan from God. Giving is not a favor to him. It is returning what is his. Holding money too tightly can make a man anxious and small. Open hands make room for trust. Give something back this week: some money, an hour, or a skill.
holdOn: Everything I have came from God. Giving is giving back.
prayer: Lord, everything I have is from you. Free me from holding on too tight. Teach me to give gladly, knowing I am only giving you back your own gifts. Let my giving be glad and quiet, not for show, and use it to help someone today. Amen.
teaser: David gave a fortune to God. Then he said none of it was really his.

title: Wisdom to Lead
verse: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”
meaning: Solomon repeated his request when God appeared to him. He asked for wisdom and knowledge to lead the people well. He knew leading was not about his glory. It was about serving God's people. The phrase go out and come in meant leading people in daily life, in work and in war.
heart: Whether you lead a team, a class project or just yourself, you need wisdom. Leadership is service, not status. A good leader goes first in the hard work and last in the line for credit. Ask God today for wisdom for one person or group that depends on you.
holdOn: Leading well starts with asking God for wisdom.
prayer: God, I need wisdom to lead well, even if it is only leading myself. Help me serve others instead of chasing status. Give me knowledge, humility and a servant heart today. Keep me from using people to look good. Help me make the people around me better. Amen.
teaser: Solomon asked God for the same thing twice. Both times, it was not money.

title: Our Eyes Are on You
verse: Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
meaning: A huge army marched against King Jehoshaphat. He gathered the people and prayed honestly. We have no power against this crowd. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you. God answered that the battle was his. The next morning, the people marched out singing, and the enemy armies turned on each other.
heart: Admitting you do not know what to do is not weakness. It is the start of real prayer. Bring God the problem you cannot solve today. Jehoshaphat also gathered people to pray with him. You do not have to face it alone. Tell him plainly: I do not know what to do, but my eyes are on you.
holdOn: I do not know what to do, but my eyes are on God.
prayer: God, I do not know what to do. I feel outmatched. My eyes are on you. Show me the way forward, and fight for me where I am weak. Give me the patience to wait for your answer, and the faith to praise you before I see it. Amen.
teaser: A king faced a huge army and admitted something most leaders never say.

title: Do Not Quit
verse: But you be strong! Don’t let your hands be slack, for your work will be rewarded.”
meaning: A prophet encouraged King Asa to keep up his work of turning the nation back to God. Do not let your hands go slack, he said. Your work will be rewarded. Change was hard, but worth it. Asa listened. He removed idols, repaired the LORD's altar and gathered the people to seek God together.
heart: Doing the right thing often feels pointless at first. Habits, honesty and faith take time to bear fruit. Do not quit on the good thing you started. Seeds stay underground for a while before anything shows. Good growth often starts where no one can see it. Do one more rep of it today.
holdOn: Do not let my hands go slack. Good work will bear fruit.
prayer: God, I get tired of doing what is right when I do not see results. Strengthen my hands. Help me keep going, trusting that you see and reward faithful work. When I want to give up on a good habit, remind me why I started. Amen.
teaser: A prophet gave a king advice that works for anyone trying to change.

title: He Is Good
verse: They sang to one another in praising and giving thanks to the LORD, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.” All the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the LORD’s house had been laid.
meaning: The exiles came home and laid the foundation of a new temple. The people sang and shouted that God is good and his love lasts forever. Some old men wept, remembering the first temple, while others cheered. The shouting and the weeping were so loud together that people could not tell one sound from the other.
heart: Joy and grief can sit side by side. You can thank God for what he is rebuilding while still missing what you lost. God is not afraid of your mixed feelings. Bring him both the thanks and the ache. Today, name one new start God has given you, and thank him for it.
holdOn: God is good, and his love lasts forever.
prayer: LORD, you are good, and your love never ends. Thank you for the new starts you give me. Hold my grief and my joy together, and keep rebuilding my life. When a new start feels small next to what I lost, help me see your hand in it. Amen.
teaser: When the new temple's foundation was laid, half the crowd cheered and half cried.

title: Study, Do, Teach
verse: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
meaning: Ezra was a teacher who set his heart on three things in order: study God's law, do it, and teach it. He did not teach what he had not lived. His life matched his words. God's good hand was on Ezra, and the king gave him everything he asked for the trip to Jerusalem.
heart: It is easy to know a lot and live little. Ezra's order matters: learn, live, then teach. People often listen more to how you live than to what you know. Take today's verse and do one thing it says before you tell anyone else about it.
holdOn: I want to study God's word, live it, and then teach it.
prayer: God, set my heart on your word like Ezra did. Help me study it, live it and only then teach it. Make my life match what I say, every day. Keep me from showing off what I know. Make me humble enough to keep learning. Amen.
teaser: Ezra did three things in a specific order. Most of us skip the middle one.

title: A Quick Prayer
verse: Then the king said to me, “What is your request?” So I prayed to the God of heaven.
meaning: Nehemiah served the king of Persia and was grieving for ruined Jerusalem. When the king asked what he wanted, Nehemiah prayed silently to God before answering. Then he boldly asked to go rebuild the city. The king also gave Nehemiah letters, timber and an armed escort for the trip.
heart: Prayer does not always need closed eyes and a long time. Sometimes it is a two-second prayer before a hard answer. Quick prayers grow from a steady habit. The more you talk to God in quiet, the easier it is under pressure. Today, before your next big conversation, pray silently first, then speak.
holdOn: A two-second prayer before I speak can change everything.
prayer: God, teach me to pray in the moment, not just in quiet times. Before I answer hard questions, remind me to turn to you. Give me boldness and wisdom. When I panic, let my first thought be a prayer to you, not a fear. Amen.
teaser: The king asked Nehemiah a question. He prayed before answering, in two seconds.

title: A Mind to Work
verse: So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
meaning: Nehemiah led the people to rebuild Jerusalem's walls while enemies mocked them. They kept going, and the wall reached half its height. The reason was simple: the people had a mind to work. Half of the men worked while the other half stood guard. Builders kept a sword at their side as they worked.
heart: Big goals get done by people who keep showing up. Mockers will talk. Let them. What wall are you building: a skill, a degree, your health? Progress is often boring. Half a wall is still more than a plan that never started. Put in an honest hour of work on it today.
holdOn: Mockers talk. Workers build. I choose to build.
prayer: Lord, give me a mind to work. When people mock what I am trying to build, keep me steady. Help me show up today and do honest work for you. When I get discouraged halfway through, give me the strength to finish what you gave me to do. Amen.
teaser: Enemies mocked the builders. The wall went up anyway. Here is why.

title: Joy Is Strength
verse: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
meaning: When the people heard God's law read, they wept over their failures. Nehemiah told them to stop grieving and celebrate with food and drink, and share with those who had none. The joy of the LORD was their strength. Then they celebrated the Feast of Booths, living in shelters made of branches for a week. There was very great gladness.
heart: Some men think joy is soft. Nehemiah said it is strength. God's joy is not pretending things are fine. It is gladness in who he is. Once you have confessed, God does not want you stuck in shame. His mercy is reason to celebrate. Do something today that brings joy, and share it with someone.
holdOn: The joy of the LORD is my strength.
prayer: LORD, I carry a lot of guilt and heaviness. Thank you for your mercy. Fill me with your joy, and let it make me strong. Show me someone to share it with today. Teach me to celebrate your goodness with others, and remember the ones who have nothing. Amen.
teaser: The people were crying over their failures. Nehemiah told them to throw a feast.

title: For a Time Like This
verse: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
meaning: Haman plotted to wipe out the Jews. Mordecai urged Esther, now queen, to speak to the king. He said that if she stayed silent, help would come another way. But maybe she was placed there for such a time as this. Esther asked her people to fast for three days. If I perish, I perish, she said, and went to the king.
heart: You are where you are for a reason: your school, team, job or family. Is there something you are staying silent about that you should speak up on? Your place may be your purpose. Speaking up can be a quiet word to a friend, a teacher or a boss. Courage does not need a stage. Speak up this week.
holdOn: Maybe I am here, right now, for such a time as this.
prayer: God, you put me where I am on purpose. Show me why. Give me courage to speak up when it matters, even if it costs me. Use me for such a time as this. When I am afraid of what speaking up will cost, remind me who stands with me. Amen.
teaser: One man's question changed history: what if you are here for a reason?

title: I Will Hold You Up
verse: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
meaning: God spoke through Isaiah to Israel in exile, afraid and far from home. He gave them five promises in one breath. I am with you and I am your God. I will strengthen you, help you and hold you up. The right hand of his righteousness pictures God's strong, faithful grip. He does not let go.
heart: Fear says you are on your own. God says the opposite, five times over. Fear may still knock. You do not have to open the door and let it run your day. Pick the promise you need most today, maybe I will help you, and say it to yourself whenever fear shows up.
holdOn: God is with me, helps me and holds me up with his strong hand.
prayer: God, you know what scares me. Thank you that I am not alone. Strengthen me, help me and hold me up today. When fear speaks, let your promise speak louder. Hold me with your strong right hand on the days when my own grip slips. Amen.
teaser: God gave scared people five promises in one sentence. You need at least one today.

title: Blessed Be His Name
verse: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
meaning: Job lost his wealth and his children in a single day. He tore his robe and fell to the ground. Then he worshiped: I came into the world with nothing and will leave with nothing. Blessed be the LORD's name. Through all this, Job did not sin or blame God. He did not yet know the full story behind his suffering.
heart: Job did not pretend his loss was small. He grieved hard and still worshiped. Faith is not the absence of tears. Loss hurts because what you lost mattered. You do not have to rush your grief to please anyone. If you are carrying a loss, let yourself grieve, and bring it to God honestly.
holdOn: I can grieve deeply and still trust God.
prayer: LORD, you give and you take, and I do not always understand. When I lose what I love, hold me. Let me grieve honestly and still bless your name. Send people who will sit with me, and give me hope that grief will not be the end of the story. Amen.
teaser: Job lost everything in one day. What he did next is hard to believe.

title: Sit With Him
verse: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
meaning: Job's three friends heard about his suffering and came to comfort him. They sat with him on the ground for seven days and nights without saying a word. They saw his pain was too great for speeches. In that culture, sitting on the ground with someone showed you were sharing their sorrow.
heart: When a friend is hurting, you do not need the perfect words. Your presence speaks. Later, Job's friends got it wrong by talking too much. A text, a meal or just being in the room can mean more than advice. This week, sit with someone who is struggling, and mostly listen.
holdOn: Sometimes the best thing I can give a hurting friend is my presence.
prayer: God, make me a friend who shows up. Teach me when to speak and when to stay quiet. Help me sit with people in their pain the way you sit with me. Keep me from rushing to fix people when they need to be heard. Amen.
teaser: Job's friends did the best thing possible for a week. Then they ruined it.

title: Kindness When Faith Is Weak
verse: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
meaning: Job was suffering, and his friends began blaming him. Job told them that a man ready to faint deserves kindness from his friends. That is true even if he is struggling to hold on to God.
heart: When a friend is doubting or walking away from faith, lectures rarely help. Kindness does. Do not wait for him to get it together. Reach out to a struggling friend today with a meal, a text or a ride.
holdOn: A friend who is ready to faint needs kindness, not a lecture.
prayer: God, forgive me for the times I judged a hurting friend. Make me kind to people who are struggling, even with their faith. Let my kindness show them your love. Amen.
teaser: Job's friends gave him advice. Job told them what he actually needed.

title: A Covenant With Your Eyes
verse: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
meaning: Job listed the ways he had tried to live right. One of the first was a promise he made with his own eyes. He would not look at a young woman with lust. He guarded his heart through his eyes.
heart: Lust usually starts with a second look. Job decided in advance where his eyes would not go. Make your own covenant today. Name one thing you will not look at, and set up one guard, like a filter or a friend.
holdOn: I made a promise with my eyes, and God helps me keep it.
prayer: God, you see what I look at when no one else does. Help me make a covenant with my eyes. Clean my mind, forgive my failures, and give me strength to look away. Amen.
teaser: Job made a promise with an unusual part of his body. Every man needs to hear it.

title: My Redeemer Lives
verse: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
meaning: In the middle of his worst pain, with his body sick and his friends against him, Job said something amazing. He knew his Redeemer was alive and would one day stand on the earth. Hope broke through.
heart: Hope is not denying the pain. It is knowing the story is not over. Christians see Job's words come true in Jesus, who rose from the dead. Say these words today, even if you do not feel them yet.
holdOn: Even in my worst pain, I know my Redeemer lives.
prayer: Jesus, my Redeemer, you are alive. When pain makes me doubt, remind me that the story is not over. Give me hope that holds on, like Job's did, all the way through. Amen.
teaser: At his lowest point, Job said five words that still give people hope.

title: Where Were You?
verse: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
meaning: After Job demanded answers, God finally spoke from a storm. He did not explain Job's suffering. Instead he asked: where were you when I laid the earth's foundations? Job saw how small his view was.
heart: It is fine to ask God hard questions. But some answers are bigger than our minds. Spend a few minutes outside today. Look at the sky or the sea, and let God remind you that he knows what he is doing.
holdOn: God sees far more than I do. I can trust what I cannot understand.
prayer: God, I have questions you have not answered. You laid the foundations of the earth, and I see so little. Humble me, and help me trust you where I cannot understand. Amen.
teaser: Job asked God why. God answered with a different question.

title: Deep Roots
verse: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.
meaning: The first psalm describes a man who loves God's word. He is like a tree planted by streams of water. He bears fruit in season and does not wither, because his roots go deep.
heart: Trees do not grow strong in a day, and neither do men. Your roots are fed by what you take in daily. Plant yourself near the water. Read a bit of God's word every morning this week, before your phone.
holdOn: My roots grow deep when I stay close to God's word.
prayer: God, plant me by your streams of water. Help me take in your word every day. Let me grow strong, bear fruit and not dry up when life gets hot. Amen.
teaser: The very first psalm compares a strong man to a tree. Here is the secret.

title: The One Who Lifts My Head
verse: But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
meaning: David wrote this while running from his own son, Absalom, who had stolen his throne. People said God would not help him. David answered that God was his shield and the one who lifts his head.
heart: Shame makes men look at the ground. God lifts heads. If you are carrying shame today, you do not have to stay there. Tell God what happened, and let him lift your eyes again.
holdOn: God is my shield, and he lifts my head when shame pulls it down.
prayer: LORD, you are my shield. When I am ashamed and people say you will not help, lift my head. Remind me who I am in you, and let me stand again. Amen.
teaser: David was running from his own son. He still wrote about lifted heads.

title: Sleep in Peace
verse: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety.
meaning: David had enemies and many worries, but he wrote that he could lie down and sleep in peace. His safety did not depend on solving every problem first. It depended on the LORD keeping him.
heart: A racing mind at night is common, especially with a phone in your hand. Tonight, put your phone away early. Give God your worries one by one, and lie down knowing he stays awake for you.
holdOn: I can sleep in peace because God keeps watch over me.
prayer: LORD, my mind races at night. I give you my worries. Keep me safe and help me sleep in peace. Thank you that you never sleep and always watch over me. Amen.
teaser: David had enemies everywhere. He still slept well. Here is how.

title: In the Morning
verse: LORD, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
meaning: David made a habit of praying in the morning. He laid his requests before God, then waited and watched for God's answer. The day started with God, not with the noise.
heart: Whatever you look at first shapes your day. Before you check messages tomorrow, give God the first two minutes. Tell him what you need, then watch for him through the day.
holdOn: I give God the first minutes of my day and watch for his answer.
prayer: LORD, in the morning you hear my voice. Help me start my days with you, not with my phone. Here are my needs today. I will watch for you. Amen.
teaser: David had a morning routine. It took two minutes and changed his whole day.

title: A High Tower
verse: The LORD will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.
meaning: In ancient cities, a high tower was the safest place in an attack. David says God is a high tower for the oppressed and a safe place in times of trouble. No enemy can reach that high.
heart: When you feel attacked, by people, stress or your own thoughts, you need somewhere safe to run. Run to God first. Today, when trouble hits, stop and pray before you react.
holdOn: When trouble comes, God is my high tower.
prayer: LORD, you are my high tower. When I feel attacked and pushed around, let me run to you first. Keep me safe, and give me strength to face the trouble. Amen.
teaser: Ancient cities had one place nobody could reach. David said God is like that.

title: How Long?
verse: How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
meaning: David felt forgotten by God and asked four times how long it would last. This is in the Bible on purpose. God lets his people be honest about feeling abandoned. By the end, David chooses to trust again.
heart: You do not have to fake being fine with God. Telling him you feel forgotten is still prayer. If God feels far right now, tell him exactly that, in your own words. Then keep talking to him.
holdOn: I can be honest with God when he feels far away.
prayer: God, sometimes I feel forgotten by you. I will be honest: it hurts. But I will keep talking to you. Show me your face again, and help me trust you while I wait. Amen.
teaser: David asked God the same question four times. It is in the Bible on purpose.

title: Pleasant Places
verse: The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
meaning: In Israel, each family got a plot of land marked with boundary lines. David says his lines have fallen in pleasant places. He is content with the life God gave him, because God himself is his inheritance.
heart: Comparing your life to other men's feeds online makes everything look worse. Look at the lines of your own life. Write down three good things God has given you today, and thank him for them.
holdOn: My life has good boundaries because God himself is my inheritance.
prayer: LORD, forgive me for comparing my life to others. Thank you for the good things you have given me. Help me be content, because you are my best inheritance. Amen.
teaser: Scrolling makes your life look small. David saw his own life differently.

title: Unshaken
verse: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
meaning: David says he keeps the LORD always in front of him. Because God is at his right hand, he will not be shaken. Where you set your eyes decides how steady you are.
heart: If your mind is fixed on fear, money or other people's opinions, you will shake. Set God in front of you today. Put a verse as your lock screen, and let it remind you who is at your right hand.
holdOn: With God in front of me and beside me, I will not be shaken.
prayer: LORD, I want to set you always before me. When I am distracted and afraid, pull my eyes back to you. Stand at my right hand, and keep me steady. Amen.
teaser: David had a trick for staying steady. It was about where he looked.

title: Because He Delights in Me
verse: He brought me out also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
meaning: David sang this after God rescued him from Saul. God brought him out into a wide open place. Why? Not because David was perfect, but because God delighted in him. God's rescue came from love.
heart: Many young men feel they must earn love by performing. God does not save you because you are impressive. He saves you because he delights in you. Let that truth sink in for one minute today.
holdOn: God rescues me because he delights in me, not because I earned it.
prayer: God, it is hard to believe you delight in me. I am used to earning love. Help me rest in your love today, and bring me into a wide open place. Amen.
teaser: God rescued David for a reason that might surprise you.

title: The Sky Talks
verse: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.
meaning: David looked up and saw that the heavens declare God's glory. The sky works like a message, day after day, without words. Everyone on earth, in every language, can see this message.
heart: Get outside today, even for five minutes. Look at the sky, the clouds or the stars tonight. Let creation remind you that a great God made all of it, and he knows you by name.
holdOn: The sky tells the story of a great and creative God.
prayer: God, the sky shows how great and creative you are. Help me notice your work today instead of rushing past it. Fill me with awe, and remind me you know my name. Amen.
teaser: The sky has been preaching for thousands of years. Most of us forget to look up.

title: Words and Thoughts
verse: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, LORD, my rock, and my redeemer.
meaning: After praising God's creation and his law, David ends with a prayer. He asks that both his words and his inner thoughts would please God, his rock and redeemer. He wanted to be clean inside and out.
heart: What you say flows from what you think about all day. Guard both. Before you post, text or speak in anger today, pray this verse. Ask if your words would please God.
holdOn: I want my words and my thoughts to please God.
prayer: LORD, my rock and my redeemer, let my words and the thoughts of my heart please you today. Clean up my language and my mind. Guard what I say and post. Amen.
teaser: David prayed about two things most men never think to guard at the same time.

title: Nothing Missing
verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
meaning: David was a shepherd before he was a king. He knew sheep depend on their shepherd for everything. So he wrote that with the LORD as his shepherd, he would lack nothing he truly needed.
heart: We are always told we need more: more stuff, more status, more followers. With God as your shepherd, you already have what you need most. Name one need today and trust him with it.
holdOn: The LORD is my shepherd. I have what I truly need.
prayer: LORD, you are my shepherd. When I feel like I am missing something, remind me that I have you. Provide what I truly need today, and help me trust you. Amen.
teaser: A shepherd who became king wrote the most famous line of the Psalms. Here it is.

title: Green Pastures
verse: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
meaning: Sheep will not lie down when they are afraid or hungry. A good shepherd makes them lie down in green pastures and leads them to calm water. God leads his people into real rest.
heart: You may be running nonstop and calling it strength. Sometimes God has to make you lie down. Do not fight the rest he offers. Take a real break today, and let him lead you to calm water.
holdOn: God knows when I need to lie down, and he leads me to rest.
prayer: Shepherd, I keep running. Make me lie down when I need it. Lead me beside still water today, and calm the fear and hunger that keep me so restless. Amen.
teaser: Sheep will not lie down unless two things are true. People are the same.

title: He Restores
verse: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
meaning: David says the shepherd restores his soul. When he is worn down, God brings him back to life. Then God guides him on right paths, not for David's glory, but for God's own name.
heart: Some of your tiredness is deeper than sleep can fix. It is soul tiredness. God can restore what is drained. Ask him today to restore you, and then follow him on the right path he shows you.
holdOn: God restores my soul and guides me on the right path.
prayer: Shepherd, my soul is tired. Restore me. Bring back what life has drained. Guide me on paths that are right, and let my whole life point to your name. Amen.
teaser: There is a kind of tired that sleep cannot fix. David knew the cure.

title: Through the Valley
verse: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
meaning: David knew dark valleys where death felt close. He did not say God would keep him out of them. He said he would not fear evil there, because God would be with him, guarding him.
heart: Faith does not skip the valley. It walks through it with God. If you are in a dark season, keep walking. Tell a trusted friend what you are going through, and remember God walks with you.
holdOn: Even in the darkest valley, I do not walk alone.
prayer: God, I am afraid of the valleys in my life. Walk with me through them, step by step. Comfort me with your rod and your staff, and keep me moving forward. Amen.
teaser: David did not say God would keep him out of the valley. He said something better.

title: A Table With Enemies Watching
verse: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
meaning: The picture changes from shepherd to host. God sets a table for David while his enemies watch. He welcomes David with oil, the way an honored guest was treated, and fills his cup to overflowing.
heart: People may doubt you, mock you or be against you. God's welcome is louder. You do not need revenge to be honored. Today, let God's welcome be enough, and stay calm around the people against you.
holdOn: God honors me at his table, even with my enemies watching.
prayer: God, thank you for welcoming me like an honored guest. When people are against me, help me rest in your welcome instead of chasing revenge. Fill my cup again. Amen.
teaser: Psalm 23 has a surprise in it: a dinner party with enemies in the room.

title: Goodness Chasing You
verse: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the LORD’s house forever.
meaning: David ends the psalm with confidence. Goodness and loving kindness will follow him all his life. The word for follow means to pursue. God's love chases him down, and he will live with God forever.
heart: Your past mistakes may feel like they chase you. David says God's goodness chases you harder. Look back over this week. Where did God's goodness catch up with you? Thank him for it.
holdOn: God's goodness and love are chasing me every day of my life.
prayer: LORD, thank you that your goodness chases me every day. When my mistakes feel close behind, remind me that your love is faster. Bring me home to you forever. Amen.
teaser: Something is following you every day of your life. David says it is good news.

title: Teach Me Your Paths
verse: Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths.
meaning: David asks God to show him his ways and teach him his paths. It is a humble prayer. David was a king and a warrior, and he still wanted God to teach him how to live.
heart: No man is too old or too strong to need teaching. What area of life are you guessing in right now: money, relationships, career? Ask God to teach you there, and look for an older man who can help.
holdOn: I am never too strong to need God to teach me.
prayer: LORD, show me your ways. Teach me your paths. I do not want to guess my way through life. Give me teachable eyes and wise people to learn from. Amen.
teaser: A king and warrior asked God for help most men would be too proud to ask for.

title: Guidance for the Humble
verse: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.
meaning: David says God guides the humble in what is right and teaches them his way. Proud people think they already know. Humble people are teachable, and God gives his guidance to people who are willing to learn.
heart: Pride says you have it figured out. Humility says you are still learning. The humble man grows faster. Today, admit you were wrong about something small, and see how much lighter you feel.
holdOn: God teaches people who know they still need to learn.
prayer: God, I want to be teachable. Strip away the pride that thinks I know it all. Guide me in what is right, and teach me your way, starting today. Amen.
teaser: God teaches one kind of person more than any other. It is not the smartest.

title: Whom Shall I Fear?
verse: The LORD is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
meaning: David calls God his light, his salvation and the strength of his life. Then he asks two bold questions: whom shall I fear, and of whom shall I be afraid? With God, fear loses its grip.
heart: Write down your biggest fear today. Then put it next to these words: the LORD is my light and strength. Fear is real, but it is not in charge. Face one small fear today with God beside you.
holdOn: The LORD is my light and strength. Fear is not in charge.
prayer: LORD, you are my light, my salvation and my strength. You know what I fear. Shrink it in your light. Give me courage to face one fear today with you. Amen.
teaser: David asked two questions that make fear smaller. Try asking them today.

title: One Thing
verse: One thing I have asked of the LORD, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in the LORD’s house all the days of my life, to see the LORD’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
meaning: David could have asked for many things. He asked for one: to be close to God all his life, to see God's beauty and to learn from him. Everything else came second to that.
heart: Most of us chase ten things at once and feel empty. What is your one thing? Before you go after your goals today, spend a few minutes just being with God, not asking for anything.
holdOn: Of all I want, being close to God is the one thing.
prayer: LORD, I chase so many things. Make you my one thing. Let me see your beauty and want you more than success, comfort or approval. Draw me close today. Amen.
teaser: If you could ask God for only one thing, what would it be? David knew.

title: Be Strong and Wait
verse: Wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for the LORD.
meaning: David ends the psalm with a command to himself and to us: wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Waiting is not weakness. It takes courage to trust God's timing.
heart: We hate waiting: for results, a job, answers, healing. Waiting on God is active trust, not giving up. Whatever you are waiting for, keep doing the right thing today and let your heart be strong.
holdOn: Waiting on God is not weakness. It takes strength and courage.
prayer: LORD, I am tired of waiting. Give my heart courage. Help me keep doing what is right while I wait for you, and trust that your timing is good. Amen.
teaser: Waiting feels weak. David said it takes more courage than acting.

title: Strength and Shield
verse: The LORD is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him.
meaning: David says the LORD is his strength and shield. He trusted God, and God helped him. The result was joy so big it turned into a song. Trust led to help, and help led to praise.
heart: Notice the order: trust, help, joy. Many men want joy without trust. Trust God with one real problem today. When he helps, do not forget to thank him out loud.
holdOn: God is my strength and shield. I trust him, and he helps me.
prayer: LORD, you are my strength and my shield. I trust you with what I am facing today. Help me, and when you do, let my heart sing with thanks. Amen.
teaser: David went from trust to help to song. Most men try to skip the first step.

title: Strength and Peace
verse: The LORD will give strength to his people. The LORD will bless his people with peace.
meaning: Psalm 29 describes God's voice in a huge storm, shaking forests and deserts. It ends with a quiet promise. The same God who rules the storm gives strength to his people and blesses them with peace.
heart: God is powerful enough to rule the storm and gentle enough to give you peace. You need both strength and peace this week. Ask him for both today, and take a slow breath before your next hard moment.
holdOn: The God who rules the storm gives me strength and peace.
prayer: LORD, your voice rules over every storm. Give me strength for what I face and peace in the middle of it. Bless me today with the calm only you can give. Amen.
teaser: A psalm about a violent storm ends with a surprisingly gentle promise.

title: Joy Comes in the Morning
verse: For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
meaning: David wrote this after God brought him back from a terrible time. He learned that God's anger lasts a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime. Crying may last through the night, but joy comes with the morning.
heart: Night seasons feel like they will never end. They do. If you are in one now, you do not have to feel happy. Just hold on until morning. Tell God how dark it is, and ask him for one sign of light.
holdOn: Crying may last for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
prayer: God, some nights feel endless. Help me hold on until morning. Thank you that your favor lasts longer than any dark season. Bring joy back to me in your time. Amen.
teaser: David learned something about long nights that he never forgot.

title: Into Your Hands
verse: Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, LORD, God of truth.
meaning: David trusted God with his very life when enemies set traps for him. He prayed, into your hand I commit my spirit. Jesus spoke these same words from the cross as he died, trusting his Father completely.
heart: Trust is handing over what you cannot control. You cannot control every outcome, but you can put your life in God's hands. Tonight, before you sleep, pray this verse and let go of today.
holdOn: I put my life into God's hands. He is faithful.
prayer: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit. I give you what I cannot control. Hold my life, my future and my fears. Thank you for being faithful and true. Amen.
teaser: David prayed these words in danger. Jesus prayed them on the cross.

title: My Times Are in Your Hand
verse: My times are in your hand. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from those who persecute me.
meaning: David was surrounded by people plotting against him. He did not know how long the danger would last. Still he said: my times are in your hand. His whole timeline belonged to God, not to his enemies.
heart: You may feel behind: in school, in your career, in life. Your timeline is not set by other people or your feed. It is in God's hand. Let go of one deadline you have set yourself today.
holdOn: My times are in God's hand, not in the hands of my fears.
prayer: God, my times are in your hand. When I feel behind or rushed, calm me. Free me from comparing my life to others, and help me trust your timing. Amen.
teaser: David's enemies wanted to decide his future. David knew who really held it.

title: Come Clean
verse: I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
meaning: David hid his sin for a while, and it ate him up inside. Then he confessed it to God without hiding anything. God forgave him. The relief David felt is all over this psalm.
heart: Hidden sin gets heavier the longer you carry it. God already knows, and he is ready to forgive. Name one thing you have been hiding. Confess it to God today, and if needed, to a trusted friend.
holdOn: When I stop hiding my sin, God forgives and the weight lifts.
prayer: God, you know what I have been hiding. I confess it now without excuses. Thank you that you forgive completely. Lift this weight, and help me walk in the light. Amen.
teaser: David hid his sin for a while. It nearly crushed him. Then he did one thing.

title: I Will Guide You
verse: I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.
meaning: After David confessed, God answered with a promise. He would teach David the way to go and guide him with his eye on him. Forgiveness was the start of a closer walk with God.
heart: God does not just forgive you and leave you. He wants to guide you. Keep your eyes on him like a player watching his coach. Ask him today for guidance in one decision.
holdOn: God teaches me the way to go and keeps his eye on me.
prayer: God, thank you for forgiving me and not leaving me. Teach me the way I should go. Keep your eye on me, and help me stay close enough to follow. Amen.
teaser: God made a promise right after forgiving David. It was about what comes next.

title: Help and Shield
verse: Our soul has waited for the LORD. He is our help and our shield.
meaning: This psalm praises God as Creator and Lord over nations. It ends with the people saying they wait for the LORD. He is their help and their shield. Their hope was in him, not in armies.
heart: What do you rely on for safety: money, muscle, your phone, your plans? None of these are bad, but none can save you. Today, say out loud: God is my help and my shield.
holdOn: God is my help and my shield. My hope is in him.
prayer: LORD, I wait for you today. You are my help and my shield. When I trust in my own strength, remind me that real safety comes from you alone. Amen.
teaser: Armies and money promise safety. This psalm points somewhere else.

title: Free From Fear
verse: I sought the LORD, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
meaning: David wrote this after escaping danger by pretending to be insane in front of a foreign king. He was afraid for his life. He sought the LORD, God answered him, and set him free from all his fears.
heart: Fear can drive you into strange choices, like it did David. The better move is to seek God first. Name the fear that is loudest in your head right now, and bring it straight to God.
holdOn: I sought the LORD, and he set me free from my fears.
prayer: LORD, I am seeking you. You know the fears that run my mind. Answer me, and set me free from them. Teach me to run to you before I panic. Amen.
teaser: David once acted insane to escape danger. Then he wrote this calm verse.

title: Taste and See
verse: Oh taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
meaning: David invites people to taste and see that the LORD is good. You cannot know a meal is good by reading about it. You have to taste it. Faith grows by trying God for yourself.
heart: You may know a lot about God without ever trusting him for real. Taste and see. Take one step of trust today: pray about something real, give something away, or forgive someone. Watch what God does.
holdOn: I want to taste God's goodness for myself, not just hear about it.
prayer: LORD, I do not want secondhand faith. Let me taste and see that you are good. Show me your goodness today as I trust you with something real and hard. Amen.
teaser: You cannot know food is good by reading the menu. Faith is the same.

title: Near the Brokenhearted
verse: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
meaning: David says the LORD is close to people with broken hearts and rescues those whose spirits are crushed. God does not keep his distance from pain. He moves toward it.
heart: Breakups, family fights, failures and losses can crush a man, even if he never shows it. God is near you in it. If your spirit feels crushed, tell God, and tell one person you trust this week.
holdOn: When my heart is broken, God moves closer, not further away.
prayer: LORD, you are near the brokenhearted. Be near me. You know what crushed me, even if I hide it from others. Save me, heal me and help me let people in. Amen.
teaser: Most people step back from someone who is hurting. God does the opposite.

title: Trust and Do Good
verse: Trust in the LORD, and do good. Dwell in the land, and enjoy safe pasture.
meaning: David saw wicked men getting ahead and good men struggling. His advice was simple: trust the LORD and keep doing good. Stay where God has put you, and enjoy his safety there.
heart: When cheaters seem to win, it is tempting to cut corners too. Do not. Trust God and keep doing good where you are. Do one honest, good thing today that nobody will reward you for.
holdOn: When others cut corners, I will trust God and keep doing good.
prayer: LORD, it frustrates me when cheaters seem to win. Help me trust you and keep doing good anyway. Make me faithful where you have put me, and give me your peace. Amen.
teaser: Cheaters seemed to be winning. David's advice was almost too simple.

title: Commit Your Way
verse: Commit your way to the LORD. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
meaning: The word commit here means to roll something onto someone else. David says to roll your whole way onto the LORD and trust him. Then God will act. You do your part, and he handles what you cannot.
heart: Some plans weigh on you like a heavy rock. Roll them onto God. That does not mean you stop working. It means you stop carrying it all in your head. Commit one plan to God today, by name.
holdOn: I roll my plans onto God and trust him to act.
prayer: LORD, I commit my way to you. I roll my plans, my future and my worries onto you. Help me trust you and do my part, while you handle what I cannot. Amen.
teaser: One word in this verse paints a picture: rolling a heavy weight onto God.

title: Do Not Fret
verse: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
meaning: David tells us to rest in the LORD and wait patiently. Do not fret when wicked people succeed with their schemes. Their success will not last. God sees, and he will judge fairly.
heart: Envy and anger grow when you watch other men get ahead the wrong way. Fretting changes nothing but your peace. Today, when you feel that envy rise, stop and say: God sees, and I will rest in him.
holdOn: I will not fret over other men's wrong success. God sees.
prayer: God, I fret when I see dishonest people getting ahead. Calm my heart. Help me rest in you and wait patiently, trusting that you see everything and judge fairly. Amen.
teaser: Watching bad men win makes you angry. David gave a better response.

title: Steps Directed
verse: A man’s steps are established by the LORD. He delights in his way.
meaning: David says the LORD makes firm the steps of the man who pleases him. God delights in his way. Even when he stumbles, he will not fall flat, because the LORD holds his hand.
heart: You do not have to see the whole road to take the next step. God directs steps, not just destinations. Take one step today that you know is right, and trust God to hold your hand on the next one.
holdOn: God makes my steps firm and holds my hand when I stumble.
prayer: LORD, establish my steps. I cannot see the whole road, but I trust you with the next step. When I stumble, hold my hand and keep me from falling. Amen.
teaser: God directs something smaller than your destination. It matters more than you think.

title: He Heard My Cry
verse: I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
meaning: David waited patiently for the LORD. It was not quick. But God turned to him and heard his cry. Later in the psalm, God lifts him out of a muddy pit and sets his feet on a rock.
heart: Some prayers are answered slowly. That does not mean God is not listening. Keep crying out. If you are stuck in a pit right now, keep praying, and reach for one person who can help you climb.
holdOn: God hears my cry, even when the answer comes slowly.
prayer: LORD, I have been waiting a long time. Turn to me and hear my cry. Lift me out of the pit I am stuck in, and set my feet on solid rock. Amen.
teaser: David waited a long time for an answer. Then God did something physical.

title: A New Song
verse: He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God. Many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD.
meaning: After God rescued him, David said God put a new song in his mouth. His praise became a story others could see. Many people who saw what God did would come to trust the LORD too.
heart: Your story of what God has done can help someone else trust him. You do not need a stage. Share one way God helped you with a friend this week. Your new song might be what he needs.
holdOn: What God has done for me can help others trust him too.
prayer: God, thank you for the new song you have given me. Help me share it humbly and honestly. Use my story to help someone else trust you this week. Amen.
teaser: God gave David a new song. It was meant to be heard by others.

title: Talk to Your Soul
verse: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
meaning: The writer is depressed and far from home. Instead of only listening to his feelings, he talks back to his own soul: why are you so down? Hope in God. I will still praise him.
heart: Feelings are real, but they do not get the final word. Talk back to your own soul with truth. If you have been low for a long time, also talk to a doctor or counselor. That is not weakness.
holdOn: I can talk back to my soul and tell it to hope in God.
prayer: God, my soul feels low. I will not pretend otherwise. Help me speak truth to myself and hope in you. Send the help I need, and let me praise you again. Amen.
teaser: This writer did something most of us never do: he talked back to his own soul.

title: Be Still
verse: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted on the earth.”
meaning: This psalm describes nations raging and the earth shaking. In the middle of it, God speaks: be still, and know that I am God. Stop fighting and striving. God will be honored over all the earth.
heart: Being still is hard for active men. But it is how you remember who is really God. Today, take two minutes of complete stillness. No phone, no noise. Just breathe and remember he is God.
holdOn: Be still, and know that he is God, not me.
prayer: God, I am always moving and striving. Help me be still. Remind me that you are God and I am not. Take the weight of running the world off my shoulders. Amen.
teaser: Nations rage and the earth shakes. Then God gives a two-word command.

title: A Clean Heart
verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
meaning: David wrote this after his sin with Bathsheba and the murder of her husband. He did not make excuses. He asked God to create a clean heart in him. He needed a new start from the inside.
heart: You cannot scrub your own heart clean, no matter how hard you try. Only God can create a clean heart. If you are carrying guilt today, pray David's prayer word for word, and mean it.
holdOn: Only God can create a clean heart in me. I ask him to.
prayer: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me. I cannot fix myself. Wash me, forgive me, and give me a fresh start from the inside out. Amen.
teaser: After the worst failure of his life, David prayed one of the boldest prayers ever.

title: Throw It on Him
verse: Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
meaning: David was betrayed by a close friend. In his pain, he wrote: cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you. God would keep the righteous from being shaken for good.
heart: Some burdens are too heavy to carry and too painful to talk about. Throw them on God. Name the heaviest thing you are carrying today, and hand it to him in prayer, again and again if needed.
holdOn: I can throw my burden on God, and he will hold me up.
prayer: LORD, I cast my burden on you. You know what is weighing me down, even the betrayal I do not talk about. Hold me up. Keep me from being shaken. Amen.
teaser: A close friend betrayed David. His response is one you can use today.

title: When I Am Afraid
verse: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
meaning: David was captured by enemies in a foreign city. He did not pretend he was fearless. He said: when I am afraid, I will trust in you. Fear came, and he answered it with trust.
heart: Courage does not mean you never feel fear. It means you decide what to do with it. Next time fear hits today, say this verse out loud: when I am afraid, I will trust in you.
holdOn: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in God.
prayer: God, I will not pretend I am never afraid. When fear comes today, I will trust in you. Be stronger than my fear, and help me act with courage. Amen.
teaser: David did not say he was never afraid. He said something more useful.

title: In the Shadow of His Wings
verse: Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.
meaning: David hid in a cave while King Saul hunted him. He prayed for mercy and pictured himself under God's wings, like a young bird sheltered by its parent. He would stay there until the danger passed.
heart: Strong men still need shelter. There is no shame in running to God when life gets dangerous. If a storm is hitting you right now, pray this verse and stay close to God until it passes.
holdOn: I take shelter under God's wings until the storm passes.
prayer: God, be merciful to me. I run to you for shelter. Hide me in the shadow of your wings until this trouble passes, and give me strength to wait. Amen.
teaser: David was hiding in a cave from a king. He pictured something surprisingly tender.

title: The Rock Higher Than I
verse: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
meaning: David cried to God from the ends of the earth when his heart was overwhelmed. He asked God to lead him to the rock that is higher than he was. He needed a strength beyond his own.
heart: When you are overwhelmed, your own strength is the problem, not the answer. You need a rock higher than you. Today, when it all feels like too much, pray this verse and ask God to lift you up.
holdOn: When I am overwhelmed, God leads me to a rock higher than me.
prayer: God, my heart is overwhelmed. I cannot climb out on my own. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I am. Lift me up and steady me. Amen.
teaser: When David felt overwhelmed, he asked to be taken somewhere specific.

title: Wait in Silence
verse: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
meaning: David tells his own soul to wait in silence for God alone. His hope does not come from people, money or schemes. It comes from God. Quiet trust is where his strength comes from.
heart: Silence can feel uncomfortable, so we fill it with noise. Try something different. Sit in silence for five minutes today. Tell your soul to wait for God alone, and let the noise settle.
holdOn: My soul waits in silence, because my hope comes from God.
prayer: God, my mind is noisy and my hopes are scattered. Teach my soul to wait for you alone. Quiet me, and let my hope rest in you, not in people. Amen.
teaser: David gave his own soul an order. It is one most of us avoid.

title: Pour It Out
verse: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
meaning: David tells everyone to trust God at all times and to pour out their hearts before him. God is a refuge. Pouring out means emptying everything, not just the polite parts.
heart: Many men bottle it all up until it explodes. God invites you to pour it out instead. Find a private place today and tell God everything on your heart, the anger, fear and hope.
holdOn: I can pour out my whole heart to God. He is safe.
prayer: God, I have bottled up a lot. I pour out my heart to you now: the anger, the fear, the hurt and the hope. You are my refuge. Thank you for listening. Amen.
teaser: Most men bottle it up. David told people to do the opposite.

title: Thirsty for God
verse: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
meaning: David wrote this in the desert of Judah, far from home. He compares his longing for God to a man dying of thirst in dry land. He wanted God more than water.
heart: We try to fill our thirst with games, scrolling, food or approval. They do not satisfy. Notice what you reach for when you feel empty today. Then reach for God first, even for a minute.
holdOn: My soul is thirsty, and only God can satisfy it.
prayer: God, you are my God. I am thirsty in a dry land. I keep trying to fill myself with things that do not last. Satisfy me with yourself today. Amen.
teaser: David wrote this in a desert. He was thirsty for something more than water.

title: God Waters the Earth
verse: You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water. You provide them grain, for so you have ordained it.
meaning: This psalm praises God for caring for the land. He sends rain, fills the rivers and makes the crops grow. Every harvest is a gift from a generous God who keeps providing.
heart: Food on your table started with rain God sent. It is easy to take daily provision for granted. Before your next meal today, stop and thank God for it, even if you are eating alone.
holdOn: Every good thing I eat started as a gift from God.
prayer: God, you water the earth and provide food. Thank you for every meal I have, even the simple ones. Help me never take your care for granted, and help me share. Amen.
teaser: Your lunch started with something only God can do.

title: Father to the Fatherless
verse: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
meaning: David describes God as a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows. The God of heaven cares most for people who have lost their protection. Where a father is missing, God steps in.
heart: Maybe your dad was absent, harsh or gone too soon. That wound is real. God offers to be the father you needed. Talk to him today as Father, and ask him to heal what was missing.
holdOn: Where my father was missing, God offers to be my Father.
prayer: Father, you know the wound my dad left, or the space he could not fill. Be a father to me. Heal what is missing, and teach me how to be a good man. Amen.
teaser: Many men grow up with a missing father. God makes them a promise.

title: Hope Since My Youth
verse: For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
meaning: An older man wrote this psalm looking back on his life. He says God has been his hope and his confidence since he was young. Faith that starts early carries a man through the years.
heart: What you build into your life now will carry you later. Faith built in your youth becomes strength in old age. Make one choice today that your older self will thank you for.
holdOn: God can be my hope and confidence from my youth.
prayer: Lord GOD, be my hope and my confidence now, while I am young. Build faith in me that lasts my whole life. Help me make choices today that I will be glad of later. Amen.
teaser: An old man looked back on his life and named what carried him since his youth.

title: When Body and Heart Fail
verse: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
meaning: Asaph almost gave up on faith when he saw wicked people doing well. Then he went into God's house and saw the bigger picture. He wrote that even when his body and heart fail, God is his strength forever.
heart: Your body will not always cooperate, and your heart will not always feel strong. God is a strength that does not depend on your feelings. On a weak day this week, say this verse and lean on him.
holdOn: When my body and heart fail, God is my strength forever.
prayer: God, my body and my heart get tired and weak. Be the strength of my heart. Be my portion when nothing else satisfies. Hold me up today and forever. Amen.
teaser: Asaph nearly quit on faith. Then he walked into one building and saw clearly.

title: Better Than a Thousand
verse: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
meaning: The writer loved being near God so much that one day in God's house beat a thousand days anywhere else. He would rather stand at the door of God's house than live comfortably with wicked people.
heart: Where you spend your time shows what you value. Is time with God a chore you squeeze in, or something you want? Make room for one unhurried moment with God today, and notice how it feels.
holdOn: One day close to God is better than a thousand anywhere else.
prayer: God, I want to love being near you like this writer did. Change what I value. Make time with you something I want, not something I owe. Draw me close today. Amen.
teaser: This writer said one day was worth a thousand. Here is the day he meant.

title: An Undivided Heart
verse: Teach me your way, LORD. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
meaning: David asked God to teach him his way so he could walk in the truth. Then he asked for an undivided heart. He knew his heart was pulled in many directions and needed to be made whole.
heart: A divided heart wants God and wants sin at the same time. It wears you out. Name one thing that splits your heart today. Ask God to unite your heart, and take one step away from that thing.
holdOn: I want a heart that is not pulled in two directions.
prayer: LORD, teach me your way. My heart is split, wanting you and wanting other things. Make my heart undivided. Help me walk in your truth with my whole self. Amen.
teaser: David asked God to fix a problem every man has: a divided heart.

title: Count Your Days
verse: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
meaning: Moses wrote this psalm about how short human life is compared to God's forever. He asks God to teach us to count our days. When we see that life is short, we grow wise about how to use it.
heart: You probably think you have endless time. You do not. That is not meant to scare you, but to wake you up. Ask yourself today: if this year were my last, what would I start or stop?
holdOn: My days are numbered, so I want to spend them wisely.
prayer: God, teach me to count my days. Wake me up to how short life is. Help me spend my time on what matters, and give me a heart of wisdom. Amen.
teaser: Moses gave a strange piece of advice: count your days. Here is why it makes you wise.

title: The Secret Place
verse: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
meaning: This psalm pictures a man who lives in the secret place of the Most High. He rests in the shadow of the Almighty, like someone safe in a fortress. Closeness to God is his protection.
heart: God is not just a place you visit in emergencies. He invites you to live close to him every day. Find your secret place: a room, a walk, a car ride. Meet God there for a few minutes today.
holdOn: I want to live in God's secret place, not just visit it.
prayer: Most High God, I want to dwell close to you. Be my secret place and my shelter. Help me meet you every day, not only when I am in trouble. Amen.
teaser: This psalm describes a secret place where a man can rest safely. Where is it?

title: Nothing Vile Before My Eyes
verse: I will set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of faithless men. They will not cling to me.
meaning: David made promises about how he would live as king. One was simple: I will set no vile thing before my eyes. He knew what you look at shapes who you become, so he guarded his eyes.
heart: Your screen is in front of your eyes for hours each day. What you watch, scroll and click shapes your heart. Today, unfollow or delete one thing that pulls you toward what is vile.
holdOn: I will not set anything vile before my eyes.
prayer: God, I want clean eyes and a clean heart. Help me guard what I watch and scroll. Give me courage to delete what pulls me down, and replace it with what is good. Amen.
teaser: A king made a promise about his eyes. Your phone makes it harder, and more important.

title: Comfort for Racing Thoughts
verse: In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.
meaning: The writer had many anxious thoughts piling up inside him. In the middle of that noise, God's comfort brought joy to his soul. God did not just remove the problem. He comforted the man in it.
heart: Anxious thoughts can spin late at night. You do not have to win the argument with each one. Bring them to God. Write your worries down tonight, and ask God to comfort you in them.
holdOn: When my thoughts race, God's comfort brings joy to my soul.
prayer: God, my thoughts race and pile up. I cannot calm them on my own. Comfort me in the middle of them, and give my soul your joy and peace. Amen.
teaser: This writer's head was full of worries. Something broke through the noise.

title: Hear His Voice Today
verse: for he is our God. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice!
meaning: The psalm reminds Israel that God is their shepherd and they are his sheep. Then it pleads: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts like your ancestors did in the desert.
heart: Hard hearts form slowly, one ignored nudge at a time. If God has been nudging you about something, a call, a habit, an apology, do not put it off. Act on it today.
holdOn: If I hear God's voice today, I will not harden my heart.
prayer: God, you are my shepherd. Soften my heart. When you nudge me today, help me listen and obey instead of putting it off. Keep my heart from going hard. Amen.
teaser: The psalm says one word twice: today. Hearts harden when we wait.

title: We Are His
verse: Know that the LORD, he is God. It is he who has made us, and we are his. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
meaning: This psalm calls people to know that the LORD is God. He made us, and we belong to him. We are his people and the sheep he cares for. Our identity starts with whose we are.
heart: Many men try to make themselves: through money, fame or their body. You did not make yourself. You belong to God. Let that take pressure off you today. You do not have to build your worth from nothing.
holdOn: I did not make myself. I belong to God, and that is enough.
prayer: LORD, you made me, and I am yours. Free me from trying to build my worth from nothing. Help me rest in belonging to you, and live like your son. Amen.
teaser: Many men try to make themselves. This psalm says something freeing.

title: Like a Father
verse: Like a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
meaning: David says the LORD has compassion on those who fear him, like a good father has compassion on his children. God is not a cold judge waiting to punish. He is a Father who cares.
heart: If your picture of God is shaped by a harsh dad, it may be twisted. God is the Father who is gentle with you when you fail. Today, picture God looking at you with compassion, not disgust.
holdOn: God looks at me like a good father looks at his son.
prayer: Father, thank you for your compassion. Heal my picture of you where it has been shaped by hurt. Help me believe that you look at me with love, even when I fail. Amen.
teaser: If your dad was harsh, your picture of God might be off. David paints a better one.

title: He Remembers We Are Dust
verse: For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.
meaning: David says God knows how we are made. He remembers we are dust. God does not expect superhuman strength from us. He knows our limits and treats us with patience.
heart: You may be harder on yourself than God is. He knows you are human, with limits. That is not an excuse to quit, but a reason to stop beating yourself up. Be patient with yourself today, like God is.
holdOn: God knows I am made of dust and treats me with patience.
prayer: God, thank you that you know my limits and remember I am dust. Free me from beating myself up. Help me grow with patience, the way you are patient with me. Amen.
teaser: God remembers something about you that you keep forgetting.

title: Filled With Good
verse: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
meaning: This psalm tells stories of people who were lost, hungry, trapped and sick. When they cried to God, he rescued them. He satisfies the longing soul and fills the hungry soul with good things.
heart: Hunger in your soul is not something to be ashamed of. It is meant to drive you to God. Cheap fixes only make it worse. When you feel empty today, cry out to God and ask him to fill you.
holdOn: God satisfies my longing soul and fills me with good.
prayer: God, my soul is hungry for more than this world gives. Do not let me settle for cheap fixes. Satisfy my longing, and fill me with good things from you. Amen.
teaser: This psalm is full of desperate people. They all have one thing in common.

title: Guard Your Heart
verse: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
meaning: A father teaches his son to guard his heart above everything else. The heart here means the center of a person: thoughts, desires and choices. Everything in life flows out from it.
heart: You guard your phone and your wallet. Do you guard your heart? What goes in through your eyes, ears and friends shapes it. Today, choose one thing to keep out and one good thing to let in.
holdOn: Everything in my life flows from my heart, so I guard it.
prayer: God, help me guard my heart. Show me what I am letting in that harms me. Give me discipline to shut it out, and fill my heart with what is good and true. Amen.
teaser: A father gave his son one piece of advice above all others. Here it is.

title: Not Your Own Understanding
verse: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
meaning: A father tells his son to trust the LORD with all his heart, not his own understanding. In all his ways he should acknowledge God. Then God will make his paths straight.
heart: Smart men can be the worst at trusting God because they trust their own minds. Use your brain, but do not worship it. Bring a big decision to God today before you make it alone.
holdOn: I will trust God with my whole heart, not just my own understanding.
prayer: LORD, I lean on my own understanding too much. Teach me to trust you with my whole heart. In every part of my life, I acknowledge you. Make my paths straight. Amen.
teaser: Smart men often struggle with this verse the most. Here is why.

title: Water Others
verse: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
meaning: This proverb says the generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will be refreshed. Generosity is like watering a garden. The one who pours out ends up being watered too.
heart: Selfishness feels like it protects you, but it shrinks you. Generosity grows you. Refresh one person today, on purpose: buy a coffee, lend a hand, or encourage someone who is running dry.
holdOn: When I refresh others, God refreshes me too.
prayer: God, free me from selfishness. Make me generous with my time, money and words. Show me someone to refresh today, and refresh my own tired soul as I give. Amen.
teaser: This proverb promises something to people who give. It is not what you expect.

title: Words That Cut or Heal
verse: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
meaning: Some words are like a sword thrust, cutting deep. The proverb says careless speech wounds people. But the tongue of the wise brings healing. Words have real power to hurt or help.
heart: Banter can cross a line into cutting words without you noticing. Watch your words today, in person and online. Say one healing word to someone, and if you cut someone recently, own it.
holdOn: My words can cut like a sword or bring healing.
prayer: God, forgive me for the times my words cut people. Guard my mouth and my thumbs today. Make my words wise and healing, and help me own it when I hurt someone. Amen.
teaser: Your words are either a sword or a medicine. This proverb explains the difference.

title: Walk With the Wise
verse: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
meaning: This proverb says you become like the people you walk with. Spend time with wise men, and you grow wise. Hang around fools, and you get hurt. Your friends shape your future.
heart: Look at the five guys you spend the most time with. Where are they heading? You will probably end up there too. Spend time this week with someone wiser than you, and ask him a real question.
holdOn: I become like the people I walk with, so I choose them carefully.
prayer: God, give me wise friends. Show me which friendships are pulling me down, and give me courage to change them. Make me someone who helps others grow wise too. Amen.
teaser: Look at your five closest friends. This proverb says you are looking at your future.

title: Slow to Anger
verse: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
meaning: This proverb links patience with wisdom. A man who is slow to anger has great understanding. A man with a quick temper shows he is a fool. Temper reveals what is inside.
heart: A quick temper can destroy friendships, jobs and families in seconds. Being slow to anger is real strength. Next time you feel anger rise today, count to ten and ask God for wisdom before you react.
holdOn: Being slow to anger is a sign of understanding, not weakness.
prayer: God, you know my temper. Slow me down. Give me understanding before I react. Help me control my anger so it does not destroy the people and things I love. Amen.
teaser: A quick temper reveals something about a man. This proverb says what.

title: A Gentle Answer
verse: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
meaning: This proverb gives a simple rule about conflict. A gentle answer turns anger away. A harsh word stirs it up. You cannot always control how others act, but you can choose your reply.
heart: In an argument, the harsh comeback feels powerful, but it pours gas on the fire. A calm answer takes more strength. In your next heated moment, lower your voice and choose a gentle reply.
holdOn: A gentle answer is stronger than a harsh one.
prayer: God, when I am attacked, I want to strike back with words. Give me the strength to answer gently. Use my calm words to cool things down instead of heating them up. Amen.
teaser: In an argument, one move ends it and one makes it worse. Most men pick wrong.

title: Get Advice
verse: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
meaning: This proverb says plans fail without advice, but they succeed with many counselors. No one sees everything alone. Wise people ask others for input before they act on big decisions.
heart: Pride wants to figure it out alone. Wisdom asks. Before your next big decision, whether money, school, work or relationships, ask two or three people you trust what they think.
holdOn: Plans succeed when I ask for advice instead of going alone.
