prayer: God, I do not want to make big decisions alone. Give me humble ears and wise counselors. Help me listen to good advice and follow your direction in it. Amen.
teaser: Plans fail for a common reason. This proverb names it.

title: You Plan, God Directs
verse: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.
meaning: This proverb says a man plans his path in his heart, but the LORD directs his steps. Planning is good. But God is the one who actually guides where your feet land.
heart: Make your plans, and hold them loosely. God may redirect you in ways you do not expect. When a plan falls apart this week, do not panic. Ask God where he is directing your steps instead.
holdOn: I make plans, but God directs my steps.
prayer: LORD, I have plans for my life, and I give them to you. Direct my steps. When things change, help me trust that you are leading me somewhere good. Amen.
teaser: You can plan your path. This proverb says who actually steers your feet.

title: Learn From the Ant
verse: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
meaning: This proverb tells the lazy man to go watch the ant. Ants have no boss telling them what to do, yet they work hard and store food for later. Even small creatures show the value of discipline.
heart: Laziness rarely looks like doing nothing. It looks like scrolling, delaying and making excuses. The ant just gets to work. Pick one task you have been putting off, and do the first ten minutes of it today.
holdOn: I do not need a boss to do my work well.
prayer: God, forgive me for laziness and endless excuses. Make me disciplined like the ant. Help me work hard without being forced, and prepare wisely for what is still ahead. Amen.
teaser: This proverb sends lazy men to learn from a tiny teacher.

title: Born for Hard Times
verse: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
meaning: This proverb says a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for times of trouble. Real friends do not disappear when life gets hard. That is when they show up most.
heart: Anyone can be a friend when things are fun. A brother shows up in the hospital, the breakup and the bad news. Who in your life is going through trouble right now? Show up for him this week.
holdOn: A real brother is born for hard times.
prayer: God, thank you for friends who show up in hard times. Make me that kind of friend. Show me who needs me right now, and help me be there in person. Amen.
teaser: Anyone can be a friend on a good day. This proverb names who you need on a bad one.

title: Listen First
verse: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
meaning: This proverb says answering before you have heard someone out is foolish and shameful. Many arguments happen because people reply to what they think was said, not what was said.
heart: When someone is talking, are you listening or just waiting to reply? Today, in one conversation, listen all the way through. Then ask a question before you give your answer.
holdOn: I will listen all the way before I answer.
prayer: God, teach me to listen. Forgive me for cutting people off and assuming. Slow down my mouth and open my ears, so I understand people before I answer them. Amen.
teaser: Most arguments start with a simple mistake. This proverb calls it foolish.

title: Take Instruction
verse: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
meaning: This proverb says to listen to advice and accept correction so you will be wise later in life. Wisdom is built over time by people who let others teach them.
heart: Correction stings, especially for proud men. But every wise old man was once a young man who listened. Think of someone who has corrected you lately. Ask yourself honestly if he was right.
holdOn: If I accept correction now, I will be wise later.
prayer: God, I do not like being corrected. Humble me. Help me listen to wise people and accept their advice, so I grow into a wise man in the years ahead. Amen.
teaser: Every wise old man has one thing in common from his younger years.

title: Deep Water
verse: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
meaning: This proverb says the purposes in a person's heart are like deep water. A man of understanding knows how to draw them out. People carry more inside than they show.
heart: Many men have deep water inside and no one asks them about it. Be the man who draws it out. Ask a friend a deeper question today than how are you, and really listen.
holdOn: People carry deep water inside. I can help draw it out.
prayer: God, give me understanding. Help me see the deep water in the people around me. Teach me to ask good questions and to listen with real patience and care. Amen.
teaser: Every man you know is carrying deep water. Few people ever draw it out.

title: Do What Is Right
verse: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
meaning: This proverb says doing what is right and just pleases God more than sacrifice. Religious acts cannot cover up wrong living. God cares about how you treat people every day.
heart: You can go to church and still cheat, lie or mistreat people. God wants your life, not just your rituals. Today, do one right and fair thing, especially where no one will notice.
holdOn: God wants me to do what is right, not just look religious.
prayer: God, I do not want a faith that is only for show. Help me do what is right and fair today. Let my everyday life please you more than any religious act. Amen.
teaser: God says he prefers one thing over religious offerings. It is harder to fake.

title: Same Maker
verse: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.
meaning: This proverb says rich and poor have one thing in common: the LORD made them all. Money does not change a person's worth. Every person bears the mark of the same Maker.
heart: It is easy to respect people with money and status and ignore the rest. God made them all. Today, treat a worker, a cleaner or someone in need with the same respect you would give a boss.
holdOn: Rich or poor, every person was made by the same God.
prayer: God, you made every person, rich and poor alike. Forgive me for judging people by money or status. Help me treat everyone with respect, because every one of them is yours. Amen.
teaser: Rich and poor have one thing in common. This proverb names it.

title: Fall Seven Times
verse: for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
meaning: This proverb says a righteous man may fall seven times, yet he rises again. Falling does not make him wicked. What marks him is that he keeps getting back up, while the wicked stay down.
heart: You will fail, maybe often. That does not disqualify you. The difference is getting back up. If you fell recently, in a habit, a test or a relationship, get up today and take the next right step.
holdOn: Falling does not define me. Getting back up with God does.
prayer: God, I have fallen more times than I can count. Thank you that you lift me up. Give me the grit to rise again today, and keep me from staying down in shame. Amen.
teaser: This proverb says a good man falls seven times. The point is what happens next.

title: Skilled in His Work
verse: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
meaning: This proverb notices a man who is skilled at his work. Such a man will stand before kings, not obscure people. Excellence opens doors. Doing good work well is honored by God and people.
heart: Whatever you do, a job, a sport, your studies or a trade, get good at it. Skill is built by daily practice, not talent alone. Pick one skill and practice it for thirty focused minutes today.
holdOn: Doing my work with skill honors God and opens doors.
prayer: God, you gave me abilities and the chance to grow them. Help me work with excellence, not shortcuts. Make me skilled and faithful in my work, for your glory. Amen.
teaser: This proverb says skill can take a man to an unexpected place.

title: Integrity That Lasts
verse: A righteous man walks in integrity. Blessed are his children after him.
meaning: This proverb says a righteous man walks in integrity, and his children are blessed after him. A man's character does not just affect him. It shapes the people who come after him.
heart: Whether or not you have kids someday, people are watching how you live: younger brothers, cousins, teammates. Your integrity is a gift to them. Live today in a way you would want them to copy.
holdOn: My integrity today can bless people long after me.
prayer: God, make me a man of integrity. Let my choices today bless the people who come after me. Help me live in a way I would want younger men to copy. Amen.
teaser: A man's integrity does not stop with him. This proverb says where it goes.

title: Walls of Self-control
verse: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
meaning: In the ancient world, a city without walls had no defense. Anyone could walk in and take it. This proverb says a man without self-control is like that city: open to every attack.
heart: Self-control is your wall. Without it, anger, lust, laziness and greed walk right in. Walls are built one stone at a time. Choose one area today to practice saying no, even in a small way.
holdOn: Self-control is my wall. Without it, anything can walk in.
prayer: God, I have broken walls in my life. Help me rebuild them, stone by stone. Give me self-control over my anger, my desires and my habits. Guard me from attack. Amen.
teaser: An ancient city without walls was helpless. This proverb says some men are too.

title: Speak Up for Them
verse: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate. Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”
meaning: A king's mother taught him to speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves. A good leader defends the poor and needy and judges fairly. Power is meant to protect the weak, not use them.
heart: When someone is mocked or treated unfairly, silence helps the bully. Speaking up takes courage. This week, when you see someone pushed around, open your mouth and stand with him.
holdOn: I will open my mouth for those who cannot speak for themselves.
prayer: God, give me courage to speak up for people who are mocked or mistreated. Make me fair and brave. Use whatever influence I have to protect the weak around me. Amen.
teaser: A queen gave her son, a king, one job description. It still applies to us.

title: A Season for Everything
verse: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
meaning: The Teacher wrote that there is a season for everything under heaven. Times to build and tear down, to cry and laugh, to work and rest. Life moves in seasons, and God is over all of them.
heart: You may be in a season you did not choose: waiting, grieving, starting over. Seasons change. Ask God what this season is for, and do what fits it well, instead of fighting it.
holdOn: Every season has a purpose, and God is over all of them.
prayer: God, you are Lord of every season. Help me see what this season of my life is for. Give me patience to live it well, and hope that it will change in time. Amen.
teaser: The Teacher said life comes in seasons. Knowing yours changes everything.

title: Eternity in Your Heart
verse: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
meaning: The Teacher says God makes everything beautiful in its time. He has also put eternity in human hearts. We long for something beyond this life, even though we cannot see the whole of God's plan.
heart: That restless feeling that there must be more is not random. God put it there. Nothing on earth will fully satisfy it. Let that longing point you to God today instead of to the next distraction.
holdOn: God put eternity in my heart, and only he can fill it.
prayer: God, you put eternity in my heart. I keep trying to fill it with things that do not last. Point my longing toward you, and make my life beautiful in your time. Amen.
teaser: That feeling that there must be more? The Teacher says it was put there on purpose.

title: Two Are Better
verse: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
meaning: The Teacher says two are better than one, because they work better together. If one falls, the other lifts him up. But pity the man who falls when he is alone, with no one to help.
heart: Isolation is dangerous for men. Some of the worst falls happen alone. Who would lift you up if you fell? If no one comes to mind, start building that friendship today with one honest conversation.
holdOn: When I fall, I need a brother to lift me up.
prayer: God, I do not want to fall alone. Give me a friend who will lift me up, and make me that friend for someone else. Break my habit of hiding when I struggle. Amen.
teaser: The Teacher said pity one kind of man. Make sure it is not you.

title: Daniel Drew a Line
verse: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
meaning: Daniel was a teenager taken to Babylon and trained to serve the king. He decided in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's food and wine. He asked politely, and God gave him favor.
heart: Daniel decided in advance, before the pressure hit. He was respectful but firm. What lines have you decided in advance? Name one today, and tell a friend so he can help you hold it.
holdOn: Like Daniel, I can decide in my heart before the pressure comes.
prayer: God, give me Daniel's courage. Help me decide in my heart where my lines are before temptation shows up. Make me respectful and firm, and give me your favor. Amen.
teaser: A teenager in a foreign palace said no to the king's menu. It changed his life.

title: Do It With Your Might
verse: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
meaning: The Teacher says whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength. Life is short, and work done half-heartedly is wasted. Give your full effort while you have the chance.
heart: Half effort is a habit that sneaks into school, work, training and relationships. Today, pick one task and give it everything you have. Notice how different it feels to do something fully.
holdOn: Whatever my hand finds to do, I will do it with my full strength.
prayer: God, forgive me for giving half my effort. Life is short. Help me do my work today with all my strength, and do it as a gift to you. Amen.
teaser: The Teacher saw a problem with half effort. His fix is one sentence long.

title: Even If He Does Not
verse: If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”
meaning: Three young Jewish men refused to bow to the king's golden statue. Facing a blazing furnace, they said God could save them. And even if he did not, they still would not bow.
heart: Real faith does not depend on getting the outcome you want. It trusts God even if he says no. What are you trusting God for right now? Say it today: even if not, I will still follow you.
holdOn: God is able to save me. Even if he does not, I will not bow.
prayer: God, I believe you are able to rescue me. Give me faith that stays firm even if you do not do what I ask. Help me never bow to what is false. Amen.
teaser: Three young men stood in front of a furnace and said three words: but if not.

title: Perfect Peace
verse: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
meaning: Isaiah wrote a song about God's strong city. In it, he promises perfect peace to the person whose mind stays fixed on God. That person trusts him. Peace follows focus.
heart: Your mind goes where you point it. If you keep it on worries, you get anxiety. If you keep it on God, you get peace. Today, every time worry pops up, turn your mind back to God for a moment.
holdOn: God keeps my mind in peace when I keep it fixed on him.
prayer: God, my mind drifts to fear and worry. Fix it on you. Keep me in your perfect peace today. When anxiety pulls me away, gently bring my thoughts back to you. Amen.
teaser: Isaiah said peace follows something specific. It is about where your mind goes.

title: Strength in Quiet
verse: For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
meaning: Israel wanted to trust in Egypt's army for protection. God told them their strength would come from returning to him, resting, and quiet confidence in him. Sadly, they refused to listen.
heart: We think strength means more effort and more noise. God says strength grows in quiet trust. Before you push harder on a problem today, stop. Return to God, rest for a minute, and trust him.
holdOn: My strength grows in quietness and confidence in God.
prayer: Lord GOD, I keep trusting in my own plans. Bring me back to you. Teach me to rest and find strength in quiet confidence. Do not let me refuse you like Israel did. Amen.
teaser: Israel had an army to trust. God offered them a different kind of strength.

title: You Are Mine
verse: But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
meaning: God spoke to Israel, who had failed him and been exiled. He did not reject them. He said: do not be afraid, I have redeemed you, I have called you by name, you are mine.
heart: Your name means something to God. You are not a number or a failure to him. You are his. When you feel worthless today, say these words out loud to yourself: God calls me by name. I am his.
holdOn: God has called me by name. I belong to him.
prayer: God, you created me, redeemed me and called me by name. Thank you that I am yours, even when I fail. Take away my fear, and help me live like I belong to you. Amen.
teaser: God spoke to people who had failed him badly. His first words surprised them.

title: What God Requires
verse: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
meaning: People asked Micah what offering would please God. Rivers of oil? Thousands of rams? Micah said God had already shown them: do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God.
heart: God is not impressed by big religious shows. He wants three things in daily life: fairness, kindness and humility. Pick one of the three today and practice it in one specific moment.
holdOn: God asks me to do justice, love mercy and walk humbly with him.
prayer: God, I do not want to impress you with shows. Teach me to act justly, love mercy and walk humbly with you. Show me where to practice each one today. Amen.
teaser: People offered God thousands of rams. Micah said he wanted three simple things.

title: Poor in Spirit
verse: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
meaning: Jesus began his most famous sermon by blessing people who were poor in spirit. These are people who know they need God and cannot make it on their own. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
heart: Pride says you have it handled. The poor in spirit admit they do not. That is not weakness. It is the door into God's kingdom. Tell God plainly today: I need you.
holdOn: Knowing I need God is the start of real strength.
prayer: Jesus, I need you. I cannot make life work on my own. Make me poor in spirit, honest about my need, and full of your kingdom. Thank you for welcoming people like me. Amen.
teaser: Jesus opened his greatest sermon by blessing the people most men try not to be.

title: Blessed Are Those Who Mourn
verse: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
meaning: Jesus said people who mourn are blessed, because they will be comforted. Grief is not a sign that God has left you. It is where his comfort meets you most deeply.
heart: Many men are taught not to cry. But grief that is never felt stays stuck inside. If you are carrying a loss, give yourself room to mourn. Talk to God about it, and to someone you trust.
holdOn: When I mourn honestly, God promises to comfort me.
prayer: God, I carry losses I have never fully grieved. Give me permission to mourn. Meet me with your comfort, and help me not to stay numb or alone in it. Amen.
teaser: Jesus called grieving people blessed. Here is why that is not as strange as it sounds.

title: Strength Under Control
verse: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
meaning: Jesus said the gentle will inherit the earth. The word gentle described a strong horse that had been trained. It is not weakness. It is power under control, ready to obey its master.
heart: Gentleness is not being soft. It is having strength and choosing to use it well. Today, in a moment where you could dominate someone with words or power, choose to be gentle instead.
holdOn: Gentleness is not weakness. It is strength under control.
prayer: Jesus, you were strong and gentle. Train my strength so it is under your control. Help me use my power to serve people, not crush them. Make me gentle like you. Amen.
teaser: The word Jesus used for gentle was used for a strong horse. Here is why.

title: Hungry for What Is Right
verse: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
meaning: Jesus said those who hunger and thirst for righteousness will be filled. He means wanting to be right with God and to see right done. It is wanting it like a starving man wants food.
heart: What are you hungry for most: comfort, success, approval? Jesus promises to fill those who are hungry for what is right. Ask God today to make you hungry for his ways more than anything else.
holdOn: I want to be hungry for what is right, and God will fill me.
prayer: Jesus, make me hungry and thirsty for what is right. Take away my appetite for things that do not matter. Fill me with your righteousness and a passion for justice. Amen.
teaser: Jesus promised a full stomach to people with one specific hunger.

title: Mercy Comes Back
verse: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
meaning: Jesus said the merciful are blessed, because they will receive mercy. People who forgive and show kindness to those who do not deserve it live in the same mercy God gives them.
heart: Showing mercy feels like letting someone off the hook. But you have been let off the hook by God many times. Think of someone who needs mercy from you. Show it today in one small way.
holdOn: I show mercy because I have received so much of it.
prayer: God, you have shown me so much mercy. Help me show it to others, especially people who have hurt me. Soften my heart, and let me forgive like you forgive me. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said mercy works like a boomerang. Here is what he meant.

title: Pure in Heart
verse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
meaning: Jesus said the pure in heart will see God. Pure here means unmixed, like clean water. A heart that is not divided by hidden sin and double motives can see God clearly.
heart: Hidden sin clouds your view of God, like dirty water. Purity is not about being perfect, but about being honest and undivided. Bring one hidden area into the light today, before God and one trusted friend.
holdOn: A pure and undivided heart sees God more clearly.
prayer: Jesus, I want a pure heart. Clean out the hidden sin and mixed motives that cloud my view of you. Make my heart honest and undivided, so I can see you clearly. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said one kind of person gets to see God. The word he used means unmixed.

title: Peacemakers
verse: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
meaning: Jesus said peacemakers are blessed and will be called children of God. Peacemakers do not just avoid fights. They work to bring people back together, the way God brings people back to himself.
heart: Making peace takes more courage than starting a fight or walking away. Is there a conflict in your friend group or family? Take one step toward peace today: a message, an apology or a calm talk.
holdOn: I can be a peacemaker, not just a peacekeeper.
prayer: God, make me a peacemaker, not someone who runs or fights. Give me courage to step into conflict and bring people together. Show me one place to make peace today. Amen.
teaser: Peacekeepers avoid fights. Peacemakers do something harder. Jesus blessed them.

title: Let Your Light Shine
verse: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
meaning: Jesus told his followers they are the light of the world. They should not hide their light. Their good works should shine so others see them and give glory to the Father in heaven.
heart: Your good actions are meant to point people to God, not to you. You do not have to preach. Do something good today that makes people curious about what drives you, and give God the credit.
holdOn: My good works should point people to my Father, not to me.
prayer: Father, let my light shine today in how I work, speak and treat people. Keep me from showing off. Let people see your goodness through me and give you the glory. Amen.
teaser: Jesus called his followers light. Then he said where the light should point.

title: Pray in Secret
verse: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
meaning: Jesus warned against praying to impress people. Instead, he said to go into a private room, shut the door and pray to your Father in secret. God sees what is done in secret and rewards it.
heart: Your private prayer life is where real faith grows. No one is watching, and that is the point. Find a private spot today, shut the door, and talk to your Father honestly for five minutes.
holdOn: My Father sees me when I pray in secret.
prayer: Father, I want to know you in private, not just in public. Meet me in my secret place today. Teach me to pray honestly when no one else is watching. Amen.
teaser: Jesus told people where to pray. It was not where they expected.

title: Where Your Treasure Is
verse: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
meaning: Jesus said that where your treasure is, your heart will be too. What you spend money and time on shows what you love. Your heart follows your treasure, not the other way around.
heart: Look at your bank app and your screen time. They tell you what you treasure. If you want your heart to grow toward God, move some treasure toward him. Give some money or time to God this week.
holdOn: My heart follows my treasure, so I choose my treasure wisely.
prayer: Jesus, show me what I really treasure. Move my heart toward you as I move my money and time toward you. Free me from loving things that will not last. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said your heart follows something. Check your bank app to see what.

title: Look at the Birds
verse: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
meaning: Jesus pointed at birds flying by. They do not plant or harvest or store food, yet God feeds them. Then he asked: are you not worth much more than they are? Worry adds nothing.
heart: Worry about money, the future and what people think can eat your days. Next time you see a bird today, let it remind you: your Father feeds them, and he values you even more.
holdOn: If God feeds the birds, he will take care of me.
prayer: Father, you feed the birds, and you know what I need. Take my worries about money and the future. Help me trust you and live today without fear or panic. Amen.
teaser: Jesus used a bird to answer one of the biggest worries men carry.

title: Seek First
verse: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
meaning: After telling people not to worry, Jesus gave them a new focus. Seek God's kingdom and his righteousness first. Then the things you worry about, like food and clothes, will be given too.
heart: Most of us seek God last, after everything else. Jesus flips the order. Before you chase your goals today, spend the first moments seeking God. Ask him what his kingdom looks like in your day.
holdOn: When I seek God first, everything else finds its right place.
prayer: God, I put you last too often. Today I want to seek you first. Show me what your kingdom looks like in my work, my friendships and my choices. Amen.
teaser: Jesus gave a cure for worry. It is about what comes first.

title: Ask, Seek, Knock
verse: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
meaning: Jesus told people to ask, seek and knock. In the original language, these mean keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking. God is a good Father who loves to answer his children.
heart: Some men stop praying after one try. Jesus says keep going. Is there a prayer you gave up on? Pick it back up today. Ask again, seek again, knock again, and trust your Father.
holdOn: I will keep asking, seeking and knocking. My Father hears.
prayer: Father, I have given up on some prayers. Help me keep asking, seeking and knocking. Thank you that you are a good Father who hears me. Answer in your way. Amen.
teaser: Jesus gave three commands about prayer. In Greek, they all mean: keep going.

title: Go First
verse: Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
meaning: Jesus gave a simple rule for how to treat people: whatever you want others to do for you, do it for them. He said this sums up the whole Law and the Prophets. Love takes the first step.
heart: Most people wait to be treated well before they treat others well. Jesus says go first. Think of how you want to be treated today, with respect and patience, and give that first to someone else.
holdOn: I will treat others the way I want to be treated, and go first.
prayer: Jesus, teach me to go first in kindness. Help me treat people the way I want to be treated, even when they have not earned it. Make your love real in my daily life. Amen.
teaser: Jesus summed up the whole Bible's teaching on people in one sentence.

title: Build on the Rock
verse: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
meaning: Jesus ended his sermon with a story. Two men built houses. One built on rock, one on sand. When the storm hit, only the house on rock stood. The wise man is the one who hears Jesus' words and does them.
heart: Hearing good teaching is not enough. Storms test what you actually did with it. Take one thing Jesus said this week and put it into action today. That is how you lay rock under your life.
holdOn: My life stands in the storm when I build on what Jesus said.
prayer: Jesus, I hear your words, but I do not always do them. Help me build my life on the rock. When storms come, let my house stand because I followed you. Amen.
teaser: Two men built houses. A storm showed which one listened.

title: Moved With Compassion
verse: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
meaning: Jesus looked at the crowds and was moved with compassion. They were tired and confused, like sheep without a shepherd. He did not see a mob. He saw people who needed someone to care.
heart: Crowds can make us cynical. Jesus looked deeper. In your school, work or online, look for the person who seems lost. Ask God to give you his compassion, and do one kind thing for that person.
holdOn: Jesus sees lost and tired people with compassion, and so can I.
prayer: Jesus, you see people with compassion. Give me your eyes. Help me notice those who are tired and lost, and give me the courage to care for one of them today. Amen.
teaser: Jesus looked at a crowd and felt something most of us do not.

title: Gentle and Humble
verse: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
meaning: A yoke joined two oxen so they could pull together. Jesus invites us to take his yoke and learn from him. He describes himself as gentle and humble in heart. With him, we find rest for our souls.
heart: You are already pulling something, maybe pressure, fear or ambition. Jesus offers to pull with you. Learn from him today. Watch how he treats people in the Gospels, gently and humbly, and copy one thing.
holdOn: With Jesus beside me, my soul finds rest.
prayer: Jesus, I am tired of pulling alone. I take your yoke. Teach me to be gentle and humble like you. Give my soul the rest it has been missing. Amen.
teaser: Jesus described his own heart only once. Neither word was what you might expect.

title: Bruised but Not Broken
verse: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a smoking flax, until he leads justice to victory.
meaning: Matthew quotes Isaiah to describe Jesus. He will not break a bruised reed or snuff out a smoldering wick. Weak and damaged people are safe with him. He does not crush what is barely holding on.
heart: Maybe you feel like a bruised reed, barely standing. Jesus is not going to finish you off. He will heal you. Bring him your weakest place today, and trust that he handles it gently.
holdOn: When I am bruised and barely holding on, Jesus will not crush me.
prayer: Jesus, I feel bruised and weak. Thank you that you do not crush people like me. Heal me gently. Fan the small flame that is left in me back into fire. Amen.
teaser: Jesus is described with two pictures of things barely hanging on. Here is why.

title: Good Soil
verse: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”
meaning: Jesus told a story about seed falling on different soils. Some soil was hard, some rocky, some thorny. The good soil heard the word, understood it, and produced a big harvest.
heart: The same seed grows differently depending on the soil. Your heart is the soil. Busy, distracted hearts choke the word. Make space today: read slowly, think about it, and ask what it means for you.
holdOn: My heart is the soil. I want it to be good ground.
prayer: God, make my heart good soil. Clear out the thorns of worry and the hard ground of pride. Help me hear your word, understand it and grow fruit for you. Amen.
teaser: Jesus told a story about soil. It was really about you.

title: It Is I
verse: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
meaning: The disciples were in a boat in a storm at night. They saw Jesus walking on the water and screamed, thinking he was a ghost. Jesus called out: cheer up, it is I, do not be afraid.
heart: Fear often comes from not knowing what is coming toward you. Jesus speaks into that fear with his presence. In whatever storm you face today, listen for his voice: it is I. Do not be afraid.
holdOn: In the storm, Jesus says: it is I. Do not be afraid.
prayer: Jesus, I am in a storm and it is dark. Let me hear your voice over the wind. Calm my fear with your presence, and help me trust that you are near. Amen.
teaser: The disciples saw a figure walking toward them on the waves. They screamed.

title: Take Up Your Cross
verse: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
meaning: Jesus told his disciples plainly what following him costs. Deny yourself, take up your cross and follow me. A cross meant death to self. Following Jesus is not an add-on to your life. It is a new life.
heart: Many want Jesus without the cross. Denying yourself means saying no to some of what you want so you can say yes to him. Name one thing you will deny yourself today for the sake of following Jesus.
holdOn: Following Jesus means saying no to myself and yes to him.
prayer: Jesus, I want to follow you for real, not halfway. Help me deny myself where it matters. Give me strength to carry my cross today and stay close behind you. Amen.
teaser: Jesus never hid the cost of following him. Here it is, in one sentence.

title: Where Two or Three Gather
verse: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
meaning: Jesus promised that where two or three gather in his name, he is right there with them. Faith was never meant to be lived alone. Even the smallest group of believers has Jesus in the middle.
heart: You do not need a big church to meet with Jesus. Two or three is enough. Find one or two guys this week and pray together, even for five minutes. Jesus promised to be in the middle of it.
holdOn: When I gather with even one or two others in his name, Jesus is there.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for being with us when we gather in your name. Give me two or three brothers to pray with. Be in the middle of our friendship. Amen.
teaser: Jesus promised to show up in a group smaller than you might think.

title: Came to Serve
verse: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
meaning: The disciples argued about who would be greatest. Jesus said the greatest are servants. He himself came not to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.
heart: The world says great men get served. Jesus says great men serve. Lead by serving today. Do a job no one wants, help someone without being asked, and do not post about it.
holdOn: Real greatness serves others, just like Jesus did.
prayer: Jesus, you came to serve, not to be served. Kill my need to be the big man. Show me how to serve someone today, quietly, the way you served me. Amen.
teaser: The disciples argued over who was greatest. Jesus redefined the word.

title: Love Your Neighbor
verse: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
meaning: Asked about the greatest command, Jesus said to love God with everything. Then he added a second, just as important: love your neighbor as yourself. Love for God shows up in love for people.
heart: Your neighbor is not only the guy next door. It is anyone God puts in your path. Think about how well you care for yourself. Give that same care to one neighbor today, even someone you find hard to like.
holdOn: My love for God shows up in how I love the people near me.
prayer: God, teach me to love my neighbor as myself. Open my eyes to the people you put in my path today. Help me care for them the way you care for me. Amen.
teaser: Jesus was asked for one great command. He gave two.

title: You Did It to Me
verse: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
meaning: Jesus told a story about the final judgment. The King tells people that when they fed the hungry, welcomed strangers and visited prisoners, they did it to him. Jesus is found in people in need.
heart: When you help someone in need, you are serving Jesus himself. That changes everything. Look for one of the least today: someone hungry, lonely or ignored. Serve them as if they were Jesus.
holdOn: When I serve someone in need, I serve Jesus himself.
prayer: Jesus, open my eyes to see you in people who are hungry, lonely and ignored. Help me serve them as if I were serving you, because I really am. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said people will be surprised at the final judgment. Here is why.

title: Watch and Pray
verse: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
meaning: In the garden the night before his death, Jesus asked his friends to stay awake and pray. They kept falling asleep. Jesus told them to watch and pray, because the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak.
heart: Good intentions are not enough. Your body is tired and weak, especially late at night. Temptation hits hardest then. Watch and pray: know your weak hours, and plan ahead to pray and stay guarded during them.
holdOn: My spirit is willing, but my flesh is weak, so I watch and pray.
prayer: Jesus, my spirit wants to follow you, but my flesh is weak. Help me watch and pray. Show me my weak hours, and guard me through them tonight and every night. Amen.
teaser: Jesus' best friends could not stay awake. He told them why it mattered.

title: With You Always
verse: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
meaning: Before he returned to heaven, Jesus gave his followers a mission: make disciples and teach them. Then he gave a promise to carry them through it. I am with you always, to the very end of the age.
heart: The mission is big, and some days you will feel alone in it. You are not. Jesus is with you always, at work, at home, on bad days. Say it to yourself today: Jesus is with me right now.
holdOn: Jesus is with me always, to the very end.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you are with me always. Give me courage to share you with others. On days I feel alone, remind me that you have not left. Amen.
teaser: Jesus gave his followers a huge mission. Then he gave them a promise to match.

title: Before Dawn
verse: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
meaning: After a busy night healing crowds, Jesus got up very early, while it was still dark. He went to a quiet place and prayed. Even the Son of God needed time alone with his Father.
heart: If Jesus needed quiet time with God, you do too. Try getting up fifteen minutes earlier tomorrow. Before the world wakes up, go somewhere quiet and talk to your Father.
holdOn: If Jesus needed time alone with God, so do I.
prayer: Father, Jesus made time to be alone with you before dawn. Help me do the same. Give me discipline to rise early and meet you before the noise starts. Amen.
teaser: After the busiest night of his ministry, Jesus did something before dawn.

title: For the Sick
verse: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
meaning: Religious leaders criticized Jesus for eating with sinners and tax collectors. Jesus answered that healthy people do not need a doctor. He came for sinners, not for people who think they are already good enough.
heart: If you feel too messed up for God, you are exactly who Jesus came for. Stop hiding. Bring him the mess today. And look for someone others write off, and treat him like Jesus would.
holdOn: Jesus came for people who need him, and that includes me.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming for sinners like me. I do not have to clean up first. Heal me where I am sick. Help me welcome people others write off. Amen.
teaser: Religious leaders complained about who Jesus ate with. His answer was sharp.

title: Peace, Be Still
verse: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.
meaning: A violent storm hit the boat, and the disciples thought they would drown. Jesus was asleep. They woke him, and he rebuked the wind and told the sea: peace, be still. Instantly, the storm stopped.
heart: Jesus has authority over storms, outside you and inside you. Whatever is raging in your mind today, ask Jesus to speak to it. Then take a slow breath and let his peace settle you.
holdOn: Jesus has authority over the storms around me and inside me.
prayer: Jesus, you calmed the wind and the waves with a word. Speak peace to the storm in my mind today. Calm my heart, and help me trust you in the boat. Amen.
teaser: The disciples were panicking. Jesus was asleep. Then he said three words.

title: Gain the World, Lose Your Soul
verse: For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
meaning: Jesus asked a hard question. What good is it if a man gains the whole world but loses his own life? Money, fame and success cannot buy back a soul. Some trades are never worth it.
heart: Ambition is good, but not at any price. Some men trade their integrity, family or faith for success. Ask yourself honestly today: what am I trading for what I want? Is it worth it?
holdOn: No amount of success is worth losing my soul.
prayer: Jesus, keep me from trading my soul for success. Guard my integrity, my faith and the people I love. Help me chase what matters most, and nothing at its expense. Amen.
teaser: Jesus asked a question every ambitious man should answer honestly.

title: Come Away and Rest
verse: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
meaning: The disciples were so busy serving crowds that they did not even have time to eat. Jesus told them to come away with him to a quiet place and rest for a while. Rest was his idea.
heart: Busyness can look like importance. Jesus took his friends away to rest. If you are running on fumes, take a real break this week. Get away somewhere quiet, even for an hour, and be with Jesus.
holdOn: Jesus invites me to come away with him and rest.
prayer: Jesus, I am busy and worn out. Thank you for inviting me to rest. Help me step away, find a quiet place and be with you, without feeling guilty. Amen.
teaser: The disciples were too busy to eat. Jesus gave them an unusual instruction.

title: Help My Unbelief
verse: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
meaning: A desperate father brought his suffering son to Jesus. When Jesus spoke about faith, the father cried out: I believe, help my unbelief. He had faith and doubt at the same time. Jesus healed his son.
heart: You do not need perfect faith to come to Jesus. Doubt and faith can live together. Bring your doubts to him honestly today. Pray the father's prayer: I believe. Help my unbelief.
holdOn: I believe, and Jesus can help my unbelief.
prayer: Jesus, I believe, but I also doubt. Help my unbelief. Thank you that you do not turn away people with mixed faith. Strengthen what little faith I have today. Amen.
teaser: A desperate father prayed the most honest prayer in the Bible. Jesus answered.

title: Let Them Come
verse: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
meaning: People brought children to Jesus, and the disciples tried to send them away. Jesus was angry. He said let the children come, for God's kingdom belongs to people like them, people who simply trust.
heart: Children come to their fathers without a resume. That is how God's kingdom works. Drop the act today. Come to God simply, the way a kid comes to a dad he trusts.
holdOn: I can come to God simply, like a child who trusts his father.
prayer: Father, I overcomplicate my relationship with you. Help me come to you simply and trust you like a child. Remove my need to impress you with what I do. Amen.
teaser: Jesus got angry with his disciples once for a surprising reason.

title: He Is Calling You
verse: Jesus stood still and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”
meaning: Blind Bartimaeus shouted for Jesus while the crowd told him to be quiet. Jesus stopped and said: call him. The people said: cheer up, get up, he is calling you. Bartimaeus threw off his cloak and came.
heart: People may tell you to be quiet about your need. Jesus stops for people who keep calling out. If you feel overlooked, keep calling to him. He hears you. Get up today and go toward him.
holdOn: When the crowd says be quiet, Jesus still stops and calls me.
prayer: Jesus, I call out to you like Bartimaeus. Do not pass me by. Thank you that you stop for people the crowd ignores. I get up and come to you. Amen.
teaser: A blind man would not stop shouting. The crowd hated it. Jesus stopped.

title: With All Your Strength
verse: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
meaning: Jesus said the greatest command is to love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. Not part of you. All of you. Your feelings, your life, your thinking and your effort.
heart: Many men give God a corner of their lives. He asks for all of it. Which part are you holding back: your mind, your body, your money? Give that part to God today in one clear choice.
holdOn: God wants all of me: heart, soul, mind and strength.
prayer: God, I want to love you with all of me. My heart, my soul, my mind and my strength are yours. Show me what I am holding back, and help me let go of it. Amen.
teaser: Jesus named four parts of you that God wants. Most of us give him one.

title: Follow Me
verse: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
meaning: Jesus saw two fishermen, Simon and Andrew, casting their nets. He said: come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. Right away they left their nets and followed him.
heart: Jesus did not call scholars or rich men first. He called working guys and promised to make them into something new. He is calling you too. What net do you need to drop today to follow him?
holdOn: Jesus calls ordinary men and makes them into something new.
prayer: Jesus, you called fishermen, and you are calling me. Make me into the man you want me to be. Help me drop what holds me back and follow you today. Amen.
teaser: Jesus walked up to two fishermen at work. Within minutes, their lives changed.

title: Not as the World Gives
verse: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
meaning: The night before he died, Jesus gave his friends a gift: his own peace. He said it is not like the peace the world gives. So do not let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
heart: The world's peace depends on things going well. Jesus' peace holds even when they do not. If your heart is troubled today, take his gift. Pray, breathe, and choose not to let fear run your heart.
holdOn: Jesus gives me a peace the world cannot give or take away.
prayer: Jesus, I receive your peace today. My heart is troubled and afraid in some areas. Calm it with your peace, which is stronger than anything the world could offer me. Amen.
teaser: Jesus left his friends a gift the night before he died. You can have it too.

title: The Dawn From on High
verse: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
meaning: An old priest named Zechariah sang about the coming Savior. He said that because of God's tender mercy, the dawn from on high would visit us. God's mercy breaks into darkness like sunrise.
heart: If your life feels like night right now, remember that dawn always comes. God's mercy is coming toward you like the morning. Look for one small sign of light today, and thank him for it.
holdOn: God's tender mercy breaks into my darkness like the dawn.
prayer: God, thank you for your tender mercy. Shine into my darkness like the morning dawn. Help me see the first light of your goodness today, and walk in it. Amen.
teaser: An old man waited his whole life for one sunrise. Then he sang about it.

title: Growing in Four Ways
verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
meaning: Luke tells us how Jesus grew as a young man. He grew in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and with people. He grew in his mind, his body, his faith and his relationships.
heart: Growth is not just about the gym or just about Bible reading. Jesus grew in four ways. Which area is weakest for you right now? Take one small step to grow in that area today.
holdOn: I want to grow like Jesus: in wisdom, strength, faith and friendships.
prayer: Jesus, you grew in wisdom, stature and favor with God and people. Help me grow in all four too. Show me my weakest area, and help me take a step today. Amen.
teaser: The Bible gives one line about Jesus as a teenager. It names four kinds of growth.

title: Two Coats
verse: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
meaning: John the Baptist told people how to show they had really turned to God. If you have two coats, give one to someone who has none. Share your food too. Real change shows up in how you share.
heart: Repentance is not only feeling sorry. It changes what you do with your stuff. Look in your closet or your pantry today. Find one thing you do not need, and give it to someone who does.
holdOn: Real change shows up in what I share.
prayer: God, I have more than I need. Show me what to share. Help me give my extra to someone who has none, and let my generosity show that I have truly changed. Amen.
teaser: John the Baptist was asked how to prove you have changed. He talked about coats.

title: Good News for the Captives
verse: “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed,
meaning: In his hometown synagogue, Jesus read from Isaiah. The passage spoke of one sent to bring good news to the poor, heal the brokenhearted and free captives. Then he said this was fulfilled in him. It was his mission.
heart: Jesus came to free people, not to load them down. What holds you captive: an addiction, a lie, fear, shame? He came for that. Name it to him today, and take one step toward freedom with someone's help.
holdOn: Jesus came to set captives free, and that includes me.
prayer: Jesus, you came to heal the brokenhearted and free the captives. You know what holds me. Set me free. Give me courage to ask for help and walk in your freedom. Amen.
teaser: Jesus read one passage in his hometown. Then he said something that shocked everyone.

title: He Withdrew to Pray
verse: But he withdrew himself into the desert and prayed.
meaning: As Jesus became famous, crowds pressed in from everywhere. Luke says he often withdrew to lonely places to pray. The busier he got, the more he made time to be alone with his Father.
heart: When life gets busy, prayer is usually the first thing we drop. Jesus did the opposite. The more pressure you face this week, the more you need time with God. Withdraw for ten minutes today.
holdOn: The busier I get, the more I need time alone with God.
prayer: Father, when life gets busy, I drop time with you. Help me do what Jesus did. Draw me away to quiet places, and fill me there before I go back out. Amen.
teaser: As Jesus became more famous, he did something that seems backwards.

title: The Rule for Enemies
verse: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
meaning: In Luke's version of the Sermon, Jesus says to treat others exactly how you would like them to treat you. He says this right after telling people to love their enemies and do good to those who hate them.
heart: This rule is easy with friends and hard with enemies. Jesus aimed it at enemies. Think of someone you dislike. How would you want them to treat you? Treat them that way once today.
holdOn: I treat people, even enemies, the way I want to be treated.
prayer: Jesus, your rule is simple and hard. Help me treat people the way I want to be treated, even those who are against me. Give me your love for my enemies. Amen.
teaser: Jesus' most famous rule was aimed at a surprising group of people.

title: Merciful Like Your Father
verse: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
meaning: Jesus told his followers to be merciful, just as their Father is merciful. God's mercy toward us sets the standard for how we treat others. Sons should look like their Father.
heart: You look like your father in some ways, for better or worse. Jesus wants you to look like your heavenly Father in mercy. Where are you being harsh with someone? Show that person mercy today.
holdOn: As God's son, I want to be merciful like my Father.
prayer: Father, you are merciful to me every day. Make me look like you. Where I am harsh, soften me. Help me show mercy to someone who does not deserve it today. Amen.
teaser: Sons often look like their fathers. Jesus said that should be true of mercy too.

title: Out of the Heart
verse: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
meaning: Jesus said a good man brings good things out of the good stored in his heart. An evil man brings evil out of the evil stored up. What fills your heart eventually comes out of your mouth.
heart: Pressure squeezes out what is inside you. If anger or crude words come out under stress, the problem is deeper than your mouth. Fill your heart with good today: Scripture, prayer, good music and good friends.
holdOn: What fills my heart is what comes out of my mouth.
prayer: Jesus, clean what is stored in my heart. When pressure squeezes me, let good come out instead of anger and ugliness. Fill me with what is good, true and kind. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said your mouth is a window. Here is what it shows.

title: Faithful in Little
verse: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
meaning: Jesus said whoever is faithful in very little is also faithful in much. Whoever is dishonest in little things will be dishonest in big things too. Character is built and tested in small moments.
heart: Small things reveal you: returning extra change, doing chores well, keeping a minor promise. Big trust comes after small faithfulness. Be faithful in one small, unseen thing today, as practice for bigger things.
holdOn: How I handle small things shows who I really am.
prayer: God, make me faithful in small things. Help me be honest when it seems minor and nobody would notice. Build my character now, so I can be trusted with more. Amen.
teaser: Jesus said small things reveal big things. Here is the test.

title: Hold It Tight
verse: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
meaning: Explaining his story of the soils, Jesus said the good soil stands for people with an honest and good heart. They hear the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit by not giving up.
heart: Hearing the word is easy. Holding on to it when life gets busy or hard is not. Pick one verse you have learned this month. Hold it tight this week by reading it every morning and night.
holdOn: I want to hold God's word tight and keep going until it bears fruit.
prayer: God, give me an honest and good heart. Help me hold your word tightly when life tries to pull it away. Make me patient, and let my life bear fruit. Amen.
teaser: Jesus described good soil with three verbs. The last one takes the longest.

title: The One Who Stopped
verse: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
meaning: A man was beaten and left on the road. A priest and a Levite passed by. A Samaritan, from a group the Jews despised, stopped. He was moved with compassion, and he helped at real cost to himself.
heart: The religious guys passed by because they were busy or afraid. The outsider stopped. Who is lying on the side of your road: a classmate, a coworker, a stranger? Do not walk past them this week.
holdOn: I want to be the one who stops, not the one who passes by.
prayer: God, I walk past people in need too often. Give me compassion that stops and helps. Help me serve someone today, even when it is inconvenient or costs me something. Amen.
teaser: Two religious men walked past a beaten stranger. The one who stopped shocked everyone.

title: Count the Cost
verse: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
meaning: Jesus said nobody builds a tower without first sitting down to count the cost, to make sure he can finish it. Following Jesus is like that. Know what it will cost you, and commit anyway.
heart: Following Jesus will cost you something: popularity, comfort, certain habits. Count it honestly. Then decide. Half-built towers are what happens when men start without counting. Write down what following him may cost you this year.
holdOn: I count the cost of following Jesus, and I choose him anyway.
prayer: Jesus, I want to follow you with my eyes open. Show me what it will cost, and give me the courage to pay it. Help me finish what I start with you. Amen.
teaser: Jesus told people to do math before they followed him. Here is why.

title: Good Gifts
verse: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
meaning: Jesus said that even flawed earthly fathers know how to give good gifts to their kids. How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him? God loves to give.
heart: Some men expect God to be stingy because their dad was. God is not. He wants to give you his Spirit, his presence and his strength. Ask him today for what you really need, and expect good from him.
holdOn: My Father in heaven loves to give good gifts to those who ask.
prayer: Father, you are a better father than any on earth. Thank you for loving to give. I ask you for your Spirit today. Fill me with your presence and strength. Amen.
teaser: Jesus compared God to an imperfect dad. Then he said how much better God is.

title: Do Not Be Afraid, Little Flock
verse: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
meaning: Jesus called his followers a little flock, small and vulnerable. He told them not to be afraid. It is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom. God is not reluctant. He is glad to give.
heart: You may feel small and outnumbered. Jesus says do not be afraid. Your Father is glad to give you the kingdom. Let that truth push out one fear today, especially about money or the future.
holdOn: My Father is glad to give me the kingdom. I do not need to be afraid.
prayer: Father, I feel small and afraid sometimes. Thank you that you are glad to give me your kingdom. Push out my fears about the future, and help me trust you. Amen.
teaser: Jesus called his followers small. Then he told them something huge.

title: The Father Runs
verse: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
meaning: A son wasted his father's money on wild living and came home ashamed. While he was still far away, his father saw him, felt compassion, and ran to him. He hugged and kissed his son before he could finish his apology.
heart: In that culture, older men did not run. This father did. That is how God sees you coming home. Whatever you have wasted, turn around today. The Father is already running toward you.
holdOn: When I turn back, my Father runs to meet me.
prayer: Father, I have wandered and wasted things you gave me. I am coming home. Thank you that you run to meet me with compassion, not punishment. Hold me close. Amen.
teaser: In Jesus' day, grown men did not run in public. One father did.

title: One Came Back
verse: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
meaning: Jesus healed ten men with a terrible skin disease. All ten were cured, but only one came back to thank him. He came praising God loudly and fell at Jesus' feet. Jesus asked where the other nine were.
heart: It is easy to take God's help and move on. Gratitude turns back. Think of something God did for you recently. Go back and thank him out loud today, and thank a person who helped you too.
holdOn: I want to be the one who comes back to say thank you.
prayer: God, you have helped me so many times, and I often forget to thank you. Thank you. Make me grateful, like the one who came back, and help me say it out loud. Amen.
teaser: Jesus healed ten men. Only one came back. Jesus noticed.

title: Be Merciful to Me
verse: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
meaning: Jesus told a story of two men praying. A Pharisee bragged about how good he was. A tax collector stood far back, beat his chest and said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Jesus said he was the one who went home forgiven.
heart: Pride keeps score of how good you are. Humility simply asks for mercy. You do not need a long speech. Pray the tax collector's prayer today, honestly, and let God meet you there.
holdOn: My best prayer is honest: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.
prayer: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I will not compare myself to others or list my good deeds. I just need your mercy. Thank you for giving it freely. Amen.
teaser: Two men prayed in the temple. The one who said less went home forgiven.

title: Seeking the Lost
verse: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
meaning: Zacchaeus was a rich, crooked tax collector. Jesus invited himself to his house, and Zacchaeus changed. Critics complained. Jesus said he came to seek and to save the lost. He goes looking.
heart: If you feel lost, Jesus is not waiting for you to find your way back alone. He is looking for you. And he may want to use you to find someone else. Who do you know who feels lost? Reach out.
holdOn: Jesus came looking for lost people, and he found me.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming to find me when I was lost. Help me see other lost people the way you do. Use me to reach someone who feels far from you. Amen.
teaser: A crooked rich man climbed a tree to see Jesus. Jesus called him by name.

title: I Prayed for You
verse: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
meaning: Jesus knew Peter would deny him three times. Before it happened, Jesus told Peter he had prayed that his faith would not fail. And when Peter came back, he was to strengthen his brothers.
heart: Jesus knew Peter would fail and loved him anyway. He even planned to use Peter after the failure. If you have failed recently, Jesus is not done with you. Get back up, and help another brother who is struggling.
holdOn: Jesus prays for me, and he is not done with me after I fail.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you pray for me, even knowing I will fail. Do not let my faith fail completely. When I come back, help me strengthen my brothers. Amen.
teaser: Jesus knew Peter was about to fail badly. He said something unexpected first.

title: Father, Forgive Them
verse: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.
meaning: Soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross and gambled for his clothes. Jesus prayed: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing. He forgave in the middle of his worst pain.
heart: Forgiveness does not mean the wrong was okay. Jesus called it what it was and still forgave. Is there someone you cannot forgive? Start with a prayer for them today, even if your feelings have not caught up.
holdOn: Jesus forgave in his worst pain. He can help me forgive too.
prayer: Jesus, you forgave the men who crucified you. I struggle to forgive much smaller things. Help me. I choose to pray for the people who hurt me. Change my heart. Amen.
teaser: Jesus' first words on the cross were a prayer. It was not for himself.

title: Hearts on Fire
verse: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
meaning: After Jesus rose, two followers walked with him without recognizing him. He explained the Scriptures to them. Later they said: weren't our hearts burning while he talked with us and opened the Scriptures?
heart: Scripture can feel dry until you see Jesus in it. Then it comes alive. Read a passage today and ask: what does this show me about Jesus? Ask him to set your heart burning.
holdOn: When Jesus opens the Scriptures, my heart burns.
prayer: Jesus, open the Scriptures to me like you did on that road. Show yourself in your word. Set my heart on fire again, and walk with me even when I do not recognize you. Amen.
teaser: Two men walked seven miles with Jesus and did not know it. Their hearts did.

title: Darkness Cannot Win
verse: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
meaning: John opens his Gospel by calling Jesus the light that shines in the darkness. Then he adds: the darkness has not overcome it. The fight between light and darkness has a winner.
heart: Some days the darkness feels stronger: in the news, in your family, in your own head. It is not. One candle beats a dark room. Do one good thing today that brings light where it is dark.
holdOn: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness cannot win.
prayer: Jesus, you are the light that darkness cannot overcome. Shine in the dark places of my life and my world. Help me carry your light into somewhere dark today. Amen.
teaser: John begins his Gospel with a fight. He tells you the winner in the first chapter.

title: Water That Satisfies
verse: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
meaning: Jesus met a woman at a well in the heat of the day. He told her that anyone who drinks well water gets thirsty again. But the water he gives becomes a spring inside, welling up to eternal life.
heart: We keep drinking from wells that leave us thirsty: approval, pleasure, success. Jesus offers water that actually satisfies. Notice today what you keep going back to. Ask Jesus to be the spring instead.
holdOn: Only Jesus gives water that truly satisfies my thirst.
prayer: Jesus, I keep drinking from wells that leave me thirsty. Give me your living water today. Become a spring inside me, and satisfy what nothing else in this world can. Amen.
teaser: Jesus offered a thirsty person a kind of water that ends thirst for good.

title: The Light of the World
verse: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
meaning: During a festival when huge lamps lit the temple courts, Jesus stood up and said: I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.
heart: When you are confused about what to do, follow the light. Jesus does not just give advice. He walks ahead of you. In one decision today, ask: what would following Jesus look like here?
holdOn: When I follow Jesus, I do not walk in darkness.
prayer: Jesus, you are the light of the world. I do not want to stumble around in the dark. Help me follow you closely today, and give me the light of life. Amen.
teaser: Jesus made a bold claim during a festival of giant lamps. The timing was not random.

title: Known by the Shepherd
verse: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;
meaning: Jesus called himself the good shepherd. He knows his sheep, and his sheep know him. In the next verses he says he lays down his life for them. To be known and loved by him is the heart of faith.
heart: You may feel unknown, even in a crowd. Jesus knows you completely, the good and the bad, and still lays his life down for you. Spend a few minutes today just being known by him in prayer.
holdOn: The good shepherd knows me completely and still loves me.
prayer: Jesus, you are my good shepherd. Thank you for knowing me completely and loving me anyway. Help me know your voice better, and follow you closely every single day. Amen.
teaser: Jesus called himself a shepherd who knows his sheep. Here is what that means for you.

title: Wash Feet
verse: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
meaning: At the last supper, Jesus took a towel and washed his disciples' dirty feet, a slave's job. Then he said: if I, your Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, you should wash one another's feet.
heart: Washing feet is humble, dirty work. Jesus did it to show what love looks like. What is the humble job nobody wants in your house, team or workplace? Do it today without being asked.
holdOn: If Jesus washed feet, no job is beneath me.
prayer: Jesus, you washed your friends' dirty feet. Humble me. Show me the jobs nobody wants, and help me do them gladly for others, the way you served your friends. Amen.
teaser: The Lord of everything grabbed a towel and did a slave's job.

title: Stay Connected
verse: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
meaning: Jesus said he is the vine and we are the branches. A branch only bears fruit if it stays connected to the vine. Apart from him, we can do nothing that lasts.
heart: You can do a lot without Jesus: work, train, earn. But nothing that truly lasts. Stay connected through prayer and his word, not just on Sunday. Check in with him three times today, even briefly.
holdOn: Apart from Jesus I can do nothing that truly lasts.
prayer: Jesus, you are the vine, and I am a branch. Keep me connected to you. When I try to do life on my own, pull me back. Let my life bear fruit that lasts. Amen.
teaser: Jesus used a plant to explain why some men's lives bear fruit and others do not.

title: I Have Overcome
verse: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
meaning: Jesus told his friends plainly that in this world they would have trouble. He did not hide it. But he told them to take courage, because he has overcome the world. Their peace would be found in him.
heart: Following Jesus does not mean a trouble-free life. It means you have someone who has already won. When trouble hits today, do not be surprised. Say: in this world I have trouble, but Jesus has overcome.
holdOn: In this world I will have trouble, but Jesus has overcome the world.
prayer: Jesus, you told me I would have trouble, and I do. Thank you for being honest. Give me courage and peace in you, because you have already overcome the world. Amen.
teaser: Jesus never promised his followers an easy life. He promised something better.

title: Devoted Together
verse: They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.
meaning: After the Holy Spirit came, the first believers devoted themselves to four things. They learned from the apostles, shared life together, ate together, and prayed. Their faith was lived in community.
heart: Faith grows in community, not in isolation. Which of the four is missing in your life: teaching, friendship, shared meals or prayer? Take one step to add it this week, maybe dinner with believing friends.
holdOn: My faith grows best with others, in teaching, friendship, meals and prayer.
prayer: God, I do not want to follow you alone. Give me a community of believers to learn, eat and pray with. Show me how to take a step toward them this week. Amen.
teaser: The first church did four things together. Most of us are missing at least one.

title: One Heart
verse: The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and soul. Not one of them claimed that anything of the things which he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common.
meaning: The early believers were one in heart and mind. Nobody claimed their things were only their own. They shared everything, and no one among them was in need. Love made them generous.
heart: Selfishness divides; sharing unites. You do not need to give away everything, but you can hold your stuff loosely. Share something you own with a friend in need this week: a ride, tools, time or money.
holdOn: When I hold my stuff loosely, love brings people together.
prayer: God, make me generous like the first believers. Help me hold my things loosely and share them gladly with others. Bring unity among your people, starting with me, today. Amen.
teaser: The first Christians did something with their stuff that still surprises people.

title: Built Up
verse: So the assemblies throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
meaning: After Saul, the persecutor, turned to Jesus, the churches had a time of peace. They grew stronger, lived in awe of the Lord, and were comforted by the Holy Spirit. And they kept growing in number.
heart: Growth comes from awe of God and the comfort of his Spirit. Seasons of peace are for building up, not slacking off. Use this calm season to grow stronger: read more, pray more, serve more.
holdOn: In seasons of peace, I want to be built up, not slack off.
prayer: God, thank you for seasons of peace. Help me use them to grow stronger. Fill me with awe of you and the comfort of your Spirit, and build me up. Amen.
teaser: The church's worst enemy became a believer. Then something good happened.

title: Songs at Midnight
verse: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
meaning: Paul and Silas were beaten and locked in stocks in the deepest part of a prison. At midnight, instead of complaining, they prayed and sang hymns to God. The other prisoners were listening.
heart: Your midnight might be a hard diagnosis, a breakup or failure. Praise in the dark is powerful, and people notice how you handle pain. Play or sing one worship song today, even if you do not feel like it.
holdOn: I can praise God in my midnight, and others will notice.
prayer: God, give me faith to praise you in the dark like Paul and Silas did. When life locks me in, let me pray and sing. Use my response to point others to you. Amen.
teaser: Two men sat bleeding in prison at midnight. What they did next shook the building.

title: Not Far Away
verse: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.
