meaning: Paul spoke to thinkers in Athens who worshiped many gods. He told them the true God made everything and wants people to seek him. And he is not far from any one of us.
heart: Some men think God is distant or hard to find. Paul says he is close, closer than you think. Reach out to him today, even with a simple prayer: God, if you are near, show me.
holdOn: God is not far from me. When I seek him, I can find him.
prayer: God, you are not far from me. Thank you for being close, even when I cannot feel it. I reach out to you today. Help me seek you and find you. Amen.
teaser: Paul told a crowd of philosophers where God is. They did not expect his answer.

title: More Blessed to Give
verse: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
meaning: Paul said goodbye to church leaders he had trained. He reminded them he had worked hard to support himself and help the weak. He quoted Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive.
heart: Working hard so you can give to others is a strong way to live. Paul did it with tents. What can your work provide for someone else? Give part of what you earn or make this week to someone in need.
holdOn: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
prayer: Jesus, you said it is more blessed to give than to receive. Help me believe it and live it. Let my work provide for others, not just for me. Make me a giver. Amen.
teaser: Paul quoted a saying of Jesus that is not found in any of the four Gospels.

title: Peace With God
verse: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
meaning: Paul explains that we are made right with God by faith, not by our good works. Because of that, we now have peace with God through Jesus. The war between us and God is over.
heart: Many men carry a sense that God is angry with them. If you trust Jesus, that war is over. You have peace with God. Let that truth calm you today, especially when guilt tries to start the fight again.
holdOn: Through Jesus, the war is over. I have peace with God.
prayer: God, thank you that I am made right with you by faith in Jesus. The war is over. When guilt shouts at me, remind me that I have peace with you. Amen.
teaser: Paul announced the end of a war many men do not know they are still fighting.

title: No Condemnation
verse: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
meaning: After describing his own struggle with sin, Paul makes a powerful statement. There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. God's verdict over them is not guilty.
heart: Shame tells you that you are your worst moment. Romans 8:1 says something else. If you are in Christ, God does not condemn you. When the shame voice speaks today, answer it with this verse.
holdOn: In Christ, there is no condemnation for me.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that in you there is no condemnation. I give you my shame. Help me hear your verdict over me, not guilty, louder than the voice that accuses me. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote about his own failures. Then he wrote the most freeing sentence in Romans.

title: When Words Run Out
verse: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
meaning: Paul admits that we often do not know how to pray as we should. But the Holy Spirit helps us in our weakness. He prays for us with groans too deep for words.
heart: Some days you have no words for God. That is fine. The Spirit prays for you. Sit quietly today and simply say: Spirit, pray for me. I do not know what to say.
holdOn: When I do not know what to pray, the Spirit prays for me.
prayer: Holy Spirit, I do not always know how to pray. Help me in my weakness. Pray for me with groans deeper than words. Thank you that I am never praying alone. Amen.
teaser: Paul admitted something about prayer that most of us are afraid to say.

title: Renew Your Mind
verse: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
meaning: Paul tells believers not to be squeezed into the shape of the world. Instead, be transformed by renewing your mind. A new way of thinking leads to a new life and to knowing God's will.
heart: The world pushes its shape on you every day through screens, friends and ads. Change starts in your mind. Replace one lie you believe with God's truth today. Write it down and read it often.
holdOn: I am changed from the inside as God renews my mind.
prayer: God, I do not want to be squeezed into the world's mold. Renew my mind. Replace the lies I believe with your truth, and change me from the inside out. Amen.
teaser: Paul says the world has a mold. Here is how not to be pressed into it.

title: Overcome Evil With Good
verse: Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
meaning: Paul ends a section about living at peace with enemies with this charge. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. Revenge lets evil win. Doing good defeats it.
heart: When someone wrongs you, the natural move is to hit back. That lets evil drag you down. Fight back with good instead. Do one good thing today for someone who has been against you.
holdOn: I will not be beaten by evil. I will beat it with good.
prayer: God, when people wrong me, I want to strike back. Help me fight evil with good instead. Give me creative ways to do good to people who hurt me. Amen.
teaser: Paul told believers how to win a fight without throwing a single punch.

title: The God of Hope
verse: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
meaning: Paul prays a blessing over the church in Rome. He calls God the God of hope. He asks God to fill them with joy and peace as they trust him. Then they will overflow with hope by the Spirit's power.
heart: Hope is not wishful thinking. It is trust in God's character, filled by his Spirit. If you are low on hope today, ask the God of hope to fill you. Then share some of it with someone else.
holdOn: The God of hope fills me with joy and peace as I trust him.
prayer: God of hope, fill me with joy and peace as I trust you. Let your Spirit make me overflow with hope, so I can share it with others who are running low. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave God a title that you might need to hear today.

title: God Is Faithful
verse: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
meaning: Paul wrote to a church full of problems: pride, division and sin. Yet he reminded them that God is faithful. He had called them into friendship with his Son, and he would keep them strong to the end.
heart: Your faith may feel shaky, but God's faithfulness is not. He called you, and he will keep you. On days you feel like a failure as a believer, remember: God is faithful, even when I am not.
holdOn: Even when I am unfaithful, God stays faithful.
prayer: God, thank you that you are faithful even when I am not. You called me into friendship with Jesus. Keep me strong to the end, and help me trust your faithfulness. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote to the messiest church in the Bible. His first words were encouraging.

title: Stand Firm
verse: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
meaning: Paul ends his letter with short commands: watch, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, be strong. The next verse adds the key: let everything you do be done in love. Strength and love go together.
heart: This verse is a call to manhood rooted in faith. Be alert, stay steady, be brave and strong. But do it all in love, not pride. Choose one of the commands and live it on purpose today.
holdOn: I will watch, stand firm, be brave and be strong, all in love.
prayer: God, make me watchful, steady in faith, brave and strong. Keep me from pride and harshness. Let everything I do today flow from love for you and for people. Amen.
teaser: Paul closed a letter with commands that sound like a coach's pregame talk.

title: If God Is for Us
verse: What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
meaning: After showing that nothing can separate believers from God's love, Paul asks a bold question. If God is for us, who can be against us? With God on our side, no enemy has the final say.
heart: You may feel like people, problems or your own past are against you. They are real, but they do not get the last word. Say this verse out loud today, and walk into your day with steady confidence.
holdOn: If God is for me, no one can stand against me for good.
prayer: God, thank you that you are for me, not against me. When I feel surrounded, remind me that you have the final word. Give me steady confidence in your love today. Amen.
teaser: Paul asked a question that ends a lot of fear. Here it is.

title: Run to Win
verse: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, so that you may win.
meaning: Corinth hosted famous athletic games. Paul used that picture. Every runner trains hard and runs to win. Believers should run their race with the same focus, but for a prize that lasts forever.
heart: Athletes train with purpose, not randomly. Bring that same focus to your faith. What is one discipline you can practice daily, like prayer, Scripture or serving? Start training today like you want to win.
holdOn: I run my race for God with focus, like I want to win.
prayer: God, I want to run my race with purpose. Give me the discipline of an athlete, not for a trophy that fades, but for a prize that lasts forever. Help me train today. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote to a city famous for its games. He told believers to run like athletes.

title: Love Endures
verse: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
meaning: In his famous chapter on love, Paul says love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things and endures all things. Real love does not quit when it gets hard.
heart: Many relationships fall apart when they get costly. Real love keeps showing up. Think of a friend or family member you are tempted to give up on. Choose to keep loving them today in one specific way.
holdOn: Real love does not quit when it gets hard.
prayer: God, your love never gives up on me. Teach me to love like that. Help me bear with people, keep hoping for them, and endure when love costs me something. Amen.
teaser: Paul described love with four verbs. Every one of them is about not quitting.

title: Comforted to Comfort
verse: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
meaning: Paul wrote that God comforts us in all our troubles. Then he gave a reason: so we can comfort others with the same comfort we received. Our pain, once comforted, becomes a gift to others.
heart: What you have been through can help someone else. A guy facing what you faced needs to hear from you. Think of one hard thing God helped you through. Who needs that comfort now? Reach out to him.
holdOn: God comforts me so I can comfort others with that same comfort.
prayer: God, thank you for comforting me in my troubles. Use my pain to help others. Show me someone going through what I went through, and help me comfort him well. Amen.
teaser: Paul said God comforts us for a reason beyond ourselves.

title: Treasure in Clay Jars
verse: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
meaning: Paul says believers carry the treasure of the gospel in clay jars, ordinary and breakable. That way it is clear the power comes from God, not from us. Our weakness shows off his strength.
heart: You do not have to be impressive for God to use you. Cracked jars let the light shine out. Stop hiding your weakness today. Let God use it to show his power through you.
holdOn: I am a clay jar, and God's power shines through my cracks.
prayer: God, I am ordinary and breakable. Thank you for putting your treasure in me anyway. Let your power shine through my weakness, and keep me from pretending to be strong on my own. Amen.
teaser: Paul said God stores his greatest treasure in a surprising container.

title: A New Creation
verse: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
meaning: Paul says that anyone who is in Christ is a new creation. The old has gone, and the new has come. Your past does not define you. In Christ, you are made new.
heart: You may still hear old names in your head: failure, loser, addict. In Christ, those are not your names anymore. Write one old label down today, cross it out, and write: new creation.
holdOn: In Christ, I am a new creation. The old has gone.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that in you I am a new creation. Free me from the old labels I still carry. Help me live today as the new man you have made me. Amen.
teaser: Paul made a claim about your past that sounds too good to be true.

title: Grace Is Enough
verse: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
meaning: Paul begged God three times to remove a painful problem he called a thorn. God did not remove it. He told Paul his grace was enough, because his power is made perfect in weakness.
heart: Some struggles do not go away fast, even after prayer. That does not mean God is absent. His grace is enough for today. Bring your thorn to him again, and ask for strength to carry it well.
holdOn: God's grace is enough for me, and his power shows in my weakness.
prayer: God, you know the thorn I live with. I have asked you to remove it. Until you do, let your grace be enough. Show your power in my weakness today. Amen.
teaser: Paul prayed three times for something. God said no, and explained why.

title: Fruit, Not Effort
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
meaning: Paul lists the fruit the Holy Spirit grows in believers: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness and faithfulness, and more. Fruit is not forced. It grows from staying connected to God.
heart: You cannot white-knuckle your way into patience or kindness. Fruit grows slowly from a living connection. Which fruit is weakest in you right now? Ask the Spirit to grow it, and stay close to him today.
holdOn: The Spirit grows his fruit in me as I stay close to him.
prayer: Holy Spirit, grow your fruit in me. I cannot force patience, kindness or joy on my own. Keep me connected to you, and let your character show in my life. Amen.
teaser: Paul described godly character as fruit. That one word changes everything.

title: Carry Each Other's Loads
verse: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
meaning: Paul tells believers to carry each other's burdens. When you help a brother with his heavy load, you fulfill the law of Christ. Love is not a feeling here. It shows up under someone else's weight.
heart: Every man you know is carrying something heavy. Ask a friend today what he is carrying. Then do one thing to help him with it, even if it is just listening and praying with him.
holdOn: When I help carry a brother's load, I fulfill the law of Christ.
prayer: Jesus, you carried my heaviest burden on the cross. Help me carry others' loads. Show me a brother who is struggling, and give me the strength and love to help him. Amen.
teaser: Paul explained the law of Christ in one short sentence about weight.

title: Made for Good Work
verse: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
meaning: Paul says we are God's workmanship, his masterpiece, created in Christ for good works. God prepared those good works ahead of time for us to walk in. You were made on purpose, for a purpose.
heart: You are not saved by good works, but you are saved for them. God has good things for you to do today. Ask him at the start of the day: what good work have you prepared for me? Then watch for it.
holdOn: I am God's workmanship, made on purpose for good work.
prayer: God, thank you that I am your workmanship. Show me the good works you prepared for me today. Help me walk in them with joy and not miss what you have planned. Amen.
teaser: Paul called you a masterpiece. Then he said what you were made for.

title: Forgive Like You Were Forgiven
verse: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
meaning: Paul tells believers to be kind and tenderhearted, forgiving each other. The model is God himself, who forgave us in Christ. We forgive because we have been forgiven so much.
heart: Holding a grudge is like drinking poison and hoping the other guy gets sick. Remember how much God forgave you. Then forgive someone today, even if only in prayer to start.
holdOn: I forgive others because God has forgiven me so much.
prayer: God, you forgave me completely in Christ. Help me forgive the people who hurt me. Make me kind and tenderhearted instead of bitter. Free me from my grudges today. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave the reason for forgiveness in three words: just as God.

title: He Will Finish It
verse: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
meaning: Paul wrote from prison to a church he loved. He was confident that God, who began a good work in them, would keep working until it was finished. God does not abandon projects halfway.
heart: You may feel like a construction site, messy and unfinished. God is not done with you. He started this, and he will finish it. Be patient with your progress today, and trust the builder.
holdOn: God started a good work in me, and he will finish it.
prayer: God, I feel unfinished and messy. Thank you that you began a good work in me and will complete it. Help me trust your timing and keep growing every day. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote from a prison cell with complete confidence about one thing.

title: Strong in the Lord
verse: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might.
meaning: Paul begins his description of God's armor with this command: be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. The strength for spiritual battle does not come from you. It comes from him.
heart: You are in a fight, against temptation, lies and discouragement. Your own strength runs out fast. Be strong in his. Today, before facing your hardest moment, pray this verse and lean on his might.
holdOn: My strength for the fight comes from the Lord, not from me.
prayer: Lord, I am in a fight I cannot win alone. Make me strong in you and in the strength of your might. Arm me for today's battles, and keep me standing. Amen.
teaser: Paul's famous passage about God's armor starts with a single command.

title: To Live Is Christ
verse: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
meaning: Paul wrote from prison, not knowing if he would live or be executed. He said for him, to live is Christ and to die is gain. Living meant serving Jesus. Dying meant being with him.
heart: What would you say completes this sentence: for me, to live is what? Money, fun, success? Paul's answer was a person. Ask yourself honestly today what you live for, and ask Jesus to become the answer.
holdOn: For me, to live is Christ. That is my reason for living.
prayer: Jesus, I want my life to be about you. Free me from living for lesser things. Make you my reason for living, and give me peace about everything ahead. Amen.
teaser: Paul finished a sentence that every man should try finishing honestly.

title: Others First
verse: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
meaning: Paul tells believers to do nothing out of rivalry or pride. Instead, in humility, they should count others as more important than themselves. Selfish ambition destroys teams, friendships and churches.
heart: Competition is fine in sport, but rivalry poisons friendships. Today, put someone else first: let him win the argument, give him credit, or help him succeed. Notice how it frees you.
holdOn: In humility, I can put others first without losing myself.
prayer: God, I am often driven by rivalry and pride. Humble me. Help me count others as more important than myself, and help them succeed with a truly glad heart. Amen.
teaser: Paul named two things that ruin teams. Most of us struggle with both.

title: God at Work in You
verse: For it is God who works in you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.
meaning: Paul tells believers to work out their faith seriously. Then he explains why they can. God is working in them, giving them both the desire and the power to do what pleases him.
heart: Wanting to do right is already a sign that God is at work in you. You do not have to manufacture good desires. Ask God today to strengthen both your desire and your ability to follow him.
holdOn: God works in me, giving me the desire and power to do good.
prayer: God, thank you for working in me. Give me the desire to do what pleases you, and the power to do it. Keep working when I feel weak or unwilling. Amen.
teaser: Paul explained where good desires come from. It is not from you.

title: Forget What Is Behind
verse: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind and stretching forward to the things which are before,
meaning: Paul admits he has not arrived yet. But he does one thing: he forgets what is behind and strains toward what is ahead. Past failures and past wins both stay in the past. He keeps pressing forward.
heart: Some men are stuck on past failures, others on past glory. Both keep you from moving forward. Name one thing from your past you need to let go of today, and take one step toward what is ahead.
holdOn: I forget what is behind and press on toward what is ahead.
prayer: God, I keep looking back at my failures and my old wins. Help me let go of both. Give me focus and strength to press forward toward what you have ahead. Amen.
teaser: Paul admitted he had not arrived. Then he named the one thing he did.

title: Citizens of Heaven
verse: For our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
meaning: Philippi was a Roman colony, proud of Roman citizenship. Paul told the believers there that their true citizenship was in heaven. They lived on earth, but they belonged to God's kingdom and waited for their King.
heart: Your passport says one country, but your deepest loyalty belongs to another. That changes how you treat money, status and politics. Today, make one choice that shows your citizenship is in heaven.
holdOn: My true citizenship is in heaven, and I live like it here.
prayer: Jesus, my true home is with you. Help me live on earth as a citizen of heaven. Loosen my grip on things that will not last, and keep me waiting for you. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote to a city proud of its passports. He told them about a better one.

title: Strength for Anything
verse: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
meaning: This verse is often quoted by athletes. But Paul wrote it about contentment. He had learned to be content with plenty and with nothing, hungry or full. Christ gave him strength to handle every situation.
heart: This verse is not a promise to win every game. It is a promise that Christ can carry you through anything, including losing. Whatever today brings, much or little, ask Christ for strength to be content.
holdOn: Through Christ, I can face anything, whether I have much or little.
prayer: Jesus, teach me the secret of contentment. Whether I have plenty or not enough, give me your strength. Help me face whatever comes today with you, not with panic. Amen.
teaser: This is one of the most quoted verses in sports. Most people miss what it means.

title: Pray Instead of Worry
verse: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
meaning: Paul says not to be anxious about anything. Instead, bring everything to God in prayer, with thanks. He is not saying problems are fake. He is saying where to take them.
heart: Worry replays the problem in your head. Prayer hands it to God. Make a list of your worries today. Turn each one into a short prayer, and add one thing you are thankful for.
holdOn: Instead of worrying, I bring everything to God with thanks.
prayer: God, I worry about too many things. I bring them all to you now, one by one. Thank you for what you have already done. Take my anxiety and give me your peace. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave a simple swap for anxiety. It takes about two minutes.

title: Think About These Things
verse: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report: if there is any virtue and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
meaning: Paul lists what believers should fill their minds with: things that are true, honorable, just, pure, lovely and worthy of praise. What you think about, day after day, shapes who you become.
heart: Your mind is like a garden. What you plant grows. If you fill it with junk, junk grows. Check what you watched, read and scrolled yesterday. Today, feed your mind one thing from Paul's list.
holdOn: I fill my mind with what is true, pure and good.
prayer: God, guard my mind. Help me think about what is true, honorable, pure and good. Show me what junk I need to cut out, and fill me with what is worthy of praise. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave believers a filter for their thoughts. Your feed probably fails it.

title: Endurance With Joy
verse: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with joy,
meaning: Paul prayed that believers would be strengthened with all power, by God's glorious might. The goal was not flashy miracles. It was endurance and patience, and doing it with joy.
heart: Sometimes the most powerful thing God does is help you keep going. Endurance with joy is a sign of his strength. Ask God today for power to endure one hard thing, and to do it with a good attitude.
holdOn: God's power in me shows up as endurance with joy.
prayer: God, strengthen me with your power, not for show, but to endure. Help me keep going through hard things with patience and joy. Let your might carry me today. Amen.
teaser: Paul prayed for God's power. What he wanted it for might surprise you.

title: Holding It All Together
verse: He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.
meaning: Paul describes Jesus as before all things. In him all things hold together. The same Jesus who created the universe keeps it from falling apart, moment by moment, every day.
heart: When your life feels like it is falling apart, remember who holds things together. Jesus holds the universe and your life. Bring him the part of your life that feels like it is coming apart today.
holdOn: Jesus holds all things together, including my life.
prayer: Jesus, you hold the whole universe together. Hold my life together too. When things feel like they are falling apart, remind me that you are still holding on to me. Amen.
teaser: Paul said something holds the universe together. He named him.

title: Walk in Him
verse: As therefore you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
meaning: Paul says that just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, keep walking in him. Faith is not a one-time event. The way you started, by trusting him, is the way you keep going every day.
heart: Some men had a big moment with God years ago and have coasted since. Walking is daily. What does walking with Jesus look like today? Take one step: pray, read or obey one thing he said.
holdOn: I received Jesus by faith, and I keep walking with him daily.
prayer: Jesus, I received you as my Lord. Help me keep walking in you every day, not coasting on old moments. Keep me trusting you step by step, starting today. Amen.
teaser: Some men met God once and coasted ever since. Paul had a word for them.

title: Work as for the Lord
verse: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men,
meaning: Paul wrote to believers, many of them servants and laborers. He told them to work hard from the heart, as if working for the Lord, not for people. God sees and rewards faithful work.
heart: Your boss, coach or teacher may not notice your effort. God does. Whatever job you have today, even the boring parts, do it with your whole heart as if Jesus were your boss.
holdOn: Whatever I do, I work with my whole heart, for the Lord.
prayer: Lord, help me work with my whole heart today, for you and not for applause. Make even boring tasks an act of worship. Thank you that you see faithful work. Amen.
teaser: Paul told workers who their real boss is. It changes how you clock in.

title: Dress for the Day
verse: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
meaning: Paul tells believers to put on kindness, a soft heart, humility and patience, like putting on clothes each day. They do this because they are God's chosen people, holy and dearly loved.
heart: You get dressed every morning without thinking. Character is also something you put on daily. Before you leave the house today, choose one quality from Paul's list to wear on purpose.
holdOn: Because I am loved, I put on kindness, humility and patience.
prayer: God, thank you that I am chosen and dearly loved. Help me put on kindness, a soft heart, humility and patience today, like clothes. Let people see your character in me. Amen.
teaser: Paul told believers what to wear. It was not about clothes.

title: Let Peace Make the Call
verse: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
meaning: Paul says to let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts. The word rule meant to umpire, like a referee who makes the call. When you face a decision, let Christ's peace make the call.
heart: In decisions and arguments, what makes the call in your heart: fear, pride or anger? Let Christ's peace be the referee today. If something takes your peace away, step back and pray.
holdOn: I let the peace of Christ make the calls in my heart.
prayer: Jesus, let your peace rule my heart like a referee. When fear or anger try to make the call, let your peace speak louder. And make me thankful today. Amen.
teaser: Paul used a sports word to describe how peace should work in your heart.

title: Let the Word Live in You
verse: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
meaning: Paul tells believers to let the word of Christ live in them richly. As it fills them, they teach and encourage each other, even through songs, with thankful hearts toward God.
heart: The word should not just visit you once a week. It should move in and live there. Memorize one verse this week. Then share it with a friend who needs encouragement.
holdOn: I want the word of Christ to live in me richly, not just visit.
prayer: Jesus, let your word live in me richly. Fill my mind and heart with it. Help me use it to encourage my friends, and give me a thankful heart. Amen.
teaser: Paul said God's word should live in you, not just visit you now and then.

title: Seasoned With Salt
verse: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
meaning: Paul says our speech should always be full of grace and seasoned with salt. Salt adds flavor and keeps food from going bad. Gracious, wise words make conversations better and help us answer people well.
heart: Your words can be bland, bitter or seasoned with grace. Before you reply to someone today, especially someone who disagrees with you, add some grace. Be honest, but be kind too.
holdOn: I want my words to be full of grace and seasoned with salt.
prayer: God, season my words with grace. Help me speak honestly but kindly, especially to people I disagree with. Give me wisdom to know how to answer each person well. Amen.
teaser: Paul compared good conversation to cooking. Here is his secret ingredient.

title: Faith That Works
verse: remembering without ceasing your work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father.
meaning: Paul remembered the believers in Thessalonica for three things. Their faith produced work, their love drove labor, and their hope in Jesus kept them going. Their faith was visible in what they did.
heart: Faith, love and hope are not just feelings. They produce work, labor and endurance. What does your faith produce? Do one piece of work today that comes directly from your faith.
holdOn: My faith works, my love labors and my hope endures.
prayer: God, let my faith produce real work, my love real effort, and my hope real endurance. Make my faith visible in what I do today, not just in what I say. Amen.
teaser: Paul remembered one church for three things. Each was faith turned into action.

title: More Than Words
verse: Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
meaning: Paul told the believers that he loved them so much he shared not only the gospel but his own life with them. They had become very dear to him. Real ministry is shared life, not just words.
heart: People rarely remember sermons, but they remember who showed up. Share your life with someone, not just your opinions. Invite a younger guy to hang out, eat together, and let him see how you live.
holdOn: Real love shares my whole life, not just my words.
prayer: God, make me a man who shares his life, not just his words. Show me someone to invest in. Help me open my home, my time and my heart to him. Amen.
teaser: Paul said he gave believers more than the gospel. He gave them himself.

title: Overflowing Love
verse: May the Lord make you to increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all men, even as we also do toward you,
meaning: Paul prayed that the Lord would make their love increase and overflow for each other and for everyone. He wanted love that keeps growing and spills over to people outside the church too.
heart: Love that is kept inside a small circle stays small. Let yours overflow today. Do something kind for someone outside your usual group, someone you would normally walk past and ignore.
holdOn: I ask God to make my love grow and overflow to everyone.
prayer: Lord, make my love grow and overflow. Let it spill past my small circle to everyone around me. Show me someone outside my group to love well today, on purpose. Amen.
teaser: Paul prayed for a kind of love that does not stay in its lane.

title: A Quiet, Working Life
verse: and that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you,
meaning: Paul told believers to aim to live a quiet life, mind their own business and work with their hands. In a world of drama and noise, steady work and a calm life are honorable.
heart: Drama, gossip and online fights eat time and peace. Paul's ambition was quieter: honest work and a calm life. Today, skip one piece of drama, and put that energy into real work instead.
holdOn: A quiet life of honest work is a worthy ambition.
prayer: God, make my ambition a quiet, honest life. Help me stay out of drama and gossip. Give me pride in good work with my hands and mind, done for you. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave a surprising goal for ambitious men: a quiet life.

title: Build Each Other Up
verse: Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.
meaning: Paul told believers to encourage one another and build each other up. Words can tear down or build up. Building up is a choice and a skill that grows with practice.
heart: Many guys trade insults as a way of bonding, but too much of it tears people down. Today, give a real compliment to a friend. Tell him one thing you respect about him.
holdOn: I use my words to build my brothers up, not tear them down.
prayer: God, make me an encourager. Help me notice what is good in others and say it out loud. Use my words today to build up my friends and family. Amen.
teaser: Guys often bond by tearing each other down. Paul gave a better way.

title: Thanks in Everything
verse: In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
meaning: Paul says to give thanks in every situation, because this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus. He does not say thank God for everything bad. He says to give thanks while you are in it.
heart: Gratitude in hard times is not pretending. It is finding what is still good. Even on a rough day, there is something to thank God for. Write down three things you are grateful for before bed tonight.
holdOn: In every situation, I can find something to thank God for.
prayer: God, help me give thanks in every situation, not just the good ones. Open my eyes to what is still good today. Make gratitude a habit in my heart. Amen.
teaser: Paul did not say thank God for everything. Read it closely.

title: He Will Do It
verse: He who calls you is faithful, who will also do it.
meaning: Paul prayed that God would make the believers holy through and through. Then he gave them confidence: the one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it. Their growth depended on God's faithfulness.
heart: You may doubt you can ever change. Good news: your growth does not depend only on you. God called you, and he is faithful to finish it. Trust him with your change today, and take one step with him.
holdOn: The one who called me is faithful, and he will do it.
prayer: God, I doubt I can really change sometimes. Thank you that you are faithful. You called me, and you will do it. Make me holy through and through, day by day. Amen.
teaser: Paul ended a big prayer with six words that take the pressure off.

title: Growing Under Pressure
verse: We are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds,
meaning: Paul thanked God because the believers' faith was growing more and more, and their love for each other was increasing. They were under real pressure, yet they kept on growing.
heart: Pressure can either crush you or grow you. Look back at the last year. Has your faith grown? Has your love grown? Thank God for any growth, and ask him for more this year.
holdOn: Under pressure, my faith and love can still grow.
prayer: God, thank you for any growth in my faith and love. Let pressure grow me instead of crush me. Keep my faith growing and my love increasing this year. Amen.
teaser: This church was under heavy pressure. Paul thanked God for what was happening anyway.

title: Eternal Comfort, Good Hope
verse: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
meaning: Paul prays that Jesus and God our Father, who loved us, would encourage the believers. God has given us eternal comfort and good hope through grace. Our hope is not earned. It is a gift.
heart: If you feel discouraged, remember that your hope is a gift from a Father who loves you. It does not depend on your performance. Ask God today to encourage your heart and strengthen you for good work.
holdOn: God gave me eternal comfort and good hope, as a gift of grace.
prayer: Father, you loved me and gave me eternal comfort and good hope. Thank you that it is a gift. Encourage my heart today, and strengthen me for every good work. Amen.
teaser: Paul described two gifts from God. Neither one can be earned.

title: Do Not Grow Tired
verse: But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
meaning: Some believers in Thessalonica had stopped working and were living off others. Paul told the rest: brothers, do not grow tired of doing what is right. Keep working, keep giving, keep doing good.
heart: Doing right gets tiring when others are slacking or taking advantage. Do not let them change you. Keep doing the right thing today, even if it feels like no one else is.
holdOn: I will not grow tired of doing what is right.
prayer: God, I get tired of doing right when others do not. Give me strength to keep going. Keep me from becoming bitter, and help me do good again today. Amen.
teaser: Some men were slacking and living off others. Paul spoke to the ones still working.

title: The Worst of Sinners
verse: The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
meaning: Paul, who once hunted and jailed Christians, wrote that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. Then he added: of whom I am the worst. If God saved Paul, no one is beyond his grace.
heart: You may think your past is too dark for God. Paul's was darker. Jesus came for sinners, not for people who have it together. Thank God today that his grace reached you too.
holdOn: If Jesus could save Paul, no one is beyond his grace.
prayer: Jesus, you came to save sinners, and I am one. Thank you that my past is not too dark for your grace. Help me live grateful and humble today. Amen.
teaser: A man who once jailed Christians called himself the worst sinner. Here is why.

title: Train for Godliness
verse: For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now and of that which is to come.
meaning: Paul told Timothy that physical training has some value. But training in godliness is valuable in every way. It helps in this life and also in the life to come.
heart: Hitting the gym is good. Paul does not knock it. But your soul needs training too. Match your workout today with a spiritual rep: read a passage, pray, or serve someone.
holdOn: My body needs training, and so does my soul.
prayer: God, thank you for my body and the strength to train it. Help me train my soul even more. Build godliness in me that lasts in this life and the next. Amen.
teaser: Paul compared the gym to something with even better returns.

title: Man of God
verse: But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
meaning: Paul called Timothy a man of God. He told him to flee the love of money and the pride he had just described. Instead, pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance and gentleness.
heart: A man of God knows when to run and when to chase. Run from greed and pride. Chase character. Which of Paul's six things will you pursue today? Pick one and go after it on purpose.
holdOn: As a man of God, I flee what is wrong and chase what is good.
prayer: God, make me a man of God. Help me run from greed, pride and lust. Help me chase righteousness, faith, love, endurance and gentleness with all my heart and strength. Amen.
teaser: Paul called Timothy a man of God. Then he told him what to run from and run to.

title: Contentment Is Gain
verse: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
meaning: Paul warns about people who think godliness is a way to get rich. He says godliness with contentment is great gain. We brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out.
heart: Ads are designed to make you feel like you need more. Contentment is a quiet rebellion against that. Today, resist one purchase you do not need, and thank God for what you already have.
holdOn: Godliness with contentment is real gain, worth more than money.
prayer: God, free me from always wanting more. Teach me contentment. Help me be grateful for what I have, and find my real gain in you, not in things I buy. Amen.
teaser: Paul named the best investment you can make. It does not involve money.

title: Rich in Good Works
verse: that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share;
meaning: Paul told Timothy to instruct the rich to do good, be rich in good works, and be generous and ready to share. Wealth is a tool to help others, not just something to keep.
heart: You may not feel rich, but compared to most of history, you probably are. Be rich in good works. Share something today: money, time or a skill, with someone who needs it.
holdOn: I want to be rich in good works, not just in money.
prayer: God, everything I have is from you. Make me rich in good works and generous with what I own. Show me someone to share with today, gladly and freely. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave rich people a job description. You might qualify more than you think.

title: Not a Spirit of Fear
verse: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
meaning: Timothy was young and timid, leading a church under pressure. Paul reminded him that God did not give us a spirit of fear. He gave us a spirit of power, love and self-control.
heart: Fear is not from God. When you feel timid today, remember what God has put in you. He gave you power to act, love to move you, and self-control to steady you. Do one brave thing you have been avoiding.
holdOn: God gave me a spirit of power, love and self-control, not fear.
prayer: God, I feel timid and afraid sometimes. Thank you that you gave me power, love and self-control. Help me act with courage today in the thing I have been avoiding. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote to a timid young leader. He reminded him what was really inside him.

title: Run From It
verse: Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
meaning: Paul told young Timothy to flee youthful lusts. Do not stand around and negotiate with temptation. Run. Then pursue what is good, and do it alongside others who call on the Lord with a pure heart.
heart: Some temptations you cannot fight; you have to run from them. Know your danger spots: certain apps, places or late nights alone. Make a plan today to leave fast, and find a brother to run with.
holdOn: Some temptations I do not fight. I run, and I run with brothers.
prayer: God, give me the wisdom to run from temptation instead of flirting with it. Show me my danger spots. Surround me with brothers who chase purity with me, and keep my heart clean. Amen.
teaser: Paul gave young Timothy advice about lust that is simple: do not stay and fight.

title: He Remains Faithful
verse: If we are faithless, he remains faithful; for he can’t deny himself.”
meaning: Paul quoted an early Christian saying. If we are faithless, he remains faithful, because he cannot deny himself. God's faithfulness is not based on our performance. It is part of who he is.
heart: On days you blow it, you may think God has given up on you. He has not. His faithfulness does not swing with your mood or your record. Rest in that today, and get back up.
holdOn: Even when I am faithless, God remains faithful to me.
prayer: God, I am not always faithful to you. Thank you that you remain faithful to me, because that is who you are. Hold me when I slip, and help me get back up quickly. Amen.
teaser: Paul quoted an early Christian saying. Its last line is a huge relief.

title: God-Breathed
verse: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
meaning: Paul tells Timothy that all Scripture is breathed out by God. It is useful for teaching truth, showing what is wrong, correcting it, and training us to live right. The Bible is God's training manual.
heart: The Bible is not just old stories. It teaches, corrects and trains. Let it correct you, not just inspire you. Read today's verse again and ask: what does this correct in me?
holdOn: God breathed out Scripture to teach, correct and train me.
prayer: God, thank you for your word, breathed out by you. Let it teach me, show me where I am wrong, correct me and train me to live right. Help me listen to it, not just read it. Amen.
teaser: Paul said Scripture does four things. Most of us only let it do one.

title: Finish Well
verse: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
meaning: Near the end of his life, waiting for execution, Paul looked back. He said: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. He wanted to finish strong.
heart: Many men start strong and fade. Paul finished. Think about the man you want to be at the end of your life. What would need to change now for you to say these same words then?
holdOn: I want to fight the good fight, finish my race and keep the faith.
prayer: God, I want to finish well. Help me fight the good fight, run my race to the end and keep the faith when it is hard. Shape me now into the man who finishes strong. Amen.
teaser: Paul wrote his last letter from prison. He summed up his life in three short lines.

title: Grace Has Appeared
verse: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
meaning: Paul tells Titus that the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people. Grace is not just an idea. It showed up in a person, Jesus, and it changes how we live.
heart: Grace is not only forgiveness for the past. In the next verse, Paul says grace trains us to say no to ungodliness. Let grace train you today: say no to one wrong thing because you are loved.
holdOn: God's grace has appeared in Jesus, and it trains me to live right.
prayer: God, thank you that your grace appeared in Jesus to save me. Let your grace also train me. Help me say no to what is wrong and yes to what is right today. Amen.
teaser: Paul said grace does more than forgive. It also does something you may not expect.

title: Kindness Appeared
verse: But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
meaning: Paul describes the moment God's kindness and love for people appeared. He saved us not because of good things we did, but because of his mercy. God's love made the first move.
heart: You did not earn God's kindness. It came to you first. When you feel unworthy today, remember that God's love made the first move toward you. Then make the first move of kindness toward someone else.
holdOn: God's kindness came to me first, not because I earned it.
prayer: God my Savior, thank you that your kindness and love appeared to me when I did not deserve it. Save me by your mercy, and help me show that same kindness to others today. Amen.
teaser: Paul described the moment God's kindness showed up. It was not a reward.

title: A Word for Younger Men
verse: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded.
meaning: Paul gave Titus instructions for every group in the church. For younger men, his message was short and direct: be sober-minded, self-controlled and clear-headed. The next verse says to set a good example in everything.
heart: Out of everything Paul could say to young men, he chose self-control. It covers anger, desire, spending, screens and speech. Pick one area where you lack control, and set one simple rule for it this week.
holdOn: As a young man, I choose self-control and a clear head.
prayer: God, you know where I lack self-control. Give me a sober and clear mind. Help me set a good example in how I act, speak and spend my time this week. Amen.
teaser: Paul had one main instruction for younger men. It was only a few words long.

title: You Refresh People
verse: For we have much joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
meaning: Paul told his friend Philemon that his love had brought great joy and comfort. Philemon had refreshed the hearts of many believers. Some men leave people drained. Philemon left them refreshed.
heart: Do people leave time with you feeling drained or refreshed? You can choose to refresh. Listen well, encourage, help out. Be the guy who leaves people better than he found them today.
holdOn: I want to refresh the hearts of the people around me.
prayer: Lord, make me someone who refreshes others, not someone who drains them. Fill me with your love, so I can pour it out. Show me whose heart needs refreshing today. Amen.
teaser: Paul told a friend one thing about him that every man should want said about himself.

title: He Was Tempted Too
verse: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
meaning: Hebrews says that Jesus himself suffered when he was tempted. Because he knows what temptation feels like, he is able to help those who are being tempted. He is not shocked by your struggle.
heart: Jesus felt the pull of temptation and never gave in. He gets it. When you are tempted today, do not hide from him in shame. Run to him immediately and say: you know this, help me.
holdOn: Jesus knows what temptation feels like, and he helps me in it.
prayer: Jesus, you were tempted and you understand my struggle. When temptation hits today, help me run to you, not away from you. Give me your strength in the moment I need it. Amen.
teaser: Jesus knows exactly how temptation feels. That changes who you run to.

title: Come Boldly
verse: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
meaning: Because Jesus understands our weakness, Hebrews invites us to come boldly to God's throne of grace. There we receive mercy and find grace to help us right when we need it.
heart: Shame makes you hesitate before God. Grace invites you to come boldly. You do not need to clean up first or use fancy words. Walk right in today, in prayer, and ask for the help you need.
holdOn: I can come boldly to God's throne and find help when I need it.
prayer: God, I come boldly to your throne of grace, not because I am good, but because Jesus opened the way. I need mercy and help today. Thank you for welcoming me. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews invites you to approach God in a way that might surprise you: boldly.

title: Anchor for the Soul
verse: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,
meaning: Hebrews describes our hope in God's promises as an anchor for the soul. It is sure and steady. Like an anchor in a storm, it keeps us from drifting or being smashed on the rocks.
heart: Storms do not ask permission before hitting your life. Your anchor matters more than the weather. Is your hope anchored in God's promises or in things going well? Tie your soul to his promises today.
holdOn: My hope in God is an anchor that holds my soul steady.
prayer: God, be the anchor of my soul. When storms hit and I start to drift, hold me steady. Let my hope rest in your promises, not in how things are going. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews compares hope to a piece of ship's equipment. It is a good picture.

title: Hold Fast
verse: let’s hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful.
meaning: Hebrews urges believers to hold tightly to the hope they confess, without wavering. The reason is not that we are strong. It is that the one who promised is faithful. He will keep his word.
heart: When doubts come, you do not have to let go. Hold fast, not because your grip is perfect, but because God is faithful. Say your faith out loud today, even if your feelings are shaky.
holdOn: I hold fast to my hope, because the one who promised is faithful.
prayer: God, my grip on faith feels weak some days. Help me hold fast without wavering. Thank you that you are faithful to your promises, even when I am not strong. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews tells you to hold on. Then it gives a reason that has nothing to do with you.

title: Spur Each Other On
verse: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
meaning: Hebrews tells believers to think about how to stir one another up to love and good works. The next verse says not to give up meeting together. Faith grows when brothers push each other forward.
heart: Good friends push you toward good, like a training partner. Think about one friend today. How can you spur him on? Invite him to church, encourage a good decision, or do something good together.
holdOn: I think about how to push my brothers toward love and good works.
prayer: God, give me brothers who push me toward good, and make me that kind of brother. Show me how to spur a friend on today toward love and good works. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews asks you to plan something most of us never do: pushing friends toward good.

title: Sure of What You Cannot See
verse: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
meaning: Hebrews defines faith as being sure of what we hope for and certain of what we do not see. Then it lists people like Noah, Abraham and Moses, who trusted God before they saw the outcome.
heart: Faith does not mean you have no questions. It means you trust God's promises even before you see them come true. What are you trusting God for that you cannot see yet? Keep trusting him today.
holdOn: Faith is being sure of God's promises before I see them.
prayer: God, I want faith like Noah, Abraham and Moses. Help me trust your promises even when I cannot see how they will come true. Make me sure of what I hope for in you. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews gives the Bible's clearest definition of faith. Then it tells real stories.

title: Drop the Weight
verse: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
meaning: After listing heroes of faith, Hebrews pictures them as a crowd cheering us on. It tells us to throw off every weight and the sin that tangles us, and run our race with endurance.
heart: Runners do not race in boots and backpacks. Some things in your life are not sin, just weight that slows you down. Name one weight and one sin that trip you up. Drop one of them today.
holdOn: I throw off what slows me down and run my race with endurance.
prayer: God, show me the weights and sins that slow me down. Help me throw them off. Let me run my race with endurance, knowing others have run before me and cheer me on. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews pictures a stadium full of fans. Then it tells you what to take off first.

title: Discipline Pays Off
verse: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
meaning: Hebrews admits that discipline never feels good at the time. It is painful. But later it produces a peaceful harvest of right living for those who have been trained by it.
heart: Every coach knows training hurts. Correction from God, parents or mentors stings too. Do not quit when it hurts. Think of one hard correction you are facing, and ask what God is training in you.
holdOn: Discipline hurts now, but it produces peace and right living later.
prayer: God, I do not like discipline. It hurts. Help me trust that you are training me. Let the hard lessons I am learning now produce a peaceful harvest in my life later. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews admits that discipline feels terrible. Then it describes the payoff.

title: Free From the Love of Money
verse: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
meaning: Hebrews tells believers to keep their lives free from the love of money and to be content with what they have. The reason is a promise: God said he will never leave us or forsake us.
heart: The love of money promises security, but it never delivers enough. God's presence is your real security. Today, when you feel anxious about money, remember his promise: I will never leave you.
holdOn: I can be content, because God will never leave me.
prayer: God, free me from the love of money. Help me be content with what I have. Thank you for your promise never to leave me or forsake me. Be my real security. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews gave a cure for loving money. It is a promise, not a budget.

title: Do Good and Share
verse: But don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
meaning: Hebrews ends with simple instructions for daily life. One is this: do not forget to do good and to share what you have. These sacrifices please God, just like worship does.
heart: It is easy to forget to do good when life is busy. Put a reminder on your phone today to do one good thing and share one thing with someone. Small sacrifices please God.
holdOn: Doing good and sharing are sacrifices that please God.
prayer: God, I forget to do good when I am busy. Remind me today. Help me share what I have and do good for someone, as an act of worship that pleases you. Amen.
teaser: Hebrews says God is pleased by a kind of sacrifice anyone can make today.

title: Ask for Wisdom
verse: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
meaning: James says if anyone lacks wisdom, he should ask God. God gives generously to all and does not scold people for asking. Wisdom is a gift God loves to give.
heart: Many men hate asking for directions. God does not scold you for needing wisdom. What decision are you stuck on? Ask God for wisdom about it today, specifically, and then look for his answer.
holdOn: When I lack wisdom, I can ask God, and he gives generously.
prayer: God, I need wisdom for the decisions in front of me. Thank you that you give generously and do not scold me for asking. Give me wisdom today, and help me follow it. Amen.
teaser: James says God answers one kind of prayer generously, without any scolding.

title: The Crown of Life
verse: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.
meaning: James says the man who keeps going under trial and temptation is blessed. When he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life God has promised to those who love him.
heart: Temptation is a test, not a death sentence. Every time you hold the line, you grow stronger. Remember the prize. When temptation hits today, picture the crown of life, and stand firm one more time.
holdOn: Every time I endure temptation, I move closer to the crown of life.
prayer: God, give me strength to endure temptation. When I am tested today, help me stand firm. Remind me of the crown of life you promise to those who love you. Amen.
teaser: James describes a prize for men who hold the line under temptation.

title: Every Good Gift
verse: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.
meaning: James says every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights. Unlike the sun, which moves and casts shifting shadows, God does not change. His goodness is steady.
heart: Every good thing in your life has a source. Make a list today of five good gifts you have: people, abilities, chances. Thank the Father of lights for each one by name.
holdOn: Every good gift in my life comes from my unchanging Father.
prayer: Father of lights, thank you for every good gift in my life. Thank you that you never change. Help me notice your gifts today and thank you for each one. Amen.
teaser: James called God the Father of lights. Then he said how God differs from the sun.

title: Swift to Hear
verse: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
meaning: James gives three short instructions to his brothers: be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to get angry. Most conflicts would shrink if men followed this simple order.
heart: Most of us reverse it: quick to speak, quick to anger, slow to listen. Flip it today. In your next disagreement, listen fully, pause before you answer, and keep your temper.
holdOn: I want to be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger.
prayer: God, I talk too fast and get angry too quickly. Make me quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger. Help me practice this in my next hard conversation. Amen.
teaser: James gave three instructions in one sentence. Most men do them in reverse.

title: Doers, Not Just Hearers
verse: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
meaning: James warns that hearing God's word without doing it is self-deception. He compares it to looking in a mirror and then forgetting what you look like. The word is meant to be lived.
heart: You have read many lessons. How many changed something you do? Look back at one lesson from this month. What did it ask you to do? Do it today, not someday.
holdOn: I do not just hear the word. I put it into action.
prayer: God, I do not want to fool myself by only hearing your word. Help me do what it says. Show me one thing I have heard but not done, and give me courage to do it today. Amen.
teaser: James compared hearing without doing to a strange habit with a mirror.

title: No Favorites
verse: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
meaning: James rebuked believers who gave the best seats to rich visitors and pushed poor people aside. He said faith in the Lord Jesus does not fit with playing favorites. Jesus treats people the same.
heart: We all play favorites: by money, looks, popularity or usefulness. Watch how you treat people today. Give the same respect to the janitor as to the boss, and to the outsider as to the cool guy.
holdOn: Faith in Jesus means I do not play favorites with people.
prayer: Lord Jesus, forgive me for playing favorites. Help me treat every person with the same respect, rich or poor, liked or left out. Let my faith show in how fair I am today. Amen.
teaser: James caught a church doing something most of us do without noticing.

title: Faith That Shows
verse: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
meaning: James says faith without works is dead. He is not saying works earn salvation. He is saying real faith always shows up in action. A faith that changes nothing is not alive.
heart: If your faith never changes how you spend your time, money or words, ask if it is alive. Let your faith move today. Do one specific thing because you believe Jesus, not just think about him.
holdOn: Living faith always shows up in what I do.
prayer: God, I do not want a dead faith. Make my faith alive and active. Show me how to put it into action today in how I treat people and use my time. Amen.
teaser: James said one kind of faith is dead. Here is how to tell if yours is alive.

title: Wisdom From Above
verse: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
meaning: James describes the wisdom that comes from God. It is pure, peaceful, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruit, fair and sincere. Godly wisdom has a recognizable character.
heart: Some wisdom sounds smart but is harsh, proud or fake. God's wisdom is gentle and sincere. Before you give advice or make a call today, check it against James' list. Does it look like heaven?
holdOn: Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle and full of mercy.
prayer: God, give me wisdom from above, not just clever thinking. Make my wisdom pure, peaceful, gentle and merciful. Let my advice and my decisions look like you today and always. Amen.
teaser: James described how to recognize wisdom that comes from God. It has a clear look.

title: Draw Near
verse: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
meaning: James gives a promise and a challenge. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Then he adds: clean your hands and purify your hearts, you who are double-minded. Closeness and cleaning go together.
heart: God is not playing hard to get. When you move toward him, he moves toward you. Take one step closer today: a few minutes of prayer, confession of a known sin, or reading his word slowly.
holdOn: When I draw near to God, he draws near to me.
prayer: God, I want to be close to you. I draw near now. Clean my hands and purify my divided heart. Thank you for your promise to draw near to me too. Amen.
teaser: James made a promise about closeness to God. It starts with your move.

title: Pray in Trouble, Sing in Joy
verse: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
meaning: James asks two quick questions. Is anyone suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise. Every mood is a reason to turn toward God, the bad days and the good.
heart: Many men only pray when things go wrong, or only when things go right. James covers both. Whatever your mood today, turn it toward God: pray if it is rough, praise if it is good.
holdOn: In trouble I pray, and in joy I sing praise. Every mood turns to God.
prayer: God, I want to turn to you in every mood. When I suffer, I will pray. When I am glad, I will praise you. Thank you for being with me on good days and bad days. Amen.
teaser: James asked two quick questions that cover every mood you will ever have.

title: Confess to a Brother
verse: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
meaning: James tells believers to confess their sins to one another and pray for one another, so they may be healed. Secrets keep us sick. The prayers of a righteous person are powerful and they work.
heart: Confessing to God is vital. But James says something many men avoid: confess to each other too. Hidden struggles grow in the dark. Find one trusted brother this week and tell him what you are fighting.
holdOn: When I confess to a trusted brother, healing can begin.
prayer: God, I keep some struggles hidden even from my friends. Give me the courage to confess to a trusted brother. Let us pray for each other and find healing together. Amen.
teaser: James said one thing helps men heal that most of us never do.

title: A Living Hope
verse: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
meaning: Peter praises God for his great mercy. Through Jesus rising from the dead, God gave believers a new birth into a living hope. Their hope is alive because Jesus is alive.
heart: Some hopes die: a team, a plan, a relationship. Your hope in Jesus cannot die, because he is alive. When you feel hopeless today, remember the empty tomb. Your hope has a pulse.
holdOn: My hope is alive because Jesus rose from the dead.
prayer: God, thank you for your great mercy. Because Jesus rose, my hope is alive. When other hopes die, let this living hope hold me up and fill me with joy. Amen.
teaser: Peter called hope living. He explained why it cannot die.

title: A Roaring Lion
verse: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
meaning: Peter warns believers to be sober and alert. The devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour. Lions pick off the weak and the isolated. Peter wanted men awake.
heart: Lions hunt the one who drifts from the herd and the one who is not paying attention. Stay alert and stay close to your brothers. Where are you drifting or tired right now? Get back close today.
holdOn: I stay alert and close to my brothers, because the enemy hunts the isolated.
prayer: God, keep me sober and alert. Show me where I am drifting from you and from my brothers. Protect me from the enemy, and keep me close where I am safe. Amen.
teaser: Peter compared the enemy to a hunting lion. Lions have a favorite kind of prey.

title: Chosen
verse: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
meaning: Peter wrote to scattered believers who felt like outsiders. He told them they were a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own possession. Their identity came from God, not the crowd.
heart: The world may treat you like an outsider for your faith. Do not let that define you. God calls you chosen, royal and his own. Walk into today knowing who you are, and point others to his light.
holdOn: I am chosen, royal and God's own possession.
prayer: God, thank you that I am chosen and that I belong to you. When I feel like an outsider, remind me who I am. Help me point others to your marvelous light today. Amen.
teaser: Peter wrote to people who felt like outsiders. He gave them four new titles.

title: Brotherly Love
verse: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous,
meaning: Peter sums up how believers should live together. Be of one mind and show sympathy. Love each other as brothers, and be tenderhearted and humble. Strong communities are built on these qualities.
heart: Love as brothers. That means loyalty, honesty and showing up. It also means a tender heart, which is not weakness. Be humble and kind with your friends today, even when banter would be easier.
holdOn: I love my brothers with loyalty, honesty and a tender heart.
prayer: God, help me love my brothers well. Give me sympathy, a tender heart and humility. Make my friendships strong, honest and kind, so they reflect your love to others. Amen.
teaser: Peter listed what makes a band of brothers strong. Some items might surprise you.

title: Love Covers
verse: And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.
meaning: Peter tells believers that above all, they should keep loving each other deeply. Love covers a multitude of sins. It does not keep a record of every wrong, and it forgives quickly.
heart: Friendships break over small offenses that pile up. Love lets things go. Is there a minor offense you keep holding against a friend? Choose to cover it with love today and move forward.
holdOn: Deep love covers many sins and does not keep score.
prayer: God, you cover my sins with your love. Help me love my friends deeply enough to let small offenses go. Free me from keeping score, and help me forgive quickly. Amen.
teaser: Peter said one thing above all others. It is about what love does with mistakes.

title: Use Your Gift
verse: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.
meaning: Peter says each believer has received a gift from God. Use it to serve others, as a good manager of God's grace. Your gifts are not just for you. They are meant to bless people.
heart: Maybe you are good with tools, numbers, music, sports or listening. That gift came from God for a reason. Use it to serve someone this week: fix something, teach something, or help someone.
holdOn: My gifts are from God, and I use them to serve others.
prayer: God, thank you for the gifts you have given me. Show me how to use them to serve others. Make me a good manager of your grace, not someone who wastes his gifts. Amen.
teaser: Peter said you have been given something. Then he told you what to do with it.

title: He Cares for You
verse: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
meaning: Peter tells believers to cast all their anxieties on God, because he cares for them. The word cast means to throw something heavy off yourself. God is strong enough to catch it.
heart: Many men carry worry like a backpack full of rocks. God says throw it on me. Name your biggest worry today. Pray it out loud, and picture yourself throwing it into his hands.
holdOn: I throw my worries on God, because he cares for me.
prayer: God, I am carrying worries that are too heavy for me. I throw them on you now. Thank you that you care for me. Help me stop picking them back up again. Amen.
teaser: Peter gave an instruction about worry that sounds like a physical action.

title: Everything You Need
verse: seeing that his divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue,
meaning: Peter says God's divine power has given believers everything they need for life and godliness. It comes through knowing Jesus, who called them by his own glory and goodness. Nothing essential is missing.
heart: You may feel like you lack what it takes to live a godly life. Peter says you already have what you need in Jesus. Stop waiting for more. Use what he has already given you today.
holdOn: In Jesus, I already have everything I need for a godly life.
prayer: God, thank you that your power has given me everything I need for life and godliness. Help me know Jesus better, and live from what you have already given me. Amen.
teaser: Peter made a big claim about what you already have. It is good news.

title: Add to Your Faith
verse: Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge;
meaning: Peter tells believers to make every effort to add to their faith. Start with goodness, then knowledge, and he goes on to list self-control, endurance and love. Faith is the base, but it should keep growing.
heart: Faith is not the finish line. It is the foundation. Peter lists qualities to build on it. Pick one, maybe self-control, and make an effort to grow in it this week. Write down one step.
holdOn: I build on my faith with goodness, knowledge and self-control.
prayer: God, I do not want my faith to stay small. Help me add goodness, knowledge and self-control to it. Give me the effort and the grace to keep building my life on you. Amen.
teaser: Peter said faith is not the finish line. He listed what to build on top of it.

title: Keep Growing
verse: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.
meaning: Peter ends his last letter with one instruction: grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Then he gives him glory now and forever. Growth never stops for a believer.
heart: Some men treat faith like a finished course. Peter says keep growing in grace and in knowing Jesus, all your life. Pick one way to keep learning: a book, a podcast, a mentor or a Bible plan.
holdOn: I want to keep growing in grace and in knowing Jesus all my life.
prayer: Jesus, I want to keep growing in your grace and in knowing you. Keep me from coasting. Give me hunger to learn more about you, and let my life give you glory. Amen.
